title: I'll do your homework for you...
author: drsbm
body: That line in episode 9. I LOST IT. Maybe it has been a rough few weeks for me, so I was already primed for something to take me over the edge. With my limited schedule as a full-time working mom, this story was a random gift from the universe and once I entered the world, I couldn't stop until I was done, even sacrificing my rest was a small price to pay to witness their incredible journeys. I laughed. I cried. I laughed. I cried. It was amazing. It was exhilarating. The story explored multiple themes: life and death; safety and security; attachment and belongingness; restriction and liberation; losses and abandonment. These profound themes were interwoven into a story line that was light and heavy at the same time. Yes, I laughed through my tears so be ready to experience the full range of emotions. We can be so caught up in our mundane routines that sometimes we need a refresher to shock us back into reality, to put us back on track on this continuum of space and time, and that at the core of our existence is the need to just remember that we matter, no matter how big or small. Every now and then, a story comes along that reminds us to give our eyes, "a break from the sun." This was my break. And, I am ever so grateful... P. S. I viewed the ending of the story as a renewed beginning, that life and death is a full circle and that we need to strive to be at peace with every choice/path we take.

title: Loveable characters that you just can't hate, including the villians
author: robertayers-1967
body: I really enjoyed this show. The characters and their motivations were understandable, and you couldn't really dislike any of them, even the vile villain, because they kept your interest. Woo Do Hwan has impressed me in everything I've seen him in so far, but every single character, even the side characters, were just so lovable.The plot is pretty good too. Woo Do Hwan plays the main character who is given some devastating news. After getting this information, he soon sees his ex girlfriend who also has some of her own bad news she's dealing with. He decides to kidnap her from her wedding and go on an odyssey to find his real father who might know something about his sickness. Of course the girls husband to be isn't having it and quickly finds the courage to go after her and get her back. So many other things happen in this 10 episode series that it would take too many words to talk about it all. Along the way, all the characters involved, including minor characters, learn something about themselves.I really loved all these characters, and though at times some of the crying in this show might've went a little too far, and some of the things characters pulled off seemed a little impossible without some type of repercussions, I couldn't help but be glad they were not caught.The two leads had great chemistry, but I would have to say all the characters in Mr Plankton were great. They all seemed to enjoy making this series. Shout out to the dark brooding figure with the sunglasses as well who was a bodyguard working for the girl's husband to be's mother.

title: Strong Tarantino's Vibes
author: ilkaeva
body:
Drawing a parallel between Mr. Plankton and Quentin Tarantino's movies may seem unconventional at first given the distinct genres and styles-K-dramatic poignancy versus Tarantino's kinetic, genre-bending approach. However, both works explore complex characters and human connections amidst dark, often tragic circumstances, while employing distinctive storytelling elements.Narrative Complexity and Emotional Depth:
Like many of Tarantino's films, Mr. Plankton thrives on character backstories and layers of emotion intertwined with present events. While Mr. Plankton focuses on Hae-jo's journey to make peace with his past before facing death, Tarantino characters often confront their own pasts through violent, redemptive, or transformative arcs (Kill Bill's revenge quest being one example). In both cases, the emotional stakes drive the character motivations and plot.Character-Driven Plot with a Focus on Redemption and Reconciliation:
Tarantino's characters, from the Bride in Kill Bill to Django in Django Unchained, often seek redemption or personal justice. Similarly, Mr. Plankton centers on Hae-jo's quest to reconcile with his origins and lost love before his life ends. Though Tarantino's stories tend to be more revenge-fueled, both share an undercurrent of resolution-seeking amidst chaos, tragedy, and broken lives.Use of Dark Humor and Tragic Undertones:
While Tarantino often leverages dark humor to cut through intense moments, Mr. Plankton leans into bittersweet melancholy but occasionally finds surreal levity or humanity amid its bleakness. Both styles add a nuanced texture, making their tales compelling and emotionally layered.Structuring Themes Through Symbolic Journeys:
In many Tarantino films, characters embark on journeys-literal or figurative-that represent more than their immediate quests. Mr. Plankton similarly crafts Hae-jo's road trip as a symbolic trek to resolve identity crises and familial dysfunction. While the settings and tone are worlds apart, the idea of using travel as a means to self-realization and closure is a shared narrative device.Focus on Relationships in a Chaotic World:
Tarantino often pits human connections against a chaotic backdrop of violence, betrayal, and morally gray dilemmas. Mr. Plankton places Hae-jo's relationships in the context of existential crises, strained family bonds, and lost love. The chaotic worlds may differ-criminal underworlds versus inner emotional turmoil-but the portrayal of relationships tested by extreme circumstances forms a strong parallel.While Mr. Plankton adheres more to romantic tragedy and personal drama and Tarantino emphasizes explosive genre storytelling, both show how storytelling, complex characters, and challenging thematic content can elevate their respective narrative worlds. In a way, each explores what happens when people try to reclaim meaning amid inevitable endgames.

title: After a Long Time, a K-Drama Worth Every Tear
author: olxlife
body: Netflix's Mrs. Plankton took me by surprise. Expecting a typical K-drama, I found instead a deeply moving series filled with complex emotions and relationships. From the mother-son bond to friendships and sibling ties, it explores themes of love, loyalty, and healing in a way that feels authentic. The visuals add depth to each scene, and the last three episodes were tear-jerkers that I couldn't look away from. Balancing comedy, a hint of adventure, and raw emotion, it's been a long time since I binge-watched something this powerful in one day. It's been a long time since a K-drama has moved me like this, and Mrs. Plankton managed to do so with grace and authenticity. For anyone looking for a show that offers depth, emotion, and an unforgettable experience, Mrs. Plankton is a must-watch. It's a beautiful reminder of the power of storytelling and how, sometimes, even the most unexpected shows can leave a profound impact.

title: How Can You Not Love This Drama?
author: PalmBeachG
body: How can you not love a drama that uses California Dreaming by the Mama and the Papas as one of their theme songs? The theme of this drama to me was reminiscent of the Stockholm Syndrome from the 70s (Patty Hearst Case) -Rich heir gets kidnapped who falls in love with her kidnapper, all the while the family is desperately searching for her (but molded into a different script). The script here is that the heir is getting married and it is his bride to be that gets kidnapped. You have to love the ML, the kidnapper who does it just for fun because he is dying anyway. They drift and goes on a quest with her to find his real dad before he dies. He has a smile that is just contagious. It ends up in real love. The ending of this drama is the most loving and touching I have ever seen and the saddest too.

title: Mr. Plankton ~ the best one!
author: muna-38484
body: Mr. Plankton(my dear Haejo)- I just wanted to tell you that you were never alone. You were loved by many people. You had a cool best friend like Kkari, a lover like jolly Jae-mi, a jackpot bonus like Bongsuk and a brother from another mother like happy Heung. So, we are not going to cry anymore. We'll cherish you and all those memories we had together. You were amazing Do-hwan.I've watched numerous sad movies/series but this was the saddest & also the warmest. Perfect title of the story "Mr. Plankton".You must watch it. I loved all of those characters. They were all so good in their job; they made me laugh and cry my heart out.Haejo, "What did I do to deserve this? Being born by accident, left to wander the streets and suddenly die as if struck by lightning"!When you said I want to live...I cried with you throughout the drama. You were trying to comfort Jaemi while hurting too. You tried to be the strongest and be the protector despite getting vulnerable by your own condition. You deserved all the love. Woo do Hwan, you are extremely talented and gifted.My dear Jaemi, you cried so much that I wanted to give you a big hug.Heung, you were the most selfless and if I could find a man like you in real, I'll never let him go.To the writer of Mr. Plankton, you are so so talented. You once said that in this world, memories left behind by those who live and those who have lived are intertwined, so there is no such thing as a final ending. Life is so uncertain and unfair. It's not happy ending everytime in life, it ended that way because it was meant to be.Thank you for giving this lovely piece of art, it is one of my favourite.To the makers, we really want to see them doing another project together, they were so good together.

title: Why people like it so much
author: anetemurmane
body: It's not bad, but it's not good either. The overall storyline initially drew me in, but each episode itself seemed very bland and mostly annoying. When you change the speed of the show to faster, is never a good sign. The last 20 min of the show were really enjoyable.I understand tastes might differ based on person, but it feels like everyone who is overhyped have not seen truly great dramas where the each episodes issue is not only miscommunication or just no proper communication. Some miscommunication is understandable here and there, but it genuinely felt like an overkill and lazy writing. Will never watch it again and forget about its existence once the hype is over.

title: Blue sky
author: robertcairnduff-56748
body: Sometimes Kdramedies are nice but too wordy. They set out to fill 16 episodes (why?} and one loses interest in the characters, bored with the dialogue, and the plot(s) become confused. Sometimes Korea produces gems... usually light, but with so many pleasing aspects they sparkle.Mr Plankton (you'll be told why it's called that) is one of those gems. Perhaps because it has just ten episodes, but that's enough to become invested in the characters, be amused by the antics and enjoy the plot development.Yes, more than a few tears will be shed, but really... this is a mature, light, and entertaining show with very good acting and well-crafted throughout.You might be sad at the end, but you'll feel better having joined them on their journeys.Please watch it.

title: Wish the dubbing was better
author: ahnsk
body: Wish the dubbing pronunciation for the kdramas were better. The translated english nicknames ruins the whole experience of watching the show. I had to turn on en subtitle to understand 'lackey kkari' from the very beginning of episode 1. If you don't understand korean its hard to understand the meaning behind it.Either fully localize the name into english equivalent or stick to the korean nickname and try pronounce it better.This then makes the dialogues feel unnatural and forced. Some of the lines don't fit the characters' personalities and seem overly formal or awkward, ruining the flow of 'watch'. Stopped at episode 1, 9mins 51 into the show. Ugh.

title: Many of us are Plankton in our lives
author: elvirak-39035
body: Let's start with the fact that this is the best drama I've ever watched (I've watched almost all existing dramas). For the first time, I cried and laughed out loud at the same time. I experienced the whole range of emotions while watching. This drama shows all the facets of parenthood, so you understand that there is no ideal formula for relationships between children and parents. You can grow up in an orphanage, but be full of love. Or you can grow up with biological parents and feel like plankton. I understood absolutely every character in the series. Hae Jo turned my heart out - I felt sorry for him, I felt sorry for him, and I was angry at him. All the actors did a brilliant job with their roles, but Woo Do-hwan is an underrated diamond of Korean cinema. He plays so realistically and shows all the emotions that one look is enough. Woo Do-hwan is not afraid to be on camera with snot or ugly. I hope that we will see him on screen more often. And yes, 10 episodes were not enough for me, I would have liked to have revealed some questions regarding their relationship. Special thanks for the director's work. I felt like I was next to the characters. Thank you very much for such a realistic and beautiful ending. Although I cried non-stop through the last two episodes, it was worth it. Thanks to everyone involved in the drama.

title: 2 shining stars light up the screen
author: phd_travel
body: It's been a while since we had A list stars in a rom com. So it's wonderful to have the 2 pretty Parks back from thriller genre to this type of series. And these 2 are in their element here. Sparkling chemistry that is always pleasant never painful. Romantic comedy with lots of comedy.The story starts off involving with both their respective career crises. She with a nasty boss and he with a malpractice suit. Immediately they get our sympathies. Funny flashbacks of them as students. And luckily they are still young enough to play themselves as teens. Their also is her funny family that is always in their business headed by Jang Hye Jin of CLOY and Parasite. The humour is spontaneous and laugh out loud funny. And it is touching the way they help each other.One faults is they seem to encourage drinking alcohol to feel better. Quite wrong for people on meds for psychiatric problems. Hope it wasn't product placement by the alcohol industry.The issues with his friends are quite realistic.Recently K rom coms have lacked either a really funny story or uniformly top notch casting. This is a welcome return back to the funny and well cast shows of the past. Good thing no silly love triangles and other done to death cliches. Its mostly enjoyable. The last few episodes ran out of steam. Should have ended earlier.

title: At least 5 episodes too long.
author: mel-43715
body: Started off ok - a bit cliché-ridden but good performances by main cast and side players. Credibility straining as time went in and it had really fun out of plot by episode 8.Many of the flashbacks served no purpose and the supporting actors live story was actually more interesting than that if the main characters.Notable tropes include: several wrist grabs, at least two accidental swoons, several wake-ups in the wrong place after drinking, a premature death of a parent, a hospital stay with an unidentifiable IV drip and numerous occasions of going out to eat after the characters have just eatenNice directing and camera work certainly helped move this along but, if you're after a good drama with a well-written plot then look elsewhere.

title: Review on Dr. Slump
author: euginebarros
body: This series is outstanding, it tackles about mental health. There's a lot of learnings that you can get from the series. It's very relatable to those who are doing everything just to build their career, and those who are experiencing burn out and depression. It's very timely and relevant. The actors are very good in portraying their characters. The chemistry is there. It also talks about family. The first two episodes are very interesting, I was crying and laughing at the same time. The characters of the sorry really resonates on my experiences. I am super excited and I can't wait to watch the upcoming episodes. Kudos to the production team and the writer of this piece.

title: Dr Slump, a rom/com with a message!
author: cherrymaygarma
body: Each and everyone needs a healthy mind and body, so we will be able to face life's adversities. It affects all of us, rich or poor, young or old etc. But it is how we face our trials and tribulations that is most important. Recognizing, accepting and doing something right. Asking professional help, having good support from family and friends. We cannot just stand alone. Life's problems will always be there and every time we solve one life gets better. Beautifully and very well performed and portrayed by the all actors. To the director, writer and all the staff, a job well done! Best wishes! Congratulations!!! It is a very heartwarming and educational Korean TV series." To the whole world, let us not forget MENTAL HEALTH"

title: LOVE IT!!!!!!
author: bdgzszz
body: Didn't expect that this series would be so good!!!! It tackles mental health, depression, which are a sensitive topic to some especially here in our country. Getting checked by a psychiatrist doesn't mean that you are crazy.Park ShinHye and Park Hyung Sik's chemistry is unexpected. But I feel giddy every time they have their "moment". You can feel their emotions and feelings through their gaze and they don't need to speak to tell what they are feeling. They are both really good artists.Recommending this series to everyone! My husband who is not so with kdramas liked it also! We watched 8 episodes in 1 sitting! Hehe. We were so hooked!

title: RomCom at its Best!
author: hyungsikangels
body: Depression and Burnout is tackled in a serious yet healing way. Everything about it has been great - the script, the acting, the OSTs, the cinematography. The chemistry between Shinye and Hyungsik is just amazing as well as the chemistry of Shinye with her mom, brother and her bestfriend I can't wait how their story of recovering from the slump and their love story unfolds. My favorite is Episode 3 - I had to watch it 3 times. The love story of the second leads and how they will support the main leads is also something to look forward too - so far their interaction has been cute and gives off the Crash Course in Romance vibe.All the best to Dr Slump cast and teams especially to our dearest Hyungsik. Fighting! 💪

title: Sadly heading into a slump
author: Dillydaydream
body:
I really enjoyed this up until episode 8. Two people who are qualified and were practicing doctors must surely be in their mid to late
twenties and mature. In episode 8 they are like lovesick young teenagers. I'm not suggesting they should fall into bed because this is not
Kdramas way but it could be a more realistic age appropriate relationship.On the plus side the two leads are very good. I have liked PSH since Heirs and it's great to see her back in a drama since marrying and having her
baby. Park Hyung-Sik is good in this part and they do have nice chemistry. I'll watch it to the end with the hope that it becomes good again!

title: Super Amazing kdrama on 2024
author: thamelamanda
body: I am addicted to this kdrama!!!! I just love it sooo sooo much!! The chemistry between park hyunk sik and park shin hye is amazing. They portrait emotions really well. And the humor in this drama is in top level. Everyone should watch this kdrama. Its superb for gettting weekend hype. I think this drama need more recognition. I just cant wait for next epis. title: An Implausibly Slow Romance
author: kgenereux-75-533576
body: I had 9 stars worth of interest in Dr. Slump until this weekend, when episodes 7 & 8 were aired by Netflix USA. Ouch. The Romance vector is implausibly slow in that the female lead had already confessed to "quasi-romantically liking" "Dr. Rooftop" (they've held hands on a windswept beach and had a multitude of emotional confessions) yet in episode 8 she is suddenly bizarrely retro-ambivalent. Seriously, she's pushing 30, yet she seems to equate handholding to sexual intimacy. (Like she's spent the last 20 years ain a convent.) Also whenever any of the female actors get drunk, which happens way too often in eps. 7 and 8, they often become outrageously physically abusive to male characters. I find those drunken party scenes downright strange, and the level of acting in them falls between unconvincing and atrocious.

title: i love this drama♥
author: hayaalgeva
body: I really liked the drama, let's start with the perfect casting of the cast, it seems that Park Hyung Shik just played his real life (you can see in fan meetings and interviews that this is his mindset) seriousness and maturity alongside childishness (they say that in every mature person, there is also a little child). The drama deals with healing and recovery, competition for achievements and success alongside failure and disappointment. Friendship, and support. Insights that you get after crises (financial and mental), satisfaction in the face of fulfillment... a race for achievements in life where along the way you forget to enjoy the small things (sunset, going for a walk, enjoying nature from the blossoms and even eating ice cream) and the mental price that you pay because of the race for life. It is true that there are some childish scenes (not compatible with the model of a doctor) but they fit so well against the very sensitive subject of mental exhaustion and depression. I totally recommend watching the drama and examining it in depth and not superficially.

title: Shin Hye eye candy... rest is vanilla
author: patricia-knightley
body: Enjoyable yes... swoon worthy yes... original, clever and limited cringe screenplay... no... some segments are just too cheesy... even for KDrama standards... they just ran out of screenplay ideas on this one.But Shin Hye has never looked lovelier and it's hard not to stare at her eyes and that gorgeous hair.I buy into the chemistry as well as the topic of PTSD and depression and it's covered sincerely and authentically for the most part.Other areas of the story such as getting together, ripped apart, getting together, ripped apart again can either be enjoyed or found to be very annoying so the ride YMMV.

title: Cute simple boring
author: Infycd_
body: Simple cute story but really too boring after few episodes. They could have ended in 10 episodes. Most of kdramas had this problem. Why they always think 16 episode is mandatory???I started this drama bcz of both leads. They both were amazing in other dramas but in this perticular drama they are really not much impressive. title: AMAZING KDRAMA
author: ajkskull
body: I personally don't understand about people who called this drama boring, dragging, or how this should be less episodes. It is called doctor Slump which means it is about people who had been in their lowest point in their life that happens to be doctors, rather than medical drama (like dr romantic or such). I'm really get about the side arc (Jeongwoo malpractice arc or Min Kyungmin arc) but all that side arc only shows that regardless of their misery, it really pain for the main characters and really need time to heal themselves. I appreciate that the writers can maintain the theme of health consistently because it is really ews.

title: Strong points
author: newkrejados
body: ... But not too many. It seems this show wants to do everything. Don't get me wrong, lots of KDramas manage to pull that off. Just not this one.The mental health angle is great, but underdone. The revenge twist is decent, but not fleshed out. The characters have practically no backstory, even the two leads. The romance is tepid, at best.The PHS - PSH pairing just doesn't work. I've seen PSH in other shows; she always gives the same, narrow-range, wooden performance. There's only so much PHS can do to coax anything out of his co-lead; she just doesn't seem responsive.On the other hand, it seems PHS has come into his own. This probably wasn't the best vehicle for him to prove that. Or maybe its two-dimensional backdrop gave him the needed room to shine. Whatever the reason, there's no doubting his emotional range or physical comedy skills.

title: Fun, but why is everyone drunk all the time
author: xykatexy
body: I am now on the twelfth episode. The series is fun, but honestly very overrated because the main cast is super popular. Otherwise, I don't think there is much that makes this series special. The main couple is alright, I don't think they have that much chemistry. However, I really liked the way they comfort eachother and are helping one another with mental health.Both characters suffer from mental health disorders, and I find the portrayal of mental health issues to be somewhat a trend in nowadays' kdramas. I especially like that this one takes on the topic of overachieving and forgetting to live in the character of Haneul (even if the way they present this is over the top- the girl eating instant coffee powder to not have to use the restroom is ridiculous).The main couple is fun, and so is the side couple. It's an excellent comfort series, but there is not much to write home about.One thing though: heavy drinking is shown in every episode. Every single one. Not that I'm against drinking, but the fact that every single character has gotten blackout drunk at least once is kind of concerning. Not sure if this represents Korean society or what, but it's a bit much.

title: best ever healing drama
author: dheerajdhooper
body: After so long i really laughed while watching a series. Best ever healing drama. There is a lots of things you can get from this series. After falling into a slump how two people comforts each other. Two nemesis became friends then lovers. No boring episodes. Each characters got equal time space. It also talks about family, friends. I laughed and cried also while watching this. Kudos to the writers, actors specially Park hyung sik whose acting was mind blowing and also Park shin hye who perfectly slayed in this character. OF COURSE PARK PARK COUPLE CHEMISTRY. Lastly "We learned to be in pain for a moment and to cherish memories for awhile. In the end, we were able to escape our slumps."- Yeo Jeong Woo.

title: Good binge watch
author: Rose007lily
body: First of all, the male lead is absolutely adorable and handsome ( giving vibes like Min Min of strong girl bong so.... ). He is having emotional side too, which is according to the storyline.The female lead is good, she played the character well. But her off screen energy is addictive ( I saw some reel on Instagram and she looks so excited off screen), her character is actually depressed, so it makes sense that she acts a little low. This drama marked her best kiss scene, we all know this haha.I feel like both leads nailed the role of high schoolers, it was a burst of cheerfulness and comedy.The second lead couple is super adorable too, I actually found their story quite interesting in the last few episodes.The younger brother of female lead is funny and innocent. Whole cast did a great job.The cinematography is perfect. Bgm is great. The shifts between past and present are flawlessly executed. Overall, it's a great drama which will give you rom com & melodrama vibes.

title: Good Enough
author: PennyReviews
body: Korean Drama '' Doctor Slump '' is a slice of life melodrama with some medical drama hints.The drama has a healing story, with the romance being well paced and starting from academic rivals, to friends, to lovers, which shifted the story from the love story to the difficulties the characters had to face and overcome. Hence, the slow pace helped the mood of the drama a lot.Unfortunately, the second half of the drama felt more like a filler. There were only a few things left to be resolved and a few new things to be added to the story. At this point, the side couple was the one who kept things interesting and offered a lot of adorable moments.Finally, the performances were all enjoyable by everyone in the cast.So, overall, six out of ten.

title: For more dramas like this!
author: duolibi
body: I simply loved this drama. It was one of the dramas in which I felt moved and put myself in the characters' shoes. I also loved the part where they portray Bournout. I also found the part about exhaustion on the part of the students to be very important, always wanting to be the best to please their parents. This drama teaches us a good life lesson, in addition to laughing a lot in most episodes, it also brings lightness, sensitivity and romanticism. I would love for there to be a second one after the first season, I just loved this drama so much, I wanted more dramas like this! This drama is really worth watching, it's exciting, romantic, cute and funny, Netflix got a lot right in this drama.

title: Superb
author: jdiep-80040
body: Amazing, amazing KD. I watch a lot of KD, and the FL and ML are two of the best. Their acting are superb, and on point portraying so many mixed emotion. I can't wait until the next episode. Just finished watching episode four. Each episode revealed bits into the actor's past, and present, piecing together a cohesive story that are both endearing and funny. The story line is relevant battling mental health, and ever so inspiring. The drama showcased how one can never plan or anticipate life events. I rarely write reviews, despite watching so many dramas. However, this drama deserve great reviews, and I want to support the actors, and their future work prompting me to write this review.

title: Amazing cast and chemistry
author: stephyttt
body: I really enjoyed this drama. Both main leads portrayed their characters so well and I fell in love with their journey! I think it will particularly resonate with people that have experienced depression or going thru a tough time in their life. It provided a good mix of an interesting storyline with funny and witty moments! Loved watching their love story and how they communicated their feelings to each other so well. It was also great to see different family dynamics as that is how it is in real life sometimes. This drama was so good it deserves to be highly praised! 10/10 would recommend watching it!

title: So Disappointing
author: geewhiz46
body: I like Hyunsik - I was looking forward to seeing him as the ML in this series - he has proved he can act in other series that I have seen him in. So I guess it depends on the content and the co-star - whether he displays the same degree of ability. There is nothing you can do if the writing is bad and the co-star is unresponsive.The situation - I can't call it a story - is such that two doctors in different fields who were high school rivals find themselves in bad situations as adults. Naturally they end up living in the same building and eventually becoming friends after far too much anguished self analysis and chopping and changing for no reason.Then the contrived problems begin and my interest begins to end.I don't know what is the matter with the FL - she looks drawn and ill and has no natural ebullience at all - whilst the ML is the complete opposite - although they are roughly the same age she looks much older than him. The high school scenes were not convincing regarding her - Hyunsik got away with looking eighteen - she didn't.There is far too much talking and not enough action in this series - the family were featured too strongly - viewers want to see the lovers together - they want to see them kiss - they want them to see them be happy - writers ignore your audience at your peril - your job is to please them - not yourselves.

title: Great story, amazing acting
author: mikaelarosal
body: Park Shin-hye & Park Hyung-sik delivered an amazing acting in drama & comedy. Their chemistry is really good, built from good friendship. The story is great with a balance of drama & romantic comedy. People who are commenting about how could these doctors act like teenagers in love or the mother acting like lunatic are lacking in IQ. It's called comedy & in comedy everything is exaggerated. Watch other comedies whether Asian or not, the characters whether they're cops, boss, parents will have exaggeration of acting & words. Shin-hye & Hyung-sik nailed their characters in drama & comedy parts. If you keep an open mind, it's actually a really great drama/romantic comedy show. It depicted depression & ptsd well according to the characters experience. Depression & ptsd signs/symptoms varies & it's not one fits all. So some people can relate & some not. I highly recommend Dr. Slump, you will laugh so hard & cry your heart out. It's a story of life's happiness & stuggle, in the midst of it they found each other & fell in love.

title: THE two rivals in school met in their worst phase of life..and overcome their fears together...DOCTTHE The two rivals in school met in their worst phase of life..
author: priyankadeka-63257
body: It will be hard to say goodbye to these two.. 10 years ago they were together in a drama where Park Shin Hye was the main lead and Park hyung Shik was a supporting actor. I never imagined them as a lead couple, which turned out to be a total surprise for me. The drama is not only about love but a journey of two depressed people finding solace in each other's company. It's hard to heal yourself when you are depressed..when you are treated wrongly at your workplace, when people misuse your kindness, blame you for a crime which you never even committed. Everything you have earned that disappears in a blink of an eye- those moments I lived together with these two characters. I laughed and cried , at some point I found myself in them and most importantly in the process of healing , you realize " you can heal fully when your partner can heal too"- if you are the medicine prescribed to him for his treatment, then why not do so? And it's only worth doing when the other person also feels the same....

title: Excellent!
author: elinacharisi
body: One of the best, if not the best k drama I have seen. The acting is really good! 2 successful doctors reach rock bottom and they still find a way to overpass the difficulties they face by just connecting with each other and bringing to surface their inner child, since they missed so much in life due to the pressure to becoming doctors. title: Simple, yet surprisingly intricate, definitely worth the watch!
author: minjennie-21238
body: I did thoroughly enjoy this drama, however, I believe it could've easily been 10-12 episodes long and still felt complete.I watched this because of Park Hyungsik, who as always did a tremendous job making the role his own. This was actually my first encounter with Park Shinhye and although I enjoyed watching her character, I don't really have a strong opinion of her.If you're looking for a light-hearted yet compelling time, this is perfect for you. It's a sweet and fun watch, although it gets lethargic towards the end.I do have to say, since I had been waiting for this drama to come out for a long time because of PHS, I enjoy watching him in more serious roles so much more. I'm still very much not over happiness and his look and acting in it and I long for another serious role and look from him. I remember how some ppl had things to say regarding his weight in happiness *rolls eyes* and I'm mildly upset that he lost so much weight for this role...

title: Another K-drama where nothing happens
author: martypecciola
body: This show could have lasted 5 episodes instead of the usual 16. First episodes are ok, we gradually learn about each character, there are a few interesting stories, promising plot... and then nothing! Just a succession of scenes where they eat and say "hhhmmm it's delicious", they drink when they're sad or happy, adults acting like teenagers and telling each other "you're beautiful" and get embarrassed for nothing. And basically the same development as always.The cast was good, cinematography too, but unfortunately the writing was really poor. I enjoyed watching Park Hyung-sik in Soundtrack #1 which was soooo different from all the usual k-dramas and so natural and well written.

title: It's funny, heartwarming and relatable. Best Healing Drama
author: Scaletrose
body: Park Hyung Sik and Park Shin Hye had the best chemistry. They were both brilliant in the show. They matched each other so well in terms of their acting abilities and comedic timings. They brought me to tears but also gave me so much healing and laughters at the same time. I love all the actors in the show but Park Hyung Sik stood out the most for me. He made me cry, laugh and swoon effortlessly throughout the show. He breathed life into his character, Jeong Woo with his unique, expressive style of acting. I truly hope he gets an award for his stellar performance.Story wise, Dr Slump has a lot of heart. It's funny, heartwarming and relatable. It tells the struggles of our modern daily grind and how we could overcome our slumps through a simple yet beautiful slice of life story. Slow down, take a break, love yourself, reset your priorities and find strength through your loved ones - that was exactly the process I went through when I suffered from trauma and burnout years ago. This drama touches on sensitive topics in a light-hearted way and it's a breath of fresh air. There are no major twists but lots of meaningful conversations. I love the messages that the show is trying to convey.Having overcame my own slump, topics of mental health have always been an interest to me, yet I had tried watching a few mental health related dramas but couldn't continue as it sometimes got too dark and scary that it actually triggered my own anxiety. Hence, the plentiful comedy in Dr Slump was very much appreciated. I earnestly looked forward to the show every weekend. It was like a drug prescribed to me.

title: Finally a love story on two, not one intelligent people
author: irisandleisure
body: It's been a long time since I chance upon a love story on two highly independent intelligent person, two! Usually, one is weak or needy, and the other is hero. Here, both are heros.They are used to fighting battles alone in the society despite the holes in their hearts. But together, their holes mends. They did not become needy and leech on the other which is so common in drama.Despite feeling vulnerable to love and issues loving the other in episode 8, both responded sensibly and constructively given their inner battles. I find that more loving than all the impulsive and dramatic acts in most drama. Finally, a sensible couple.However, I speed through all other characters' scenes and sub plot, it was dull and a drag for me.

title: We can't have a break so enjoy someone else having it
author: ajwahmk
body:
Tbh this one follows a similar stories of many other kdramas.... Like welcome to samdal ri, Summer Strike, Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha, When the Weather Is Fine, Once Upon a Small Town
And many more. They all follow the same story of failure finding your roots and then rising back in a better state...

title: Insufferably corny
author: nclaire-37809
body: Started off well but degenerated from ep 8. Watch it if you like cutesy highschool-esque romance with a weak story line and below average chemistry. The two lead actors are supposedly doctors but the characters especially the FL acts like a teenage girl being coy and helpless and just generally insufferable. Don't know why kdrama writers turn every FL lead into some damsel in distress without a thought in her head, in some cases it works but here the FL lead is supposedly a doctor so that kind of forced naivete is just cringe and ill suited for the story line. In any case I don't think it's the actors fault, just really badly written drama overall.

title: Doctor Slump is Comical and Cute
author: PalmBeachG
body:
Doctor Slump is a comical and cute drama overall and the ML that was cast, Park Hyung-sik as Doctor Slump, makes the whole show. He has a way to make you smile and laugh at the same time as being handsome and romantic. Also he has a special tone in his voice that is unique that is nice and fun to listen to. I had to take off 2 stars however for the FL. Despite her broad bio that I read, I don't think she brought any chemistry to the show. Too bad as I think it could have been better. She was a little too **tchy and also acting the role as if she had a stick up her you know what - no one would ever like someone like that so the FL could have been cast better IMO. No special personality brought there. The side love story - the friends of the ML and FL is cute as well. Episode 14 finally is the turning point with the 3691 coded message that brings about the love for both, career success and money back in DR Slump's pocket, and resolving psychological problems. We have to attribute all of these miraculous things being accomplished in one episode to the code given 3691.#DoctorSlump
#ParkHyungsik
#DRSlump.

title: Great start of year with Park lovers
author: twilightsonam
body: Wow I was really waiting for this series from the day I Heard about Park Hyun Sik and Park Shin Hye it was so beautiful from the starting till end really awesome this series made my this years great list to me. What made it really beautiful was beacuse to see them as lovers and her mom, brother and uncle her supportive friend and Park Hyun Sik's doctor friend who really supports him this things make my heart so warm her family were so awesome, fun and really made family scene beautiful I really loved the family scene cuz they were so funny, and heartwarming and I really loved Park Hyun Sik and Park Shin Hye' moment together a lot and I really loved the way both of their doctor friends falling for eachother and supporting the Park lovers and the four of their scene were so beautiful too and above all my favourite was seeing Park Hyun Sik with Park Shin Hye and her family spending time together.

title: COULD BE BETTER
author: asmrsatisfyingslimebest
body:
The story and the script was good but they could have made it better. The first half was really good i enjoyed it but the second half was okay. They could have made it till 10 or 12 episodes but they made it till 16 episode so they kind of lagged. I really enjoyed their school days it was funny and how they started competing each other was also really good. It was like eniemies to lovers. The overall story was good if they wouldn't have lagged i would give it 9.4/10.The story/summary of doctor slump
Yeo Jeong-Woo (Park Hyung-Sik) always placed first in academics and he studied at the top medical school in the country. Yeo Jeong-Woo is now a popular plastic surgeon. His life goes smoothly, but, due to a mysterious medical accident, his life is pushed to the edge. At this time, he meets Nam Ha-Neul (Park Shin-Hye). She was a rival in his past and he meets her at the lowest point in his life.Nam Ha-Neul works as an anesthesiologist. When she was growing up, people called her a genius due to her extreme intelligence. She studied hard and became a doctor. Her life consists of only work and studying. She doesn't have any time to experience fun. One day, Nam Ha-Neul realizes she isn't happy with her life and she wants to make a change. At this time, she meets Yeo Jeong-Woo during one of the worst moments in her life. They comfort each other and a romantic relationship blossoms between them.

title: A very meaningful storytelling
author: caiojcfreitas
body: I'm just ending to watch this k-drama and I really appreciated about how things went on them.The way the scripter led the things so fluent were a good point to stand, watching it all were smoothly like a good time I didn't saw in k-dramas. The love was ok, the chemistry of the leads were also on point and the second couple (Hong Ran e Dae Young) were really great (I think they should developed deeper their relationship, how it started, how it went and how their sons reacted).Depression and post traumatic stress disorder was portrayed in a really humanized way. I could relate to them even though I never experienced both of this sickness.The overcome of depression by Haneul moved me to be happier, so I think you should give a chance to experience something like that too.I read a comment someone saying that it could ended in episode 8, but what make this drama different was really that. They had a plot, they wrapped well and still showed us their sadness and grief and how they overcame. And after that everything were flowers. I also think there are other better dramas who can deliver the real experience of this horrendous Korean system of work and pressure in service, and the way Park Hyung Sik acted as Yeo Jeong Woo was silly and adorable, just like other characters of him, and that's really awesome. Jeong Woo brought lightness to the history, and that's a cool thing to notice.The last thing I would like to emphasize here is one of the last talks between Nam Bada e his mother where she shows him he is not better or worst his noona, just different and lovable. Like every mom should say and be.Anyways, it's not the best drama I've watched, but was a really light one even though treat about mental health. I recommend you dig into it faster as you can. You won't regret."If there's sadness, there will always be happiness as well."

title: Bad writing and directing. Too cringe!
author: ATD67
body: The movies characters is too slow for a rom-com and their romance is so childish like kids in high school when they are both professional adults in their own respective fields. The concept is like other rom-com kdramas. This one has no originality. Need better materials/writing. The actors are great in 'other' dramas, but this one lack in many areas especially in the romance department. (Too childish) Grow up!Park Shin-hye is a great actress but this drama is one of her weakest. Park Hyung-Sik is also a good actor but his character is like a little kid not a mature adult. Not realistic at all. I blame the director and the writers for this 'cringe' script not the actors. Hopefully both actors next projects will overshadow this ridiculous drama?

title: For sure one of my favorites
author: riverlillie
body: This show is truly amazing. I wasn't expecting it to be so deep and also so cute. It actually encouraged me so much and left a lasting impression. I feel happy after watching it, and I am thankful to have seen it. I'm grateful to the writers of the show for addressing the issues that were addressed in the show (I don't want to give any spoilers). This show has definitely become one of my top favorites and will be one of my go-to shows when I am feeling down or in a "slump." I will also add that the chemistry between the main characters was incredible. It felt like I was watching a true story unfold. If you have not seen this show yet, watch it! You won't regret it. It was so cute and so emotional and just wonderful...perfect.

title: Perfect balance (and I don't give 10s!)
author: meemsyd
body: This drama was a breath of fresh air, and a perfect balance of drama and comedy.Mental health issues are at the forefront and tackled sensitively, relatable for many and ultimately hopeful. The story progresses at a steady pace and when tropes are used it's done effectively and often tongue-in-cheek.The lead actors nailed their performances and I particularly enjoyed the well written side characters - the family dynamic was so heartwarming and varied. The stories of all characters were fleshed out well, and it was just a calming cathartic sort of viewing experience, and I personally left this show with the warm fuzzies!

title: Romantic "Good Triumphs Over Evil" Drama
author: cageronimolaw
body: , so I've only seen 4 episodes so far, but this drama is Magic! The lead actors are so great, it's almost like you are experiencing their hardships, pain and happiness through their incomparable acting. Plus, they have great chemistry. But in addition, the mom, uncle, even the brat brother add a sort of family to warm Park Hyung Sik - who's family seems distant (i.e., the caustic comment from his mom when he had to go to the nurse (class fan incident)). Can't wait to see it all.I've seen it all. What a fantastic story of loss, redemption, healing, love and some revenge. As I stated above, the 2 lead actors, Park Shin Hye and Park Hyun Sik were extraordinary.This drama is full of twists, plots within plots, mysteries, villainy, jealousy, love and envy.I think it was best when they were fighting for justice. But again, humans have ordinary moments of eating, talking, dating each other, so those moments were touching, funny, mischievous.As an attorney, I found the South Korean justice system to be very weird if the dramas are accurate. If they are, there needs to be a major overhaul to ensure that justice prevails.The ending is Magic, just what is a perfect end to what is, at its heart, a tale of romance and good triumphing over evil. Do not miss this show.

title: An eight so far
author: doug2go
body: I have enjoyed about 70% of the K - romance series - they all follow the same Pygmalion protocol. - Lovers meet lovers, Lovers don't like each other , Lovers get close because of circumstances, lovers enjoy each other company and finally they bond - Well after episode 3 it seems the Koreans are acceleration this protocal - The two romantic protagonists seems to be progressing to an advanced bonding before episode 6 or 7 - which is unique and refreshing - the romantic lead's are OK - better casing may have made the series more endearing.but I am still finding it compelling - I will report back after episode 10 - hard to imagine where the storyrunner is going with this but he has got me so far.

body: I read a review which said "True to its title". title: A different kind of k drama -- fun, refreshing, romantic, moving
author: jennycampbell-44604
body: The reviewer who complained about the romance subplot is so off it's wild.First of all, this show's actual genre is crime romance. It's listed as a romance. So why would they expect there not to be a romance. And the romance itself is a slow burn and is given way less screen time than the crime and horror aspects.Second, the male lead's character arc is completely tied in with the overall plot arc and with FLs character arc, he's not just there to look pretty or make us swoon, he is very important to every aspect of the story and drives much of the action. He doesn't just pop in to be romantic, he is key to the central plot of the serial killer and is the reason why the FL even has a character arc, cause...Third, the FL is not a judge trying to advance her career, she's a demon trying to complete a mission. She's there for one job and one job only -- to find and kill murderers to send them to hell. The ML is not distracting some story of a judge trying to become a better judge, he's making her interesting by being the key to her humanizing as a demon, which is the entire central point of her character arc. Watching a demon go around coldly killing murderer after murderer with no change would get real boring after a few eps.It seems that reviewer just wanted a completely different story, with different characters and a different plot. Instead of looking at what story this show is trying to actually tell, and if it's doing a good job.Which, it really is. This show has so much going for it and the romance only adds to that. The FL and ML have fantastic chemistry. The writing is very tight and knew where it was going from the start, everything connects well together and develops so organically. Good directing a great editing. All the actors are nailing their roles. It's fun at times, scary at times, moving at times. It's been my favorite drama this year.

title: Tedious Torture Show

body: Worst K-show I've watched in quite some time.A female "judge" from hell does something wrong now she has to go up to the real world, find evil criminals, make them confess, and then kill them so they are sent to hell.Sounds incredibly stupid?Oh, yes, and it is.This judge from hell poses as a human judge and then basically goes around, finds some culprits and then beats the hell out of them until they confess.Then she kills them with a magic dagger to send them to hell.So every episode she finds some unlucky criminal she tortures at length to beat a confession out of them.If you are into torture movies like "Hostel" this might be the show for you.If you were looking for some intelligent and witty entertainment with a clever script you are at the wrong place.Instead of making the judge from hell investigate a crime and then devise some intelligent, non-violent plan to send the culprits to hell - the braindead makers of that show went the easy way.Why come up with a clever script, when the judge from hell can just torture the culprits every episode.It's like Sherlock Holmes finding a culprit and then just beating the hell out of him until they confess, and then kills them.And all the culprits know that they get killed once they confess, but they just stand there and let themselves be tortured.Not one of them tries to run away."Hello there, evil hell judge, since you are torturing me so nicely, of course I will tell you everything you want to hear, so you won't kill me. Wait! What? You are going to kill me anyway?! This must be the most stupid TV show ever we both are in right now! Can I call my agent first, please?"If there is a hell for untalented K-show makers, I hope some judge from hell sends them there.

title: Unnecessary romance line
author: shineynn
body: "The Judge from Hell" stands out for its strong female lead and compelling crime stories, yet falls short due to an unnecessary and forced romance between the two lead characters. The show's brightest aspect should be the female judge as the name shows, who is portrayed as an intelligent, principled, and ambitious woman, unafraid to challenge violent murderers and question the human laws.Unfortunately, this momentum is disrupted by the romantic subplot, which feels both forced and unnecessary. The male lead, intended as a love interest, lacks chemistry with the female lead and often comes across as intrusive. His behavior borders on stalker-like, frequently inserting himself into the female lead's life and professional affairs without adding any meaningful development to the story. The romantic tension feels artificial and distracts from the central legal drama, which is far more compelling.What makes this romantic subplot even more frustrating is how it detracts from the female lead's character development. Instead of focusing on her growth during her main and sub missions, the show repeatedly shifts attention to the awkward and poorly developed romance. This detracts from her professional arc and reduces the impact of her character's journey. The directors seem to have fallen into the trap of thinking that a female protagonist requires a romantic counterpart, even when it doesn't fit the story.The forced romance ultimately undermines the potential of "The Judge from Hell." Had the series focused solely on its strong female lead and the captivating crime stories, it could have been an exceptional drama. Instead, the romance feels like a distraction, pulling attention away from the more interesting aspects of the show and making it difficult for viewers to stay invested in the main plot. While the series has its merits, the decision to force a romance weakens what could have been a more powerful and focused narrative.

title: Good and engaging k-drama
author: writetoanonymous
body: The Judge from Hell offers a fresh and compelling storyline that immediately captures the viewer's attention. The plot is engaging from start to finish, with both the female and male protagonists delivering outstanding performances. Their chemistry and dedication to their roles bring a lot of emotional depth to the story, making the show a captivating watch.While the show keeps you hooked throughout its run, the final episode disappoints. The pacing slows significantly in the conclusion, and the lack of a proper ending leaves much to be desired. The show wraps up abruptly without resolving key plotlines or providing closure for the protagonists, which feels like a missed opportunity for a more fulfilling finale. The unresolved tension between the characters leaves viewers wanting more, and the absence of a clear settlement between the two main leads is frustrating.Moreover, the series doesn't do full justice to the real-life Kang Bit Na, a character who could have been explored much more deeply. Despite this, the overall quality of the show remains solid, with strong performances and a story that holds your attention from beginning to end-except for the unsatisfying final episode.

title: Vengeance is mine sayeth the demon
author: alaningle7
body: After making a mistake in hell a demon possesses the murdered body of a judge and is instructed to send ten souls to hell to atone for her error. As she begins her new life as a judge she comes across a dedicated police officer who has a tragic past and when she begins to send souls to hell he becomes determined to bring her to justice. The judge Kang Bit-na is played superbly by Park Shin-hye and the detective Han Da-on is played by Jae-young Kim whose opinion of her starts to soften. I personally enjoyed the earlier episodes where she was less human and exacting revenge but it is still an entertaining story and worth a watch. Be aware though it is quite violent at times in the depiction of gruesome murders.

title: **A Fresh Take on Fantasy and Justice**
author: prathikshabxa
body: This was my first time watching a law drama intertwined with the fantasy genre. I've enjoyed other law dramas like "Extraordinary Attorney Woo Young Woo," "My Suspicious Partner," "Law Cafe," "The Devil Judge," and "Juvenile Justice."This series marked actress Park Shin Hye's comeback after "Doctor Slump," and I recognized actor Kim Jae Young from "Love in Contract." Surprisingly, the chemistry between the leads was electrifying. Initially, Judge Kang Bit-na was portrayed as a fierce and ruthless woman who wasn't afraid to punish criminals and deliver vigilante justice. However, the story lost some of its momentum when she fell in love with Han Daon. While their romance was somewhat dull, the cast delivered outstanding performances.It was fascinating to see each case unfold, with the criminals facing karmic retribution in a manner similar to how they had killed and tortured their victims. The graphics were impressive, and Kang Bit-na's outfits throughout the series perfectly matched her character. The series successfully delivered on all 14 episodes. However, I felt it would have been nice to see flashbacks of Kang Bit-na's past.Eventually, the plot shifted focus to finding Kylum and defeating Satan, the mastermind behind Serial Killer J. This series, along with dramas like "Love Next Door" and "Jeongnyeon," made my weekends something to look forward to. I loved the thrills it provided and would definitely recommend "The Judge from Hell" K-drama!Thank you for taking the time to read this. I hope you have a great day!

body: This show is one of the best dramas I seen so far, so many twist and turns it will have you wanting more I really hope they make season 2.give it a try you will not be disappointed.the way the made this drama is like no other,they have so much good material for a second season,you will fall in love with the main character,I hope they make a second because I personally can't get enough of this drama,I loved the way they always show the character developed into something more,it shows that they really do care about the fans and always make sure you want to keep coming back for more so hope they continue this show I love it.

title: Every minute is a delight
author: phd_travel
body: This is a superbly entertaining series. Must give a lot of praise to the writer who has created an original feel good cleverly constructed story. Not a wasted scene. Exciting till the end. The perfect blend of fantasy, involving angels and demons (not too much) and reality, the legal system and crime and punishment. Plus there is some laugh out loud comedy. The one liners delivered by Park Shin Hye are priceless. Even the emotional moments involving victims is quite moving and the romance is cleverly woven into the story. The vigilante aspect is so satisfying - giving the criminal a taste of his or her own medicine. I don't usually like procedural crime K dramas but this is different. Each case is interesting and you can't wait to see what happens to the criminal. The use of demons inhabiting humans is more palatable than those nine tailed fox shows for sure.Disney Plus has given us some of the highest quality K dramas and this is no exception. The effects production values and visuals are all superb.Park Shin Hye looks amazing here. Her face has thinned a bit and she is stunningly beautiful. Her figure is great too. So nice she gets to wear lots of pretty clothes too. This is her best role in a while - Dr Slump slumped during the second part and Sisyphus lacked romance. Her acting skills are second to none and she has the perfect expressions for each line of snappy dialogue. Kim Jae Young actually has a lot of chemistry with her. His face is suitable for someone to take on a demon. He acts well too. The supporting cast villains and others are all top notch, even the small roles are thoughtfully cast and recognizable for most Kdrama fans.Favorite show of 2024.

title: Korean Monty Python on Kimchi Ayahuasca
author: yiazmatvsomega
body: This is a show to take lightly. Or as litly as possible. It's not a requirement, but it helps.If you consider yourself as one with a moderate-to-strong "sense of willing disbelief" then you'll be in fine territory.But imagine if Monty Python's Flying Circus was made as a Police Procedural satire, and set in Korea. Now feed the writers and actors that ayahuasca-kimchi brew, set the cameras rolling and print it.The trope stacking is *deep,* far deeper than a little show should be! Everything from the quirky-accurate autistic super-detective captain, to the bromantic rivalry between the sergeant and the cap... And onto the bumbling rookie over to the suck up officer, to the naive tomboy officer that learns something every episode.All things considered, I laughed so hard the edges of my vision started to go white. K-Coms strike again. It happens once every 5 years, but when it's a winner, it's frikken platinum.Hooo, I need a break.
