What you're left with is a series that has flashes of intensity, but having the first half of the series depicting Eiko with super-human capabilities took all the wind out of the intensity or horror elements, but then trying to humanize here in the back-half of the series while slowing the pace way down with lots of needless chatterboxing about things that just weren't that important made the show feel like a slog to get through.At the end of it I was still left with more questions than answers, and the answers we did get just weren't very good ones.The thing is, this is basically an anime set within the universe of Terminator, but if you were expecting a horror-thriller like Terminator 1 or a sci-fi action romp like Terminator 2, or finally a proper future-war setting like Terminator Resistance, well prepare to be disappointed because Terminator Zero is not that series.I only gave it a 5 because the last two episodes were decent enough, and I did like the police station setup, but the execution of how that played out was kind of dumb. And the way everyone was just a meatbag that was easily disposed of if they weren't a main character made the stakes feel pointless and the world feel like cardboard.So yes, stay away if you actually like good Terminator fanfare.

title: "I didn't have high hopes".
author: JamesEdwardAnthonyFoster
body: It's honestly a breath of fresh air to finally see them doing something different with the Terminator franchise. Let's face it we've had more then enough movies like 5 at this point things were getting really stupid although I did enjoy Terminator Dark Fate. The first 5 minutes is done very well in the year 2022 Eiko a resistance soilder is hiding in a metal locker with 4 bullets in her pistol left there she's observing a terminator walking through the bricks and rubble left in the room killing any soilders on the floor still alive. There's some somewhat violent gun scenes here and honestly some great action sequences the animation is gorgeous and looks amazing for a first episode it really just starts of with a bang. No slow pacing or anything like that starting right of with some guns firing and everything after that we go to the year 1997 and things calm down for a little while. The series has an familiar cast to like Rosario Dawson who voices an AI in the Skynet building and Timothy Olyphant who voices the Terminator. I've only seen the first episode but this anime has promise and definitely could be something special.

title: Definitely Surprise Of The year
author: Ttdf122
body: I loved it and the way they explained the time travel aspect being different timelines opened up in time instead of the same timeline over and over, which means terminator has a massive multiverse going now lol, in a never ending war. Fully enjoyed the series, the violence and blood was good the Terminator looked scary and intense like the original one. I hope this will help revive the franchise in some way, love to see Future War movies done properly and get back to the original horror tone. Easily the deepest, most nuanced story in the whole franchise. "Zero" is to Terminator what "Andor" is to Star Wars.

title: The contrast makes the character evolve
author: tillettrenart-800804
body: I haven't been a fan of Manga since I was a child that enjoyed MAZINGER Z, so it took me a while to get used to the rythm, and tone. My 1st positive reaction was smiling with the robotic Cat, which has some tender moments rarely found in Californian productions. In other words, Japanese do know how to make a robotic cat, simpatico. And by Chapter 7 I was completely digging the Japanese Approach to Robots: who else better elaborating in the Robotics topic, in contrast to Hollywood? And btw, it's actually an International team, as the developer Mattson Tomlin is Romanian, who cowrote the 8 chapters with Director Masashi Kudô. And among the producers the USA and Israel are present. Expect a very sober editing by Akari Saitô, just once I thought WTF, with an abrupt cut of a Misaki moment.Sure, it took long for me to settle in because I am too used associating TERMINATOR with Arnold; the kick ass Brad Fiedel main theme; and the American Way of Sci-fi Action. But now after finishing experimenting TERMINATOR ZERO, I believe the original appeal to Cameron/Hollywood's creation, will only evolve, as you find out what happens when other cultures give their take on the matter. Some of us are so die hard Cameron fans and its original approach that could not have pondered this story could take place in Japan. Find out what will you go missing, and what will be a fresh take never seen before under Hollywood's standard rule book: the extreme violence going on in this Manga can blush any Live Action Violence from the West; the profound philosophical conversation between Malcolm and his Creations goes one step further programming mature material, via Cartoons! The cliffhanger at the end promisses this is just the beginning of a -let's hope-, long exploration of the most leved Robot creature in Film History. I doubt anyone watches Terminator to feel fear: befriend the enemy! Lol. Afterall Judgement Day includes every corner in the Planet, so by taking some heat off Skynet as it "shares the mic" with Japan the chance to either "terminate" once for all the War between Humans and their Creations, or making the fire bigger, before some other World team takes over the "War effort vs. Machines".

title: Surprisingly good
author: lazarkochakovacic
body: When I first saw this, I thought it was just going to be a "money scheme bad show", but it was surprisingly good, everything from the animations (which is in my opinion the less important part) to the story, I feel like this show explained the time travel concept from all movies before this one, also I really love that the plot is not the same like in every Terminator movie before, the characters are new, the plot is new, but it's still Terminator and that's what i LOVE about this show. Also, I have to mention the plot twists, you just can't easily predict what is going to happen next, let alone get bored with the story. I am really happy that this show is cannon and I wouldn't mind for this to be the last Terminator.

title: Absolutely worth watching
author: mssshreyes
body: Title. Just finished watching it and have to say it definitely met expectations and held up to its Terminator brand while also acting as an excellent blend with anime. From the action to storytelling and pacing, everything was really fun to go through.So yes, definitely give it a watch. I watched it over a span of 3 days but it is definitely binge worthy. The last three episodes were what made my time. All the twists were not predictable but plot wise really crucial.The fact that this is my first review on IMDB says a lot about what a good watch it was. 100 percent recommended, must watch if you think about/plan about watching it.

title: More of the Same, Even in Anime Form
author: jjenk911
body: Netflix was cheeky enough to release this on August 29th, which on that day 27 years ago, Skynet gained sentience to bring about Judgment Day. Now, throw a Japanese version of Skynet - Kokoro - and throw two similar stories together in a blender and see what happens.I'm on episode 5, and I like what I'm seeing. Perhaps Kokoro doesn't see it that way; or Kokoro will follow Skynet's rule to take over human life. Could Kokoro go to war with Skynet, pitting their resources against one another? title: Same Same but Different
author: nash_jawdat
body: The show took a different turn from the movies.Since terminator 3 I was not impressed with any of the terminator movies. Until I have finally watched this one. This series was amazing and might have potential to beat the goat (terminator 2) in terms of the story.It kept me on the edge of my seat and intrigued on what's coming next.The writing was very well executed but the graphics are not my favorite. However, some parts of the shows graphics appeared to be quite different in a good way.I hope to see Arnold as a terminator in the future.Overall, great start of the season and the ending was good too.

title: Amazing!
author: mamudinhogaming
body: I must say, normally I don't like animes that much yet just because it is the Terminator related I wanted to give it a try and finished it in a day. However, the storytelling had made me feel like in the Terminator universe. I am starting to think it is way better than Sarah Connor TV Series. title: franchise goes Japanese
author: SnoopyStyle
body: It's 1997 Tokyo. Malcolm Lee has created Kokoro, an AI system to rival Skynet. A female soldier from the year 2022 is sent back in time to protect Malcolm and his family from a Terminator. While Malcolm communes with Kokoro, the Terminator is pursuing his three kids and their nanny Misaki.I love placing the Terminator franchise in Japan. The animation is suited for it. I have my doubts about the Kokoro room. Quite frankly, it would be more real to have a Professor X head gear. I love the Terminator chasing the group and the masses of iRobots. Sometimes, the group gets away from the Terminator too easily, but I can live with that. I also do like the resolution by making it an uncertain choice.

title: Expanding the lore but with terrible writing
author: LynneParks
body: I generally enjoyed the expansion to the Terminator lore. We get the point of view of Skynets take over from another country. But the writing and the characters were very bad. I thought their development and motivations were extremely basic. All of the characters. I have seen all these stories before and all these types of characters as well. It was very tedious to watch the same stories again and again. And the worst part is the lack of explanation and the just trust me approaches to critical problems. This show was exhausting and I only finished it because I don't like abandoning shows before they last episode. Summarily, great concept but the execution was lacking....

title: Really good
author: cssbatista1987
body: I'm a bit of a critic of anime, especially anything that comes from Netflix. It was with this in mind that I watched Terminator zero. The pace is moderate and the animation could be a little better, nevertheless, the series turned out to be very exciting, with no obvious plot.People need to forget about the Terminator film before watching this one, the plot is set in Japan, and although the story may be related to the American Terminator (something we may see in the future) it seems to me that this is going in a different direction (like a different timeline that was created). The soundtrack is also very interesting, and goes well with the series. I hope to see more soon.

title: From the first to the last second!
author: ikal1
body: I must be honest and say that I thought I would watch one, maybe two episodes, and then give up on the series-but that didn't happen.The series combines the most recognizable elements of Terminator (mostly from the second movie) and adds new twists that elevate the story to heights that the entire franchise lacks.The plot is as addictive as typhus fever, and after watching the first episode, you'll have no choice but to admit that you're hooked on the series like a junkie on crack. The story is exceptional, the characters are well-crafted with a few (annoying but necessary) cinematic clichés. The action is perfectly directed, fluid, and energetic. The animation needs no comment-pure perfection.All in all, this is a serious series that has the potential to present the Terminator story in a new, incredibly exciting way. A second season is inevitable, and I hope that the next episodes will stick to the path set by the first season.

title: Nothing you haven't seen already
author: adrenachrome
body:
TL;DR version: Derivative pseudo-philosophical garbage masquerading as deep insight.600 word review:
Going the anime route for an established franchise isn't a novel idea (the Animatrix did it already) but that's not what sinks this series.No, what kills it is pulling plot ideas, dialogue and scenes from all the other Terminator films (yes, even Dark Fate, as wretched as that film was) mashes them together, and presents it as something new. Alien:Romulus did this as well, and that film was complete crap as well.The 3 kids in this further the plot along by being idiots, which is a huge strike against this, or any other, film. They detract heavily from what the writers were trying to say, but ultimately the nonsensical plot (complete with possibly the longest death-exposition dump scene in modern film history) that is rushed in at the very last minute really sinks this.Utterly forgettable and like Alien:Romulus, an insult to a franchise already teetering on the edge of irrelevance.2/10 (the 2 is for the rather well done animation)

title: A great original Terminator movie
author: expresscontent
body: Where should I begin? I was pleasantly surprised that this animate series brought back the original Terminator movie vibe (Gloom and doom and loss of life). This series is definitely not at the same league as the newer Terminator movies (which the last 2 movies are the worse and messed everything up). This series continue the original storyline but changed a few things to fit the perspective from Japan's view (making it a new story line). The story line dialog and the intensity is great. I am almost done with the last episode but wouldn't mind if they make a new Terminator like this one.Hollywood should take notes and learn a few things from screen writers from Japan. They focused way to much on political/identity and forgot about making a good story into movies.

title: Better than all the live action sequels
author: marineproductions1
body: Over the years, terminator sequels and spin-offs have tried to replicate the magic of the original, but many have fallen into the trap of recycling the same narrative and thematic elements.This led to a stagnation in the franchise, as many of the films relied heavily on the same tropes: time-traveling cyborg assassins, relentless chases, and apocalyptic visions of a future dominated by Skynet.But this show is different. It has way more substance than the other sequels. It not only moves the story forward but also brings a level of innovation and emotional depth that has been sorely missing in many of the recent installments.It has a new way of looking at the story universe and it can be a good example of how to do a sequel to an established franchise that does rely on cliches.I highly recommend everyone take a look at this series.

title: Simply Amazing
author: danyfs12
body: Gritty, stylistic, complex, thoughtful and easily digestible given 30-minute episodes... After reading the negative reviews here I'm pretty sure most of them didn't watch it through but rather didn't like the initial construct or some singular critique near the beginning and wrote it off. They ultimately missed the explanations, as well as the very thoughtful and complex plot, the layers of introspection, game theory dynamics, and the well-written character development. Without any spoilers I'll say there are twists and turns as they weave the story together so it's worth acclimating at the beginning so you can thoroughly enjoy the rest. Initially I was skeptical of the anime approach but didn't take me long to really appreciate it and see how it was most likely the best path to push the limits on a gritty, stylistic take that was very fitting for the new story it told built on the foundation of the classic plot. They also go deeper into the specifics of the story's timeline which was just the cherry on top. Well done! Will be rewatching season 1 as I wait for season 2.

title: You've been Netflixed
author: bertrandma
body: I don't watch much anime, but when I watch anime, it's usually Studio I. G. As a market, anime is extremely formulaic and most of its consumer base seem thankful for this. I. G. Normally stands out for trying to do more than just rehashing high-school isekai tropes: for this alone, they deserve praise. Not everything they've done is amazing, but it's usually competently animated, and often enough visually ambitious. At the best of times (i.e. Ghost in the Shell) it is well written too.So I had high hopes for their Netflix collab. Afterall, Netflix's Devilman--however imperfect--was surprising at many level. And the first few minutes of Terminator Zero do not disappoint: remarkable drawing, daring animation, cinematic shots and excellent soundtrack, it's nearing Mamoru Oshii levels.Unfortunately it's all down hill from there. If action scenes remain pretty good (if less inventive) throughout, the characterisation is pretty terrible, as becomes abundantly clear by the end of the first episode. The series happily buys into facile intergenerational narrative, with three utterly detestable and unconvincing children characters, and a range of flat secondary characters. Some of them have excuses to be flat, others do not, but they all feel like cardboard cut outs.The worse however is definitely the writing itself, where everything has to be spelled out at least two or three times, to ensure it all remains accessible even to the most intellectually challenged (or least attentive) viewer.Someone once characterised Emily in Paris as being 'ambient television': a show designed to move so slowly and predictably that you can actually do something else while watching it, without risking to miss anything. That's one way to put it: the optimistic way. I'm not at all sure that people do something else while watching Netflix. The showrunner for Netflix's Witcher adaptation complained the producer imposed changes to the script in order to 'dumb it down' for American audiences. I'm not sure American audiences are dumber than the average Netflix spectator (who knows?), however I think this is a more convincing explanation than 'ambient television': in order to cater to the absolute maximal audience, everything needs to be spelled out, not once but twice. Don't leave anything to the viewer's imagination, and most importantly, don't leave anything ambiguous.The result is a weird mix: an attempt to make an 'adult' anime (and here IG shines as always), which at the same time is so simple and so slow that an eight years old would find it oversimplified. It's kind of depressing and kind of fascinating, in a highway-car-crash kinda way.

title: A Breath Of Fresh Air
author: wwwpaulogarciagardeyahoocom
body: After watching the first Terminator, I couldn't believe that the franchise started with a horror-chasen (I don't know how to spell the word), suspense and action. Because when everyone thinks about the franchise, they mostly think about the second movie, more reliant on action. Which I don't blame them, because I also think and love about the second movie. And after the third movie, everything else went south. I don't know why it sucked but they suck I guess. And now with the release of the series, It's amazing! Brutal like the first three movies if I remember correctly, released on Judgement Day and just pure perfect. I can't wait for season 2 and how the franchise going to be without Arnold.

title: Enjoyed it! I could nitpick and find flaws, but, no. This was GOOD overall.
author: TreeFiddy53
body: As a fan of the OG Terminator (Tr) movies, the announcement for an official Tr anime...by the animators of Ghost in the Shell...had me intrigued. But knowing what has become of the franchise in the recent past, I remained skeptical.It released on Netflix on...sure enough, August 29 aka Judgment Day in the Tr lore. This show is really good (minus a couple logic issues which we'll get to) and a lot of people are calling this the best thing in the franchise since the James Cameron movies in 1991.The show has 8 episodes, < 30 mins each ; a quick binge. You don't have to know anything about the previous movies to watch this show, could be a standalone show if you want it to be. There are several 'easter-eggs' to the first two movies that you'd appreciate if you've seen the films but it is not a necessity. Tr has one of the most iconic themes in film history and while there's a callback, the music for this show is solid as well.The story (with a touch of a Nolan-eqsue ending), very relevant in the age of AI that we live in, ends up being slightly more philosophical than I'd expected but no complaints. A couple characters familiar with Tr and what its capable of engage in a hand-to-hand combat with it, didn't know how to feel about that, but I chose not to nitpick.Overall - A very faithful adaptation of the series with a different take on it while retaining the originality; you've got to watch it for that to make sense. Fans of the movies need to watch this! Non-fans will likely end up watching it and then will go watch the movies. Win-win IMO.

title: Best Terminator Since Judgment Day!
author: jonathanvarleyjv-70104
body: Terminator Zero is the thrilling revival the franchise desperately needed. Set in Tokyo, this Netflix anime series boldly moves away from the familiar Sarah and John Connor saga, offering a fresh take that revitalises the classic themes with a modern twist. The stunning animation and intense action sequences are paired with deep, thought-provoking storylines that explore new characters and complex moral dilemmas.Showrunner Mattson Tomlin brilliantly crafts a narrative that pays homage to the original films while breaking new ground. The show's setting in Japan adds a unique flavor, and the focus on AI evolution and human resistance feels both timely and innovative. The blend of high-stakes action, emotional depth, and gorgeous visuals makes Terminator Zero a standout.With a gripping story that respects its roots yet forges ahead with bold new ideas, this series is a must-watch for fans and newcomers alike. Whether you're here for the nostalgia or excited for the new direction, Terminator Zero delivers on all fronts, proving that the Terminator franchise still has plenty of life left in it. This is, without a doubt, the best Terminator content since Judgment Day.

title: Stunning new story, true to the originals
author: imdb-10463
body: The depth of care at all levels of Terminator Zero is simply breathtaking.Without spoilers, Terminator Zero builds on the foundations of the original movies, but explores a completely new dimension. Direction, characters, animation and - most importantly - story plunge us back into the universe of the Terminator in a way that is both respectful and mind-expanding.Initially familiar scenes - the humans waging war against the machines in the far future - quickly lead to back to the days before Judgement Day itself, this time set in 1997 Tokyo. The ticking clock of Skynet's impending nuclear strike provides a gripping backdrop as we find ourselves rooting for new characters - both man and machine.This is how classic franchises should be honored and taken to the next level. I loved it and I want more.

title: Great philosophy, music and animation
author: arabnikita
body: Terminator Zero (2024)"What Makes you believe humanity is worth saving? Can you name a single good thing that your species has done for this world? Even One?"Questions such as these and a number of others were posed in this series and in many cases, much like the protagonist, I had no answers. When I began watching Terminator Zero, I did expect it to be different in a number of ways as it was an anime. However, I didn't imagine it to be filled with intellectual and philosophical dilemmas which ended up being the most enjoyable element.Terminator Zero, much like the James Cameron films, begins with a girl named Eiko being sent to the past in order to save humanity. What's different is that Eiko is sent back to Tokyo where a brilliant scientist named Malcolm has built his own uber powerful AI in an attempt to stop Skynet's domination. Consequently, Skynet sends a Terminator to stop Eiko and execute its own destructive plan to maintain the steel grip over the throat of humanity.With AI taking a progressively larger and larger space in our modern world, this show raises a number of interesting points both in simple and complex terms. Thanks to its steady pacing, we are able to digest the ideas while being entertained by the beautiful animation, cool action and the brilliant soundtrack that lingered with me after each episode. The Japanese voice acting is fantastic so I obviously recommend experiencing it that way. You can easily binge this show, but I would suggest watching 2 episodes at a time so that you could ponder the concepts that are presented in each episode..Movieswithoutshmovies on Instagram for honest movie and tv reviews.

title: Simplifying Golf with Childlike Charm
author: abphadore
body:
Rising Impact is an anime that dives into the world of golf, a sport often perceived as complex and slow-paced, and attempts to make it more accessible and entertaining for a younger audience. Directed by Toshifumi Kawase and produced by Studio Deen, the series is a mix of sports drama and coming-of-age story, wrapped in vibrant animation and childlike enthusiasm.Plot Summary
The anime follows the journey of young golf prodigy, Gawain Nanaumi, as he navigates the challenges and intricacies of the sport. Gawain's dream is to become a professional golfer, and the series documents his growth from a novice to a formidable competitor. Along the way, he encounters various mentors, rivals, and friends who help shape his journey.Simplifying Golf
One of the standout aspects of Rising Impact is its ability to demystify the sport of golf. Golf, often seen as a sport laden with technical jargon and intricate rules, is presented in a way that is easy to understand and engaging. The anime breaks down the basics of the sport, from swing mechanics to course strategy, in a manner that is both educational and entertaining.The use of visual aids, such as animated diagrams and slow-motion sequences, helps in illustrating complex concepts. The series also incorporates real-life golfing techniques and strategies, making it a useful introduction for viewers who are new to the sport. By simplifying golf and making it more approachable, Rising Impact succeeds in drawing in an audience that might have otherwise been uninterested in the sport.Character Dynamics and Childlike Elements
While the anime excels in its portrayal of golf, it falters in its character development. The characters, particularly Gawain Nanaumi, often come across as overly simplistic and childlike. This childlike portrayal can be endearing at times but often feels out of place given the sport's mature and disciplined nature.Gawain Nanaumi's character, for instance, is depicted with a level of naivety and innocence that can be frustratingly unrealistic. His rivals and mentors also lack depth, often fitting into stereotypical roles rather than being fully fleshed-out characters. This lack of complexity in character development detracts from the overall narrative, making it difficult for viewers to fully invest in the characters' journeys.The anime also tends to resolve conflicts and challenges with an ease that feels unearned. Gawain Nanaumis rapid progression and seemingly effortless victories undermine the hard work and dedication typically required in sports, especially one as demanding as golf. This 'child play' approach to character development and conflict resolution can make the series feel more like a fantasy rather than a realistic sports drama.Visuals and Animation
The animation quality in Rising Impact is commendable. Studio Deen does an excellent job in bringing the golf courses to life, with lush green landscapes and detailed character designs. The action sequences, particularly during intense golfing moments, are well-executed and add excitement to the narrative.Conclusion
Rising Impact is a commendable effort to make golf more accessible and entertaining, particularly for younger audiences. Its educational approach to the sport is its strongest asset, breaking down the complexities of golf in a way that is engaging and easy to understand. However, the series is let down by its simplistic character development and childlike portrayal of its protagonist.While the anime's charm and educational value make it a worthwhile watch for those interested in golf, viewers looking for a more nuanced and realistic sports drama might find it lacking. In summary, Rising Impact simplifies the sport of golf effectively but stumbles with its overly simplistic and sometimes unrealistic character portrayals.

title: A golf anime that is entertaining!?
author: Crystalskiez
body: Out of all the anime genres out there, I especially love sports-ones. Though I have to say I didn't expect golf to be included in those sports. The anime is serious but also a bit goofy at times, which does fit the childish but serious theme of Gawain, the MC. And what I love about this series is it's tempo. It doesn't waste ANY time with its storytelling and generally Gawain's skill in golf progresses at a fast rate which constantly keeps you entertained. The anime also does a good job of keeping the golf-courses entertaining and often introduces wild, innovative and visually beautiful courses that the players have to tackle. This in combination with the good fast-paced storytelling made the golf-games incredibly intense and fun to watch with psychological battles and actual physical struggles. That is incredibly impressive, especially for an anime about golf.Maybe a bit of a cliché anime since the MC basically has superpowers, but I still enjoyed it a ton. It's a very nice feel-good anime. Would recommend to anyone that likes a good sports-anime. Looking forward to what they will do with s3.

title: Funny, well written life-takes of a hitman trying to be normal

title: I liked it.
author: i-53389
body: I'm seeing a lot of reviewers panning this show due to their preconceived notions of what it should have been. I fornone like having the perspective of Zeon troops being hunted by the Gundam. You get glimpses of what it's like to go against a hero character, and what it takes to overcome just one.It was done in Unreal Engine 5, which means a lot of the environmental CGI can look photo realistic at times. On the other hand, they did not take the time to really work on the human character models skin and facial expressions, so it sometimes is a stark contrast to the environmental scenery. Overall, it wasn't a deal breaker for me and it was nice to see a more realistic Gundam work than a traditional animation.

title: A long time fan dream come true!!!
author: charlieyap-49274
body: Im surprise there is no review yet for this amazing series, so I'm gonna start the ball rolling here. This series presents a refreshing, "down-to-earth" perspective on the Gundam universe, offering a grounded look at the human cost of war rather than the usual large-scale strategic warfare that many fans may expect.The story deviates from the typical tactical war games that have become a hallmark of the franchise. Instead, it focuses more on the human element-the tragedies and chaos that arise from conflict. Admittedly, there are moments when the characters seem unsure of what to do, which can pull the viewer out of the immersion. Still, despite these occasional lapses, the narrative remains engaging and binge-worthy, a testament to the creator's vision. Notably, this is the first mainline Gundam series produced by a Western team, which makes the achievement all the more impressive.One of the standout features of this series is the battle scenes. The mobile suits feel massive and imposing, with their movements and speed depicted in a way that's both believable and thrilling. This is the most "grounded" portrayal of mobile suit combat since Gundam Thunderbolt, and it surpasses even that in terms of realism. However, while the fight sequences are excellent, the character animation could use some improvement. I'm hopeful that with a larger budget in future seasons, this aspect will see significant enhancement.For newcomers to the Gundam universe, there may be some terminology that doesn't quite resonate, but the core story is simple enough to enjoy without prior knowledge. Overall, I'd rate this series a solid 8/10-an impressive achievement and a worthy addition to the Gundam franchise.

title: Animation could be a lot better
author: marvelucat
body: I have not finished watching this series yet, but the animation of the characters is distractingly bad, so bad I felt like expressing my displeasure here. This is really just related to the expressions of the characters. The rendering looks very decent otherwise, but, I swear, ReBoot, a 3D animated series exactly 30 years old, the second such ever, has much better facial expressions and mouth movements. How can that be the case in 2024? Otherwise from that, the voice acting, action and pacing is pretty good, but I hope the production company fixes the glaring weakness in subsequent iterations.

title: The good, the bad and the Netflix
author: jared-25331
body:
I just finished watching the first season of Gundam: Requiem for Vengeance (2024-) and while this show was decent at best, I was also very disappointed as a Gundam fan. Then again, this show was made by Netflix, so I shouldn't be surprised.Positives for Gundam: Requiem for Vengeance (2024-):
I thought it was an interesting angle for this show to have the Principality of Zeon as the heroes and the Gundam Mobile Suit as the villain. title: Great anime even for people who aren't familiar with gundam
author: silasroy
body: I'll be honest, I tried watching original Gundam and couldn't get into it. However, as someone who doesn't watch Gundam, I thought this series was incredibly well done. I've been wondering why animators don't use unreal engine or video game style dynamics, so when this came out I was pleasantly surprised. I've been watching animation for a long time, I prefer it over live action, and I can say with certainty that this is the most detailed and realistic animation made so far. I had to leave this review because all the negative people claiming this has terrible animation and unrealistic facial features. Truly, there is no animation on the market that has such incredibly detailed facial features. You can see so much texture in the characters faces, even very subtle things like veins, dirt smudges, old scars, and even the pores on their skin. I've watched all the best animations on Netflix and this is by far the most intricately detailed I've seen. Not to say this is my favorite by any means, but I really appreciate the time and energy the creators put into these characters to make them as realistic as possible. The dialog isn't the absolute best, and lip syncing isn't great, but overall this animation deserves more love then hate, because they really stepped outside the box with this one. I think the people leaving negative reviews either weren't paying attention at all, or they're just incapable of seeing small details. I know for a fact that no one can name an animation with more detailed and realistic features then this, whether it's 2D or 3D. It's just absurd to hate an animation for not having perfectly realistic facial features, because no animation in the world is "perfectly" realistic, but this one is the closest I've seen. People are just placing completely unrealistic expectations on this animation, because if you haven't noticed animation isn't exactly known for having realistic facial features and expressions; everything is exaggerated in anime. So let go of unrealistic expectations and just enjoy the show.

title: The good the bad and the ugly . Gundam fan
author: justforthisa
body:
So this really is a mixed bag. Overall I'm very happy it was made but disappointed.There are some very strong points such as the animation the fight sequences the level of detail i like the main character who is a very strong female lead without being a mary sue.There are some very weak points such as the actual dialogue which fluctuates between well thought out episodes with realistic dialogue and other episodes that sound like they were written by chat gpt .There is a level of modernism that is thrown into this which is completely unnecessary and attracts from it.The accents are all over the place which normally compliments Gundam films and TV shows but in this case was poorly chosen and makes no sense.The middle half of it felt very weak and lackluster where is the beginning and ending was phenomenal. Episodes 1-2 and 6 held up to the original Gundam films. Where is episodes 3 through 5 varied from g gundam level of sillyness to some well done scenes.As far as the mobile suits various armor and fight scenes very well done. They do overpower the Gundam which I think was silly and change the face. But it's much better than a lot of the UC spin-offs we have.I do hope they make some video games with this assets.Strenths
Base story
Set design and details
Battle sequence
Strong female lead
Didn't red con anything
Solid voice actingWeak points
Silly secondary characters
Overpowered Gundam
Bad dialogue written by chat GPT or poorly translated
Filler episodes
Modern political discourse injected which has nothing to do with Gundam or anti war gundam themes.On the one hand I'm happy for anything uc thats new. But this very easily could have been much better with a little editing and a little better writing....
I'm convinced if you cut this down from 3 hours to an hour and a half and used ai to change some lines and add some it would actually A+ film . But its not . Worth watching for any Gundam fan not sure for anybody else.

title: The series and story is amazing but the visuals...
author: fqypeters
body:
I really love Gundam and have been watching and playing with it since the 80's.But I have an extremely hard time trying to enjoy this due to the absolute wonky and amateur looking visuals.As if they hired a company that only showed them pictures of what it could look like and the character facial details which looked amazing. title: Ignore the negative reviews
author: jakeleinen
body: Want a great Gundam show? It's here.Everything that defines Gundam is included in interesting, sometimes new and very entertaining ways. There's no long exposition heavy scenes, the flow of the show is consistent and engaging across all 6 episodes. Every episode hits, no fillers.I loved the abundance of references to lore and Easter eggs deployed here.I struggle to come up with any areas where the show falls short. Any negativity you read about this show will be from non Gundam fans. Which maybe that is a pitfall. Though my wife, not a Gundam fan loved it, I think an appreciation and viewing of previous series is a prerequisite to understanding the greatness of this show.Characters are not super deep but then again they don't need to be. Every archetype of character from previous shows is represented. We've seen these types before and so heavy characterization wasn't necessary.

title: Love, Death & Mechs
author: jonford-02149
body: Enjoyed this very much. Inspite of knowing very little about the Gundam franchise I was able to engage the story and got attached to the characters very quickly. I felt transported to the Eastern front and effectively "dropped in" with the Red Wolves. The tough female protagonists made the story feel less predictable helping to eschew the clumsy machismo that often comes with military shows. The mech battles did not disappoint and the classic designs were fun to see in a computer animation style. While the motion capture doesn't seem to have progressed much since the Captain Harlock movie the human character designs were very interesting and added a lot of depth to thier personas; these would make teriffic cosplay costumes. I really hope to see more from the Gundam series in this style perhaps exploring the background of some of the more central protagonists.

title: Good, satisfactory, truthful to the original.
author: argento100
body: Not a fan of the human animation, the rest of it is spectacular. The fighting scenes are awesome.Watch it in Japanese, lip sync is made for japanese dialogue. And English voice over is awful.A solid 8, expected much worse from Netflix, but was very good.Pure nostalgia and they were faithful to the spirit and message of Gundam, war is terrible, everyone suffers, dehumanizing the other only leads to becoming monsters ourselves, soldiers die for no glory, everyone loses and we all want peace.It respects the lore, it doesn't add unnecessary dumb stuff for the imaginary "modern audiences".For that I praise it. Hope there is more incoming.

title: Jank
author: egskriver
body: There's a lot of issues with this series. Quality jumps all over the place; good motion capture by the looks of it sometimes, other times walk cycles pulled straight from the ps1 era, cool looking laser firing sometimes and other times it looks like firecrackers in a puppet show, random freeze frames and meaningless slow motion.The characters feels flat, dialogue is not interesting, is there a story?On a positive tho, landscapes and scenery looks great, even if the colors are bland and mostly brown. And I did enjoy the mech night scenes.Can't give it more than a 3/10 cause mech fights alone can't give it a good score.

title: Entertaining spectacle with decent story
author: victorbaerner
body: I'm giving it an 8 because it was entertaining and enjoyable enough to want to keep watching more after each episode. The animation had some scenes that were truly breathtaking and captured the feeling of mecha combat in all its glory. It also had some scenes that were very noticeably not modeled thoroughly, but they weren't many.I would say to maybe not expect an amazing Gundam series, but I felt it captured enough of the feeling to make it a pretty amazing animation for me.My main takeaways was that the show was given too few episodes at only 6, which made it hard to fully flesh out the narrative/story and that they had to rush some of the animation scenes. It did well with what it was given in my opinion and had enough epic scenes to make it worth watching.Based on what I saw, a fully supported second season could take it to the level of greatness and I hope it gets one.

title: Worst Gundam Anime Ever
author: liyuegun
body: This is definitely the most childish Gundam animation I have ever seen. The core of Gundam is anti-war. In the original gundam, Zeon killed billions of innocent people with poison gas and landing colonial satellites with Zakus. However, it is said in the show that Zaku saved a lof of lives It's simply an insult to the original Gundam. And the subsequent plot puts Zeon in the position of a victim, which is simply unreasonable.The writer not only doesn't understand Gundam but also doesn't understand military affairs. The protagonist tells Gundam not to continue attacking at the end, but she hasn't stopped killing people in previous battles, so Zeon can only kill people but not the Federation? What is the logic of this?

title: This should be the way forward
author: seanjosephchow
body: Much better than the recent 'low effort' anime and no longer a 'kid' show.The storytelling could use more pollishing but the combat scenes were spot on with UE5. Really brings the impact of mobile suits to the next level.Hopefully they can get renewed with a larger budget and go along the timeline to also aim towards a new generation of fans, I think this is a better starting point and a whole different genre than the anime in a good way, and could turn big; such as clone wars did to star wars.Now gundam just needs actual well made AAA games or at least be as good as mecha break instead of gundam revolution. If they could pull this off a battlefield style gundam game in UE5 should be very doable.

title: Short and spectacular Gundam series that encapsulates the horrors war brings to everyone
author: davidpayze-29934
body: For such a short series (being only six episodes long: 30 minutes each), this show has kept me hooked to the characters, story and presentation.Although the latter aspect may still need to be developed more properly, with perhaps better facial animations and movement, unreal engine 5 manages to captivate the sheer scale of devastation brought on by the One Year War.All the actors and actresses has done an excellent job at conveying what it would be like to survive in a war on the losing. This includes their emphasis in the tragedy of loss.Truly an excellent choice for newcomers to the franchise!

title: Love it, will always love it....
author: winsenvanmark
body: A new take on a huge franchise, bravo is al I have to say. Yeah and great graphics for seconds.I don't know how this show always pulls on my heartstrings, but it definitely did it again.I didn't know this was comming out, but at this low point in my life, I am so happy it did.I think the show portraits every major human emotion: honour, loyalty and self sacrifice.If you're here reading this, remember you're not alone. Many people feel like this all around the world.As a 37 year old white guy from the Netherlands, chances are you are going trew worse times than me.... but I repeat: if you see this show trew my perspective, this is what the world needs.

title: Attack of the Gundam-sized clichés
author: newark-61086
body: 6 Episodes stock-full of clichés, devoid of backstory, lacking any real character development and battle scenes that pretty much all look the same. The story is about as dull and generic a war story as I have ever seen.There is honestly very little here in terms of redeeming qualities. I was tempted to give one star, but some of the visuals are relatively pretty - not so much the characters, who are overly glossy in appearance and stiffly animated, like video game characters from about 10 years ago, but the landscapes at least. Sadly, that is the best I can say about this show. I'd be incredibly surprised if somebody decided to give this a second season.

title: Would have been great 20 years ago
author: marnesiath
body: The CGI is the worst I've seen in many years, it's so bad that even Final Fantasy Spirits Within from 2001 did a lot better than this movie, voice acting ranges from quite good to "friend of the director" quality but unfortunately outside the main characters the voice acting is significantly worse.The story does seem interesting and the main characters have some depth and interesting personalities, it's just a shame it's wrapped in such mediocrity and obviously had a shoe string budget.Save yourself some time, go watch one of the anime especially given how many there are now and how deep the story and characters are in each of them.

title: Made me want to watch the original animation
author: sirlife-53804
body:
I Never saw the original anime, maybe a couple of episodes when i was young.But this version made me interested again!I love the mobile suits and fights, and the overal graphics.Yes its still visually very game styled cgi
and especially the facial expressions and lip sync is weak. title: Swing and a miss
author: socomgemini-15617
body: Neat idea, poor execution. Where to start.It's a filler for existing Gundam fans, and I feel unfriendly to the uninitiated. There is little impact so far in the story. You can chalk this up to just a small grunts story in a larger play. As for newcomers.... The show asumes you know what Gundam and the One Year War is about. It provides very little context to the setting or conflict it's based upon. It will just seem like "Robots smash!" for alot of people.On that note. There is very little character development and only backstory for the main character. Now I could be a little biased, but Gundam usually focuses on the motives and internal struggles of it's character. Here, it's pretty much taken the back seat. It is mostly survival, combat, and vengance in the moment. There is very little to get you attached to the characters themselves.When it came to the mechs and aircraft, I loved it. The Gundam EX looked awesome, and liked it's feral like temperment. The animation was smooth, the action was fantastic. But not all armour has equal attention. They couldn't decide how much horsepower the tanks had, and vehicles were inconsistent with the terrain it was on. It's details that stand out, and it get's worse with character models.Production was inconsistent.There are scenes where they look normal. Usually the high action scenes. But in others, they either look like they are being moved by marionette strings, or they are trying to throw out as much hip into their swagger as possible. Details can be offputting. Mud and dirt are built into the facial textures rather than being applied on top. They give a wax like sheen for sweat, but they accomodate efforts for protruding whispers. It's not like they weren't trying, but obviously some things were rushed and some things cut short.Character design. I really liked them. They were not generic. Most of them stood out. Application between audio and animation took a hard hit. I can forgive the lack of lip sync. This is a global franchise and sometimes it's an impossible request. It's just more noticable in a 3d format. My problem however is the aesthetic, the body language, the facial expressions (or their intensity) and the audio do not mesh for alot of characters. Hailey in particular. Loved the visual, but nothing after matched up to that. And her voice isn't the only one that didn't suit her character.Audio. They focused, again, on combat. But outside of it, the audio dressing felt lacking and empty. Squad is eating by the campfire, but you can't hear the battalion in the background? A couple episodes were rough when there is prolonged pause between sentences.I haven't even covered them all. There are too many production issues from big to small that take me out of this.Maybe it was the transition to a different medium. Maybe they needed more or longer episodes. Maybe too many ideas and not enough time to cook.I love Gundam. But this didn't leave me with a lasting impression, and will probably forget it exists within the next 3 years.

title: (Only) if you loved the original Mobile Suit Gundam, you will also love this
author: nicus-x
body: Only if you grew up loving the original Mobile Suit Gundam you can fully appreciate this series and see beyond the puppet-like rendering of the human characters and the awful English voices. If you belong to this aging category you will love the vehicle and Mobile Suit design and rendering, and the point of view from the other side of the fence. One side freedom fighters are always terrorists or merciless invaders for the other side.After a first try with the English version, I switched to Japanese audio with subtitles, and it sounded better.Also, don't try watching it with someone who didn't watch and love the original anime. They will probably hate it.

title: Unwatchable and Outdated
author: rickanderson-16283

title: Great graphics, messed up story
author: Snootz
body: As someone totally unacquainted with Gundam, I'm not bringing any pre-conceived notions or bias into this review. Graphics wise this was excellent, but these days that's kind of a given. Anyone who can't produce good CGI needs to get out of the business. So their CGI is (taken for granted) good.There are MANY reviews here that pan the CGI as "PS2 era", "non-realistic" etc etc. 'Scuse me... but when did anyone declare that ANIMATION is supposed to be photo-realistic? Yes, when I first started watching it I thought, "This looks like cut-scenes from a game"... and I was totally okay with that. I *like* cut-scenes (not necessarily made into a movie though). But the animation didn't bother me at all. The "heavy" feel of the battle tanks fighting, the movement of the mobile units, the well-done explosions were all spot-on. Who cares if the skin textures aren't photo-perfect?As far as imperfect lip-syncing... when was the last time anyone saw a Japanamerica anime that had any kind of lip-syncing at all? Usually we see the mouth move a zillion miles a second only to utter a few words. Bad lip syncing is kind of a GIVEN in these films. However I can say that personally, at no time during the film did lip syncing even occur to me as an issue... so it can't have been as bad as some negative reviews paint it to be here. (And mind you, this is a negative review. If it really was bad lip-syncing, I'd say so.) Lip syncing is nit-picking ESPECIALLY in an anime-based movie, and the least of this flick's significant problems.The CGI was good for this type of film, but CGI doesn't make a story, and that's where this falls so flat. This is basically a cookie-cutter war film. Heroes live. Heroes die. There are no "good guys" or "bad guys" here; it is two political factions under the delusion that war and killing is the path to peace. Throw in a few non-essential F-bombs to make it all "adult" and we have a formulaic war film. Yawwwn. Fine for adrenaline addicts; not so fine for those of us looking for a bit of thought put into the plot. (Ouch... that ending.)There are of course the individual stories (which they never delve in to deeply enough to make them deeply moving). It's basically oooohhh.. giant robot vs giant robot wowie wow. Six episodes that are basically identical in plot. Fight. Run. Fight again. Run again. Attack after attack. Death of close friend after close friend etc etc etc. And will someone please kill off hyper-cliche Major English Alcoholic and put a believable character in his place? PLEAASEE??? (Admittedly, this character was mildly interesting because he's a guy that had obviously seen too much war and was on the verge of PTSD... but still a lame and annoyingly cliche presentation.)THE DEAL BREAKER. The most disappointing thing in this film is the ending. I can't go in to it without extreme spoilers; suffice to say it makes one really question the sanity of the major. Senseless to the point of stupid would be a pretty spot-on description. Here is a character that war has changed beyond hope or sensible thought. Aside from that, it's a "plot twist" that seems just totally ridiculous in this setting. Summary: "What is she thinking?"I note several other reviews here make the same observation. The writing team really blew it on this one, and failed to salvage any potential in this film by bombing the ending.I suspect that flipping the "good guy / bad guy" roles of the two factions may appeal to fans from that perspective, but it does nothing for those unacquainted with prior stories. It's a weak plot twist at best and with no preliminaries, falls flat as a story contrivance. It does serve to point out that no matter which side of a war someone is on, they're still people. Had it been reversed, the Gundam unit that is presented as an "evil executioner figure" here could easily be turned into the nigh-unbeatable hero (and I expect that was the case in the earlier anime). Role reversal has been done before, and better.Overall it was six episodes of rather pointless war film. For those into battle games or Gundam fanboys it may be an ooh-ahh kind of thing, but even with that set, at this point with well over 1,000 votes it didn't even score 7 stars. As a neutral viewer, I rate it on how well it was done as a series... and that comes down to three things: story, character, CGI. The CGI is a given and IS JUST FINE considering the context. The character personalities are just barely beyond flat with the typical YES SIR! Soldier mentality, with the plot is flatter than their personalities. Some stars for turning an anime into a presentable 3D CGI with good physics... and that's about it (especially considering that godawful lame ending. Really.)

title: VERY enjoyable and engaging, character animation a bit lacking
author: chapstik-06819
body: Absolutely loving this. Compared to most Gundam shows, this is a slam dunk. Of course shows like 79, 8th MS Team, and Unicorn will make this look like a side project... I'm thoroughly enjoying it more than Seed or other series. I can look past bad animation. Do I expect more quality from the producers. Yes. But do I enjoy this show? Absolutely!The mech animation is gorgeous. However, the human animation is very uncanny, and feels like someone was moving parts with a computer mouse. In the first episode, I could even see an unfinished walk cycle. I can look past this as someone who enjoys movies with plenty of 90s cheese. I feel like the animation team was experimenting with this series because of how short it is. I have a lot of hope for 3D animation from Bandai and Sunrise in the future after seeing how they animated the fight scenes.Rated 9/10 because I feel like in terms of enjoyment, it's criminally underrated. Had a very fun time with the show and loved the Mobile Suit designs.

title: Dissapointing Gundam
author: arayarvians
body: I expected Far Cry 6-level graphics for 2024, but what I saw looks more like Far Cry 4, which was released back in 2014. The story feels lifeless due to the poor facial expressions. The characters, despite their detailed designs, lack the emotional depth that brings a story to life. When their faces fail to convey genuine emotions, it becomes challenging to connect with the plot or feel invested in their journeys. This lack of expression makes scenes that should feel intense or emotional fall flat. Even with well-crafted environments, advanced textures, and dynamic lighting, the immersion breaks when the characters look so disconnected. It's disappointing that in a game with such visual potential, the storytelling suffers because the characters don't feel real or believable, leaving a gap between the audience and the narrative.

title: Desapointing on all front except for story and Robots
author: hydradragon
body: I watched a lot of Gundam series, enough to recognize the suits. I watched 2 episodes and so far it's not good.One of the thing I like from the series is the non-stop action in fighting scene. Clever twist plot, and big giant robots fighting in an epic music score while the pilot talk to each other and try to get the edge on their opponent.In the 2 episodes I watched so far, the animation is rough, like year 2000 rough. Skyrim, Reboot, kinda rough. I can't believe how bad it is. Looks like they used the same animator for tanks, robots and humans. In the first episode, you can see the main protagonist moving with very stiff hands and arms. So much so I thought she had metal hands. There was some action for sure but it turned so blunt without any music to support it, that it felt like I was watching an incomplete or in progress preview of a show.Even the cliff edge ending at the end of the first episode felt bad.They should have kept working on it for at least another year and get better animators.Sorry for any fans that will have to endure it to the end.

title: Weird
author: and-46245
body: I'm not a Gundam fan so I figured I'd give this new show a go, hoping that perhaps it could be my entry into the series. But as some friends have put it: it's a mix of incredible jank and some good visuals.The jank comes from the really poor lip syncing. While I understand that mouth animations in 3D is actually quite demanding this still looks really bad compared to...well, anything else in 2024.Fights and battles are pretty neat, but I can't help but feel like they could've made this into an actual game instead and it'd both look and feel better than this does. The robots look good, but the people are really uncanny and weird. Their lips barely move and never fit what they say, the voice work is really spotty, the dialogue feels really basic and it comes together as incredibly bland characters. They act, talk and move like they're from a game from 10 years ago.I'm gonna guess whatever poor non-unionized workers where whipped into animating this didn't get to wipe the tears and sweat off their faces when they were made to do this show.I also took notice of how bad the audio mixing is and how little music there is. The latter is really noticable.This does not feel like a 2024 production at all. It feels cheap and bland without any soul.Seems entirely in line with other garbage Bandai Namco makes nowadays. Giant, soulless corporation making Product.

title: Feels Like a Video Game Cutscene
author: wbk-88055
body: First off, the animation feels like a bad Love, Death & Robots knock-off. It looks like it was made in a video game engine, almost like the whole show was filmed using Unreal Engine 5. IMO it comes off as lazy, as if they didn't bother with real animators or actors and just recorded the in-game graphics. It lacks that special touch that makes CGI movies truly immersive, and the final product is visually underwhelming.The story is no better. It's incredibly predictable, revolving around a woman who wants to return home to her child. It's all very one-dimensional, and the "humans are bad" narrative feels tired and overused. You know exactly where the story is going, and there's no depth or originality to keep you engaged.Disclaimer: I'm not a Gundam expert. Years ago, I watched Gundam Seed and liked the story, but I never really got into the other spinoffs because I didn't enjoy the older animation style. I always appreciated the lore and the potential in its universe.I came into this show hoping it would bring something fresh and exciting, especially with the modern animation. But Gundam: Requiem for Vengeance is a letdown in almost every way.The fights are just loud, chaotic special effects with no emotional weight behind them. The arguments between characters feel forced and unrealistic, and the writing leaves a lot to be desired.In the end, it's just a shallow, forgettable series. Six episodes later, there's nothing that stands out except that it's a missed opportunity to do something great with the Gundam universe. The animation, writing, and overall execution 5.4/10, and that's being generous.

title: Okay, but...

UHD and Dolby Vision don't help here either.I'm not sure why the quality is that bad, Netflix showed before how great CGI can look like. title: It's a meh, Gundam
author: DrCCat
body: The good: the mech combat is good with explosions abundantly peppered in. Cool action, uniforms, and world building pulls you in. The music is decent and adds to the tension. You can count on the action to keep things interesting and has good pacing.The bad: if you just watch for the mech fighting scenes you should be good. The uncanny valley by the character interaction is at Polar Express levels. The character's action are predictable and the same stereotypes we have seen before with nothing new added. Honestly, characters act w/o any repercussions for their actions, and no lessons are learned. Nothing deep is worth considering like you would see in most decently written anime. Though there are hints of introspection and insight, then back to the action. If you ever spent time in the military, one would know 90% of the actions taken would get characters killed within the 1st 10 minutes of a real fire fight. Suspension of disbelief is highly recommended & encouraged.The ugly: one big meh one would expect from Netflix. Turn of turn your brain, consume product, & be excited for next product. Nothing new just cool robot fighting & explosions.

title: Mixed Feelings
author: ShadowsBeneathTheLight
body: Honestly I don't know how I feel about this series. It's not bad, but it's definitely an interesting take. First off the animation: at times it looks really good. Personally I don't mind th video game like cutscenes with much more modern CG. The gore and explosions look amazing. But the faces is where we run into the uncanny valley problem. At times the characters look decent, particularly from side angle shots. But full on the characters suddenly look almost claymation like. It's hard to explain what exactly is going on but it is noticeable.As for the story itself, we only get 6 episodes 20 minutes long so there really isn't much there. You may come to like the Captain aka the main character but beyond that, everyone else is more or less forgettable because they don't get much screen time. For casual fans who don't know much about Gundam, you may like this show for fast paced action done with decent animation/effects. But for those enough who know who the Principality of Zeon are... yeah this is definitely an "interesting" direction.I'm not opposed to the idea of following their side of the story for a season or show specific to them if it is done well and acknowledges who they are. Frankly I thought it was very cool to see them retreating only to relentlessly get stalked by the titular Gundam. From their point of view it's got to be absolutely terrifying constantly hunted and bested by an unstoppable mobile suit who the audience knows is drenched in plot armor (because they are the main character of the franchise). In this regards, I really liked this idea. But where this falls apart is the show fails to really acknowledge the Zeon are the bad guys. They are quite literally spacenazis. They legit invade other territories, commit mass genocide, use biological weapons to wipe out civilian populations, when they run out of resources they then invade earth and wipe out half the population, yes literal billions of people, and yet this show wants us to then pretend they are good guys or at the very least the "victims" in a terrible war they started.I'm sorry that part I can't just get behind. Does that mean every single individual soldier in Zeon or any army for that matter is pure evil? No. But let's not whitewash an army that commits constant war crimes and genocide. There's a line during one episode where the main character cries for the Gundam to stop attacking them because no one else has to die and just want to go home. Girl your army invaded Earth, wiped out half the population, stripped it of resources and made life so terrible for those who remain that literal children are conscripted into the army just so they can get food to survive. And you think you guys deserve mercy. So yall good decimating half of earth but when it's just your squad left, now you suddenly say there's been too much death smh.This is why this trend of trying to humanize literal evil needs to stop. The people won't buy it and frankly it sends the wrong message. Had the show instead actually made a half way attempt at acknowledging Zeon are evil and kept the premise of a squad being relentlessly hunted down by the Gundam with an almost horror tone, it would've been great. But with the mixed messaging and other flaws this show safely sits at a 5. Neither good or bad, just different.
