title: Updated for the Modern Audience - whoever they are
author: RogerBorg
body: A mopey, masculinised Cara Loft meanders through some slow, dragging, uninteresting, overly verbose scenes, with utterly generic animation, pausing every few minutes to cry about some event from her past that we haven't seen, in order to be flattered, praised and validated by all around her.This is the She/Her-Hulk version of the character, written by the writer, to represent the writer, for the writer - the same stunning talent that previously brought us Witcher: Blood Origin.Like that absolute calamity, it's baffling who the audience for this is meant to be. I know who it's not though - me.

title: A New Perspective.
author: jewjewdove
body: Since I was a little girl I had always looked up to Lara Croft. I watched my Grandma play every single game from the first one up to Legend, then when I got my first playstation my mom bought underworld and I played that. I am 18 years old now and just finished the triology a couple months ago. Lara Croft isn't just a badass female lead anymore, she has blossomed into a genuine person with feelings. The show deeply dives into her trauma from the games and the way shes avoiding coping with them by refusing herself a minute of rest which is relatable to my personal life. Lara Croft is now more influential to me than she ever has been before, seeing her behind the scenes, the snippets where she IS vulnerable but still the strong heroic badass fighter she always is instills so much hope and admiration into me. I hope girls all over the world continue to look up to her, her porportions are realistic and while she's toned and tough she can also be soft and feminine. She is the female protagonist I've longed for my whole entire life and I refuse to let the creators hard work go to waste. Lara is a beautifully written and extremely well thought out character and as someone who's been a fan since the first game I'd trust my word.

title: Fake Lara Croft
author: Arthur_Revan
body: Animation and story are mediocre, support cast is a giant facepalm, but the biggest crime is the Lara, or to be precise, the completely lack of her.One of THE best female characters in the history of humanity, reduced to the pathetic shell full of BS drama. This is a completely different person wearing her skin and made for "modern audience". The "writers" do not understand what made her great, or more likely they don't want to.If you want to see the REAL Lara Croft, then play: "Tomb Raider: Anniversary", "Tomb Raider: Legend", "Tomb Raider: Underworld".Best trilogy and the best representation of the beloved character.

title: Very fun and captivating!!
author: luanarodriguesalb
body: I was so excited to watch it when the series came out that I finished it all in one day, and it was so much fun! I really liked the series, and I confess that watching it for the second time made me appreciate it even more. I don't understand why some people hated it. I know many were tired of Lara's suffering during the games, but no other game has managed to achieve such a significant evolution in her character as this animation did.The mourning aspect was handled with great attention and care, showing that they truly wanted to end all that suffering and transform Lara into who she always was. This conclusion is evident in episodes 7 and 8, which are, for me, the best episodes.I can't believe those who didn't like it actually watched the whole series because you can clearly see Lara's character evolution by the end and what she will become in the second season and the next game. Finally, I loved Lara's personality and her dynamics with the other characters. I had so much fun with the series that some flaws didn't bother me. People should try to enjoy things and stop being overly critical.

title: Have writers lost their talent?
author: chriscrossvikings
body:
The diminishing quality of scripts these days has been worrying. It is often that people to try to write for a modern audience rather than to stay true to quality and a profound story.Lara croft is an exceptionally easy character to write. But here she is surrounded by nagging pathetic friends, her whole life is pretty depressing.There is no fun fascinating exploring where we are allowed to be inspired by the wonder of her Tomb Raiding skills.The show is so depressing I find that my childhood memories of the same character have been greatly diminished. I shall stop
writing now before I get depressed.

title: Has a lot more potential than people give it credit for
author: morgueprince
body: The animation and art style are beautiful, the fight scenes look amazing. title: Social Emotional Learning (SEL) masquerading as entertainment.
author: grasslalexej
body: Within Freirean Pedagogy, the concept of SEL is the driving mechanism of the explicitly political purpose of education. One of its central tools is the establishment of "Generative Themes", which are supposed to envoke questions within the auditorium, which in turn create an environment of "Critical Pedagogy", which in turn facilitates the deconstruction of "problematic structures" within society & individual perception of self & community. This is a Marxist concept, most prominently demonstrated in USSR & Maoist China.Make no mistake, this production is not targeted at the original fans of the franchise, who are 40+ by now. Instead, it's targeted at their kids, who have no clue about who Lara actually was & why & how she came to fame as one of the most beloved female characters of all time.Away with the witty, cheeky, sassy, confident, wildly feminine, adventurous, independent, resilient Lara of olde! Hooray to the new & improved, traumatized, emotionally unstable, whiny, angry, in-constant-need-of-a-hug butch Lara, complete with - ahem - "preferential ambiguity", which just so happens to aggregate a not so ambiguous, DEI, paint-by-numbers supporting cast.Why, you ask? Because of the first paragraph, that's why. Keep your kids away from this.I gave it two stars because of the animation. There are glimpses of effort. It could have been three, had they actually put some grease into it. I mean, did they even watch "Arcane" or "Blue Eye Samurai"?Of course they have. Now I'd like to see the budget. I can't find any mention anywhere...

title: Just play the games

title: A major disappointment
author: vassiliskounelis
body: The new Lara series on Netflix is a major disappointment and has nothing to do with the Lara Croft we all loved. The character is weak, boring, and in no way embodies the iconic persona of Lara, who was dynamic, had humor, and a strong sense of style. Instead, this reboot version feels dull and uninteresting.I don't understand why they keep portraying Lara in such a bland way. This approach has become tiresome, and it fails to spark any excitement. The plot is equally boring, and all we see is Lara crying and dealing with psychological issues. Nothing stood out or was memorable, and it definitely doesn't live up to the image of the strong, stylish heroine we used to know and love.

title: Excellent tie in to Laras storyline
author: e_alaby
body:
I feel like a lot people are not open to how the owners of the franchise are trying to shape and evolve Lara Croft, while respecting her roots.I am a huge Lara fan, as and such, I have not agreed to everything that has come out, but in general, overall, I feel like they are doing an excellent job of taking such a legacy and presenting it to us in a new way, but still respecting what Lara stands for, who she is, and the path she is taking into becoming the Lara that we love and grew up with.Since I have more good than bad comments, I will start with the things I would have liked different in the show. I absolutely love her classic outfit, with the shorts. It is, in my opinion, such an iconic look of Lara, that I wish that they would bring out more (at least something similar), to that original outfit. There are some glimpses of this in the series, but in general, she is wearing pants and a blouse all the time. The blouse is similar to her classic look, but it lacks the shorts.I was very happy in how they created this series, and how it is tying into her storyline after the recent video games. What they have done with the new reboot games is start from a true origins perspective, when Lara was just starting her journey into becoming the character that most of us know. Early in the games she is an insecure, scared, and confused Lara. But throughout the games progression, we see how all of those experiences start shaping her as a stronger, smarter, less intimidated Lara.The reason why I think this series is really well done is because, up until now we had not seen as many signs of the classic "nonchalant" Lara. The classic Lara was very independent, calm, cool, smart, tough, and didnt flinch in the face of danger.This series takes the previous Lara from the reboot games, and with all that has happened to her so far, uses that to finally start shaping her into the strong, independent, smart, original classic Lara. Throughout the episodes, she says or does things that in the reboot games, she would never do. In general, we feel like she is not as scared anymore, and takes matters into her own hands more.I was really happy to also see that on a couple of occasions, she even made puns or jokes when she was in a dangerous situation, this was a treat and a new revelation of how she is now evolving into a bolder, stronger, and more confident character! This is more of the classic Lara that I grew up with and always loved. I am glad that they are respecting her roots, and it seems like they are gearing it up so that as more shows / games come out, turn her into the classic character of the 90's. At least thats what I hope for.That being said, the end of one of the later episodes was the best!! (when she aquires something). This enforces what I mentioned of her evolution to the classic Lara from her original adventures. Thank you to all the contributors of Laras Journey so far!! You guys have done an amazing job. Its not easy to take a classic icon, elaborate on her story and roots, and
please all fans at the same time.

title: I've seen it before
author: marcoregueira-834-481209
body: In the first 5 minutes, two white Anglo-Saxon foreigners go to a South American country, kill some wildlife, cause damage to an archaeological site, steal an ancient treasure, kill a few locals, and then smuggle the relic out of the country. These characters, portrayed as heroes or adventurers, display a sense of entitlement and privilege, committing crimes without any real consequences. The narrative reinforces harmful stereotypes and colonial attitudes, as they act with impunity and disregard for local cultures and people. I agree it's just a TV show for fun, but isn't it time to change some outdated narratives that glorify exploitation, white saviorism, and cultural appropriation?

title: dont watch if you're a fan of lara croft
author: syahrein
body: After logging in to review, I was incredibly disappointed with how Lara Croft has been portrayed in this latest version. Lara Croft has always been a symbol of strength, intelligence, and adventure, but this version strips away everything that made her iconic. Compared to previous games, this feels like a huge step backward.

title: A lot is lost in this series
author: sohzie
body: I try to keep an open mind when ever I see adaptations of games to animation/movie, but as usual time will prove that adaptations don't really capture the games they are based on more often than not. I have various qualms about the liberties taken with this animated version that go beyond the typical 'She doesn't look like xyz.' I will not be speaking of spoilers in this.First off, the pacing is very disjointed and off, almost as if they didn't know what kind of character they were trying to make. Lara Croft, in many iterations, is not a get down and dirty brawler like they are trying to make her out to be in this. She has generally been a very intellectual, well thought out and planned individual, who is also agile and fit enough to scale rough terrain. This not only was relayed in the way she spoke, but in the intricate puzzles she could run into while in various tombs, down to the very interactions she had with the villains. In this animated foray, she looses a lot of that for what appears to be an attempt to make her more masculine, but vulnerable and less likely to rely on her intellect. An aspect I do not like at all.The animation style is a mixed bag. There are times where I genuinely think that the animation is fairly high in value and work, but other times where I am left wondering if certain aspects are being forced on characters making them feel unnatural compared to other drawn characters in the series. Unlike various adaptations of Lara Croft in games and movies, the features of this Lara Croft have a very.....forced look that isn't at all like any prior iterations. It isn't because she has muscle definition, it is because there are other facial structure and body structure that seem indicative of something else.Supporting characters are either cliche or very forced in 'type' in such a way that it actively takes away from the story they are trying to tell. It feels almost like a rehash of a story the SE games did with Lara's past, but they tried to flesh it out to force fit other characters in so that it diversified the scope and breadth of Lara as a character, without really doing it well. Think of a Jigsaw puzzle where the person putting it together finds a piece that almost fits, but instead of trying another piece just jams that one together and calls it good enough.Overall I find it hard to really recommend this series to anyone, whether you are a new or old fan of Lara Croft. This animation feels like a cash grab rather than a genuine effort series over all.

title: "Always looking for 'treasure' to be more exciting than it is"
author: daisukereds
body: She can jump a mile horizontally, pierce solid rock with a knife, moves without ANY resistance underwater (as if she wasn't), gets hurt but doesn't matter!Ultimately, the visuals are pretty decent and the animations are okay. Hayley Atwell has a nice voice.. I guess. But it is pretty boring and iterative on already explored ideas. Almost like a children's show. I especially didn't enjoy it as much as I would have, had the companions not been as annoying or the plot as generic.I would really like to see the original Lara animated, but it probably wouldn't work as the Action gameso do, when you are in Control."Good job, Lara. I'm proud of you!"

title: Absolutely loved it!
author: nanitheducc
body: Dead Boy Detectives is a decently fast-paced show with lots of well written characters and a great storyline.It is set in The Sandman universe, but how exactly it fits within the timeline, I am not sure.It has been a while since I watched The Sandman though.This show has everything I would want from entertainment. Supernatural creatures, Ghosts, Witches and Mediums? I'm in. There is queer representation? Not only that, the queerness isn't ignored, the butt of a joke, but just another way of being? Take all my money.After rewatching it for several times, you really start to notice all the little details that everyone involved put into this masterpiece. The acting is very good, the costume department went above and beyond and the set designs?? Gorgeous.Everything has it ups and downs ofcourse, which is why I gave it a 9/10 instead of a 10/10. There is always room for improvement.Without delving too far into spoiler territory, everything hell related could have been... stretched out more? I would have loved it if we got to see more of hell and all it entails for 2 episodes instead of just 1.This brilliant show truly deserves all the attention it's getting. I absolutely love it, and would love it even more if we get to see even more of the Agency and their adventures!

title: love it
author: yesterdaysfish
body: The show is fun, I love the special effects, I love the characters.It's gory and campy in just the right amounts for me. The soundtrack is nice.It has Ruth Connell.The first episode didn't catch me, but after the second I couldn't stop watching. I binged the show in two days.It's not perfect at all, but it's not claiming to be and it's an overall great experience and definitely worth a watch (or three in my case).I hope there's going to be more because I want to know what happens next. I want to see all the relationships unfold and develop, because that's a thing the show does, there's so much interpersonal development going on.If you like supernatural themes, ghosts and witches and you're into quirky and diverse characters then this is the right show for you.

title: Lockwood User Review comparison flawed
author: BarneyGrapes
body:
After reading all the reviews comparing this to Lockwood, I wouldnt base your enjoyment of this series on these comparisons. I also think there's some attachment bias when they state Lockwood is better. It was first, and they're probably a little aggravated, understandably so, that their series was cancelled and Dead Boy isn't filling the gap of unfinished business or story completion they're yearning for. And I agree. Cancelling good series is frustrating.They can be forgiven for making the comparison, since at the very base the comparison is tempting due to the ghost theme and the makeup of the team. But the similarities end there.Dead Boy Detectives (dbd) is fantasy based. Witches, faeries, elementals, gods, etc
Lockwood is more horror / ghost focused.Dead Boy is current day, mystery focused. Detectives rather than investigators
Lockwood is more dystopian future focused. They're more agents fighting a war than detectives. I would argue that there are plenty of movies that do Lockwood theme. It's not at all unique.Dead boy is more light hearted
Lockwood focuses more on tense scenes and dread.Dead boy characters are more likeable. I really haven't grown to like any of the Lockwood main characters. And I find the acting in Lockwood can frequently be a bit stilted. Not terrible, but just enough to give the edge to Dead Boy on acting/directing. It's more fluid, and the characters that come across as stilted, feel purposefully directed that way as part of their character awkwardness. I also find Lockwood really stretches to justify doing the work at night when if all they have to do is locate the source, would be much more reasonable during the day.All in all, I dont really find these series similar at all other than the paranormal theme and trio of characters. And even then, there's massive differences.

title: Supernatural light
author: joecoop-91789
body: This is a solid show taking attributes from many other shows of a similar ilk, particularly supernatural with the loop episode etc and then Rowena turns up, despite this if you like this sort of thing it is relatively light hearted and good to watch and the female lead is excellent.The idea seem a bit muddled in the sense that it is dark in parts but then lightened by comedy or goofiness they could have potentially made it more scary and lore based and I think it would have been a beer watch as at the moment the first season appears to be driven towards teens and as a 40 year old supernatural fan there is definitely a gap in the market so I hope they can build on the first season !

title: Love love love love love!!
author: nielsennessalex
body: Beautiful writing, beautiful cinematography, beautiful character arcs, I mean what more could you want? Dead Boy Detectives is captivating, thrilling, emotional, funny, and everything else you could possibly want from a series. I'm on my third rewatch, and I'm yet to get bored of it. I'll steer clear of spoilers, but honestly every time I watch it I pick up on some new detail that I missed and it's so much fun. Easily my new favourite TV series. It would be a tragedy if it doesn't get renewed for a season two, so give it a watch! I can guarantee that there's something for everybody in this show and you wont be disappointed.

title: Could be better
author: FinleyKolapo
body: The dynamic between the two 'dead boys' is fun to watch. However, Crystal the psychic seems out of place. Her sudden integration into the group felt forced, and the first episode focuses so much on her that you'd think she founded the agency.Maybe it should be written better, because at first, I thought Crystal would be just a one-time character as a client. Then, out of nowhere, she suddenly becomes central (like, literally positioned at the center of the screen) in every scene.Fortunately, things improved in the second episode. I enjoyed every scene that actually focused on the 'detective' part. Crystal character also got better towards the end, so probably just the introduction that's not smooth enough.

title: This show has it all
author: isafee
body: THE BEST SHOW ON NETFLIX AT THE MOMENT. I loved Edwin from the very first minute, and I love Charles more every time I rewatch it, and I didn't think I could love either of them any more. And then there is Crystal Palace, who is an absolute icon, a queen, a legend. And to complete the lot there is Niko, who spreads joy wherever she goes. I could go on listing all the side characters, because they are all iconic, but that would take forever. Basically, this show is incredible, the story and the characters pull you in and it as the relationships deepen, so will your love for this show. The writing is good, the acting incredible, the music superb, the plot never slackens and there is never a dull moment. Do yourself a favour, just. Watch. It.

title: Real nice surprise to watch the whole season and enjoy it
author: Caspar1986
body: It delved straight into the supernatural and fantasy of the show in the first episode and it becomes a pleasure to meet the characters as the season develops and take interest in the storylines. It's easy to follow and the characters are very likeable and believable in their acting which is difficult to achieve with a supernatural element to the story. I didn't know what to think but now I'm hoping to get to watch a good few more seasons to see how the characters now carry the story on. Ruth Connell is an amazing actress, she played a great character in Supernatural and manages to carry on the excellence in this series again, she has so much expression in her roles it really lends itself to the shows.

title: Easy and fun but Lockwood and co. Was so much better
author: ppiwowarczyk-58587
body: The show itself is fun and easy, ridiculous (In a good way) but kinda cringe sometimes, and the main villain is cartoonishly evil.Show struggles with something I call "wannabe gen z dialogues and themes" that are kinda painful. But that's fine because it's still enjoyable. What I'm mad at is that Netflix already had great show with the same theme (Lockwood and co.) and they canceled it and created another production also based in uk? In fairness cg is way better in this show and it's quite obvious that it had bigger budget but Lockwood and co. Has better writing and characters are way more likable and less cartoonish. I'm still hoping they will renew it. Overall, it's fun but forgettable unfortunately.

title: Good concept but uninspired execution
author: mauramartindale
body: Neil Gaiman is more often a miss than a hit for me. I love his concepts, but more often than not I feel that he fails at the execution. That said though I was excited for this after having watched the trailer. On paper it is everything I love, but it wasn't executed well. It's so weirdly paced. It felt rushed in some aspects such Crystal joining them and getting to know them, and then dragged in others. The dialouge combined with the pacing of some scenes made conversations between characters really stilted and forced. It also bothered me that they didn't seem to trust the audience to connect the dots. We can see that their bag is a lot bigger on the inside than the outside (most of us have watched Harry Potter or Doctor who) it doesn't need to be explained 5 seconds later with really forced and unnatural dialouge. We can see that they are best friends and care deeply for each other, it doesn't have to be ruined by bad dialouge that explains it in a way people who have been friends for decades would never talk. The scene where one of them tells the medium is enough. This goes on and on which is a shame. Jayden Revri really stands out in his role, he's a very talanted actor. Kassius Nelsson's acting however leaves much to be desired. I thought Yuyu Kitamura was really fun in her role. George Rexstew is good, but I think he struggles at times but he has the hardest role to play. I really liked the dynamic between Charles and Edwin but that's about it. It just feels badly executed with poor writing for the most part. The mysteries the plot evolve around were really boring. I was on episode four when I realised that it wasn't going to get better in regards to that, it felt like a pilot episode. It felt uninspired. This is really a nitpick but I found it funny when the Crystal wants to rent a room and says she's 22 to which a woman replies there's no chance she older than 18 and then they have a closeup on the Crystal who looks much older than 22 and is in real life is 26. Genuine question, why couldn't they have changed it to them being in their 20s?

title: If you love fantasy just watch this!
author: millie-12909
body: It's amazing and so underrated. The characters, the storyline and everything is awesome. You can bond with all the characters easily. It's so amazing that made me write an IMDB review for the first time in my life. I'm waiting for the second season and hope that Netflix wouldn't cancel the show just like all the other amazing ones that they cancelled. And i would like to see the cast in more movies so they could succeed more and more because they definitely deserve it specially the actor who plays as Edwin Payne. I wanna see him more and more. And again I'm just saying this show is amazing just give it a chance!

title: light, fun popcorn entertainment - for the CW crowd
author: spasticfreakshow
body: For fantasy and sci-fi geeks, this one's a miss, unless...you're an actual child or adolescent. It is a bit campy, but there are better campy shows in the genre (Mysterious Benedict Society, Killjoys, Vagrant Queen) with better scripts, plots, character development, production values and better acting. That is to say, the characters on this show are attractive, better than Xena Warrior Princess actors, but worse than anything NOT on the CW - and the soapy vibe to the show is also very CW reminiscent. I, personally, like LGBT characters being naturally interspersed in a show, just like IRL, and I think reviewers deducting points for that are neither objective, nor reliable reviewers. That said, the characters themselves are all remarkably one-note; getting into bed with Berlanti was a strategic error on the part of Gaiman. Sandman was far better than this, and it feels like a waste of possibly good material. But if you are the type of person who loves everything on the CW and has no complaints about it (and you're a teen), you'll agree with the people giving this mediocrity ten stars. There are enough people with low expectations and lack of critical analysis that this should get a second season...so let's hope they hire FAR better writers for S2, and like other reviewers said, keep the boy detectives front and center.

title: It's decent enough
author: archanademonia
body: As a big fan of the Sandman show, I was intrigued to learn Dead Boy Detectives had dropped. To me it seems like a mix between a teen drama, Scooby Doo and Goosebumps. I am also getting some Good Omens tribute. However, each episode's story is interesting, the acting (which is decent) is a bit goofy and the vfx style is a bit retro which makes the show curiously fascinating. The teen drama is what throws me off a bit but I guess it is fitting considering the age of the main characters. I do wish the showrunnes would have tried to cater to an older age group as well, considering that the show belongs in the Sandman universe, because throughout season 1 I couldn't shake the feeling that the audience this was intended for are way way younger than me. I find the mix of gore and teen drama wildly confusing, but at the same time the show managed to keep me locked in. So the cons are the cringe moments, the overuse or words brills and aces, the absolutely creepy story involving the cat king and the weakest storyline and acting I've seen in a looong time regarding the demon David.

title: Absaloutely Amazing
author: ehayes-32846
body: This show is so charming and sweet.The pacing of it is perfect, it doesnt go too fast or too slow. All of the characters are interesting and likeable and it is all together very entertaining. The writing starts off a bit strange but it gets better almost immediately. Every single character shines through and stands out. My only complaint is how much they say 'tick', it's totally unessecary and so silly, like they probably say 'tick' about every five minutes but I'm pretty sure thats just something the charachters do because they do it in every single iteration. Overall I totally adore this show and so does everyone else I've spoken with who's wached it.

title: Watch Doom Patrol or Lockwood & Co instead
author: bird-81298
body: Love the comics; Neil Gaiman is an amazing author. Such a unique story. Love Doom Patrol; the show did the comics totally justice and made me so excited for this spinoff. Sadly, HBO kicked it to Netflix and this is what you get. This TV show is terrible. Only giving it over a five because the source material still gives me hope for it to be great. The casting is so off that it was painful to watch. Story lines are basic, effects are cliche at best, no chemistry with the cast and every scene feels like work. Please spend your time watching the Doom Patrol with the Dead Boy detectives, or watch Lockwood and Co.

title: Love it
author: darkhrse-40372
body: All of the characters are so fun. You can't help but like them all in some way, even the villans. The actors all do such an amazing job, and every time you watch it you notice some new facet of it. LGBTQIA+ characters and relationships are treated casually and there's not this assumption of heteronormativity that you usually get in other shows. The mysteries are engaging and make sense, and they have you trying to figure them out alongside the dead boy detectives. The overarching storyline is excellently done. All of the characters are strange in their own way, and endlessly endearing. I am desperately waiting for a renewal of this show. It handles topics like repression and abuse well, without sounding like something out of a therapy book. I am completely obsessed with this show.

title: Light fun. But plot holes everywhere.
author: alannahfayemagick
body: Good and light fun, easy to watch. Just don't focus on the plot too much. Haha. Eg. Iron is bad, but they can hold a crow bar? Ghosts can handle real books but others don't see the book floating? Ghosts can walk through walls but help you up hand in hand? Hahahaha. All in all its fun and easy. The main character is a little hard to swallow. The way he's written is uptight and team too much, and it took us a few eps to get over him. Not sure if it's the acting, the writing, the speed he speaks, not sure what it is? But again. The story is fast, fun and the show is easy to watch and has some fun characters in new roles.

title: Just wow
author: Bld4310
body: I absolutely love the show! I watched the whole thing in a day, and I just can't even begin to say how much the show rocks. The casting is amazing, I would love to see these actors in more things! The lines are perfect the writing the scripts the producing like it's all just so Great. We needed something new and different and this is exactly what we needed. So many new Movies with the stars we're used to, But scripts are written terribly and production is terrible. But this show really loud me and I wish there was more episodes and many more seasons and I hope there are going to be. I loved the plot as well. Give it a try!

title: The best show of 2024
author: bogwood-49241
body:
This show did not deserve cancellation. Heartwarming, inclusive, magical, fantastically written and acted. I hope the petition and campaign that are going around to save it are successful as this show has so much world building and potential.Jayden Revri and George Rexstrew do an amazing job portraying their characters, with great humour and also depth of emotion when required. The rest of the cast also do a phenomenal job, and the chemistry between all of them is greatly enjoyable. It is no suprise Season 1 was met with critical acclaim and remained in the Top 10 for weeks.#savedeadboydetectives
#renewdeadboy detectives.

title: its ok ,if theres nothing else to watch!
author: stuwright05
body: Its ok , quirky i suppose, but hmm just so many ideas from other shows, such as harry potter or fringe, and the lead actors, aren't standing out much , it has some good moments but its definitely a teen show. Someone else said its not funny, but i disagree it does have its humorous moments in my opinion, i just think its a bit cheap at times and repetitive, but it has its moments and I honestly I had fun watching some of it.Crystal and the witch are the best characters, I suppose it reminds me of lost girl, but with more special effects, crystals cute, and that helps lol. It turns out she used to be on hollyoaks, I had no idea...

title: Loved It!
author: bbbr-82954
body: I can't get enough of this show. I have watched it over and over again. Great characters, a great story, fast paced, nail bitting, keeping on my toes and not boring at all. It leaves you wanting more, like a good book you can't put down. Each character has great growth. I love the stories from the different realms. It is a wonderful way to keep the story interesting and intriguing. I am so excited for season 2. I hope they announce it soon. Jenny is such a fascinating character, I hope she shows up in season 2. Love, love, love that Ruth Connel was casted for this she is such a unique, powerful actress.

title: Great characters, story, plotlines...why so dark (cinematically)?
author: bretthiett6
body: Love this show....but I can't see much. I thought TV was a visual medium. I would like to see what's going on. There is something "new" in direction that is making stuff dark...I guess "more natural". I don't care. If I'm going to WATCH a show/movie, I would like to SEE what's going on. Faces, expressions, actions... This has been a trend as of late seemingly starting with Game of Thrones last season and continuing with many other shows (Willow, for one). The characters are great, realistic (I think that's why Ghostbusters 84 was so good, the characters were real, not like the McCarthy Ghostbusters). The storylines are really expansive, more than the ghosts...Gaiman's stories are well done and nonlinear. Again, why so dark? Stop it with "this is how it would really look!" I'm watching a show TO SEE IT! Otherwise, it's a 10. Put up some fake light somewhere!

title: New and fun to watch
author: missyhummer
body: We enjoy that it is something different and fun to watch. We are looking forward to upcoming seasons.The characters have unique personalities and are fairly well developed.We don't have a lot of time for watching TV, but when we came across The Dead BOY Detectives we were intrigued and before we knew it we had binged watch the entire first season. This is definitely something we can watch and enjoy together.We are hoping for several more seasons and the expansion of each character, especially Niko, as well as the introduction of new ones.We also enjoy Ruth Connell as the Night Nurse, she is the perfect actress for this character.

title: Creepy but yet fun
author: lakings97
body: Dead Boy Detectives is a Netflix series based on DC universe characters Charles Rowland and Edwin Paine. George Rexstrew and Jayden Revri are the actors representing these lovable characters. The story follows these two boys who were killed and their murders went unsolved. The boys instead of moving on to afterlife, they decide to stay on Earth and solve cases that involve the supernatural. The series felt like a CW show filled with characters that pertain towards the Gen Z kids. The initial episode takes place in London and thinking it was a good start but then it moves to a small town in America. Charles and Edwin help Crystal (Kassius Nelson) and winds up using her psychic powers to help the boys with their cases. Yusu Kitamura played Niko who also adds another dimension to the group. Jenn Lyon played the antagonist witch where she kidnaps kids to use their blood to be able to stay young much like the witch from Disney's Sleeping Beauty. Michael Beach is the only known veteran actor on the show who played a walrus that choose to be a human instead of being with his own kind. Andi Armagarian and Amanda Tapping were the directors of a few episodes. Overall the series felt like I was watching Supernatural, I was hoping for something better but felt this series was just checking off boxes as the series was developing. It had a good start and it was fun, but it could have been better if they had just stuck with the boys instead of adding weirdly odd gay characters.

title: New favorite show 100%
author: kelliesecond
body: I love this show SO MUCH!!While I'm incredibly disappointed in Netflix for not giving this show the proper promotion it deserves (I'm not shocked, they do this way too often) , I will say that I'm still incredibly pleased I stumbled upon this show on my own!It has so much heart, serious topics aren't handled with kid gloves but instead with a deep understanding and an air of empathy. The characters all have so much depth and the story lines leave nothing to be desired!Netflix has popped out a series of iffy shows over the years but this is certainly not one of them. I've put everyone I can onto this show and they've all loved it.We're all hoping for a season 2.

title: Who is it for?
author: wbrqq
body: Well, this is infuriating. We really need to get rid of the trope of characters being complete dicks to people just because they're smart. There's too many people around already who think they can treat people badly just because they have a skill or money or brains. And the main character here is just the worst. No redeeming features and, as far as I can tell, not even a particularly good detective.And for a show that seems to be pitched at 13 year olds, why is it so full of mostly unnecessary swearing? Anyway, here we have a badly written version of Lockwood & Co where all the characters run around shouting at each other, cases are solved incredibly easily and every shot has a weird fuzzy vignette applied. I'm a fan of Neil Gaiman, but this sucks. Dreadful.

title: Make season 2
author: nanninannu
body: I swear if Netflix doesn't make season 2 I am officially giving up on that platform. This is such a good tv show!!! And amazing lgbtq+ representation with good slow burn and characters and stories!!!If someone is looking to watch more lgbtq+ tv shows, this is definitely something to check out. We need more lgbtq+ tv shows (and movies but in this case shows) and having more like this makes me happy that times are changing. I hope they renew it and make another season, it deserves proper closure! And maybe even fan service and give the fans what they want and obviously they want Edwin and Charles. (So I hope in season 2 they add that because who knows if we're going to get a season 3, with how shady Netflix is, they always like to cancel shows at season 2 🙄) but for now hopefully we do get a season two, I need to know more!

title: This is my favorite show right now!!
author: zelpdx
body: I love this show and I'm going to be so sad if there's not a season 2. The show is really character driven and every character is interesting. I relate the most to Niko because she's silly and does her own thing. Even antagonistic characters are hard not to like a little bit. Esther is so funny, every character is so funny. There's so many sweet and sincere moments between characters but there's also a lot of really good comedy. I'm currently on my third rewatch and I've been recommending it to all my friends. I'm so excited to see where the show goes from here. Thanks mom for introducing this show to me!!

title: Brilliant show!
author: justwright-35606
body: I'm only on episode 2 of this show but I love everything about it! It's well written with very funny dialogue, but its greatest strength lies with the performances! There are a lot of quirky traits, funny one liners, and plenty of excellent interactions. The entire cast is fantastic, but a stand out is Yuyu Kitamura as Niko! She usually gets a random line that brings belly laughs to scenes. She plays the part to perfection!If I had to pick one thing I don't like about this show, it's that it takes place in Port Townsend yet was quite obviously not filmed there. I've been to Port Townsend and it's actually one of my favorite places on earth. I was excited when the show told us that's where the main characters were headed. Sadly, this was obviously filmed in Canada and I can't fault them for doing this. It's cheaper to film in Canada but try to make it look like Washington State.Still, I feel robbed that two gorgeous dead guys never actually made it to the state where I live!!

title: 2 SEASON PLS!!
author: whitellswa
body: I'm incredibly grateful to TikTok for bringing this amazing show into my life. It's been a long time since I've found a show where I love absolutely every character. The cast is incredible, everyone is so charismatic and does a fantastic job with their roles.Edwin stole my heart from the very first episode. Oh my god, his outfit is just something else, so gorgeous. Charles also won me over completely. Nico is my favorite girl, she's so positive, bright, and inspiring, a truly memorable character. All the little creatures (cats and dandelion elves) are so funny and add so much to the show.The best!(I'll be happy with whoever the main character ends up with because I like both pairings.)

title: Sooo Goood! Highly Recommend!
author: katharinasimon
body: I'm not exaggerating when I say that Dead Boy Detectives is the best thing I've seen in years! I truly haven't been this obsessed with anything in a long while.It's a huge recommendation for anyone that likes supernatural stories, found family, a diverse set of likeable three-dimensional characters with a beautiful friendship dynamic and also positive queer representation, that's neither overbaring nor only there as a token.Dead Boy Detectives deals with dark themes and big emotions in a very kind and effective way, never coming across as tasteless. It keeps a comfortable balance between humour, gruesome realities and so much love - both platonically and romatically.Structurally, the show consists of entertaining supernatural detective cases - one for each episode - tied together nicely by an overarching plot of defying what is expected of one for the sake of friendship and doing good.The dialogue is fun and written in a way that it's not constantly and blatantly obvious that it was in fact written - something not every show pulls off these days! Many of the characters have their own unique way of speaking that is fun to listen to and adds to make them feel real from the start.Speaking of characters, all the major and minor characters are fun to watch. Even the antagonists are easy to love (or love to hate) due to a mixture of great costume design, witty dialogue, stunning acting performances and in some cases interesting redemption arcs.What the show admittedly lacks on rare occasions with unconvincing green screen usage, it makes up for with impressive and very much convincing practical effects on many more occasions.There really is no going wrong in checking this beautifully made show out. Who knows, you might just fall in love with it! I certainly have!

title: An Engaging Mystery with Supernatural Touches
author: gabrieledasilva-81636
body: Dead Boy Detectives is a series that masterfully blends the supernatural with mystery in an intriguing way. Based on the DC Comics characters created by Neil Gaiman, the show presents a captivating narrative that hooks viewers from the first episode.The strongest aspect of the series is, without a doubt, the charisma of the protagonists. The young, dead detectives, Charles Rowland and Edwin Paine, are complex characters who, despite their tragic circumstances, maintain a sharp sense of humor and an endearing camaraderie. The chemistry between the two actors is palpable, and the development of their personal journeys, both in relation to the world of the living and the dead, is one of the most engaging elements of the plot.In addition to the protagonists, the series stands out for its atmosphere. The gothic and eerie setting perfectly aligns with the tone of the story, creating a constant sense of mystery. The visual aesthetic is rich and detailed, with settings that seem to have stepped right out of a nightmare, adding immensely to the immersion in the universe.The plot moves at a brisk pace, skillfully balancing the mysteries being investigated with character development. The show explores themes such as loss, regret, and redemption without ever losing the supernatural detective rhythm. The blend of dark humor, light horror, and a good dose of emotion makes each episode a unique experience.If you're a fan of dark stories with a touch of mystery and detectives, Dead Boy Detectives is a must-watch. Full of twists, scares, and memorable characters, this series delivers much more than just a simple detective adventure.

title: Save Dead Boy Detectives
author: tvwilsontv
body: I absolutely loved this show. It's a great balance between quirky, queer, and mysterious along with having amazing emotional moments. As a queer person, I really enjoyed the fact that the queerness of the show was there but it's not all in your face but it's still important. Netflix loves to take amazing shows with queer characters and cancel them after one season unless it breaks records. I'm sick and tired of falling in love with a show only for it to be canceled with an ending that either has a cliff hanger or could go ANYWHERE. The ending in Dead Boy Detectives season 1 was so wide, I need to know what happens next. Please uncancel it Netflix.

title: A great show, poorly advertised
author: annekh88
body: I stumbled on this show entirely by accident, having not seen any marketing for it at all. Which is a shame because it's a great show.The acting is first-class - a rewatch had me noticing small nuances I missed the first time round. The plot doesn't drag, it has a slight element of 'monster of the week' keeping it fresh though there is an overarching plot. Even costume and set design are amazing.Even though it's a Sandman spin-off, it's entirely it's own beast and I know nothing about the Sandman yet still followed everything in this show. Perhaps if you watched the other show you'll pick up on additional things but it's definitely nit a requirement.A fun show, with great acting that deserved more promotion than it got.

title: Another YA Supernatural Misfire
author: johnspringer-95440
body: It has paper-thin characters, rushed character development, repetitive expositional dialogue, inconsistent world-building, and lame supernatural dangers. The "cases" the titular characters take on are simplistic and easily-resolved. It seems like the series is for a young teenage audience but it also has elements that are inappropriate for that demographic like repeated f-bombs and a simulated orgy scene. The performers are apparently trying to be whimsical and kinetic most of the time. None of them have the chops to pull it off and they just come across as cloying, obnoxious and goofy. Their general hyperactive quippiness also undercuts the show's few attempts at genuine pathos.

title: A fun supernatural show
author: paynefretwell
body: I really enjoyed this show and I wish it hadn't been canceled. It's nice having something you can enjoy and not have to think too hard about.Dead Boy Detectives has a monster of the week format with some long-term questions and mysteries. Great side characters really fill out the cast and the two leads are so engaging that you can easily forget they're dead.I really hope Netflix changes their mind and gives this show another shot. Lack of advertising led to low early viewership. The show needed more time to build its audience by word of mouth. It's way too easy for shows to get dropped without ever having a chance to reach their intended audience.

title: Fun and entertaining!
author: tvsafnari
body: This show is exactly as it sounds, fun and a bit corny. After being bombarded with far too many scifi/fantasy shows that are unnecessarily depressing and take themselves way too seriously, I am very thankful to have found this show.First and foremost, this show is fun. It's relatively fast paced and never gets boring. The cast of characters is very well rounded, and each has their own dynamic personality. The writing is quite good I must say, everything flows naturally without being forced, while both taking care of the character development and storyline.On the weaker points of this show... the acting is not going to win anyone an oscar to be honest, but they still do manage to create interesting captivating characters. The visual effects are okayish, but there are definitely other shows that do that part better. Then it can definitely be argued that the show is corny, but to me personally that is honestly a positive trait, because the show doesn't take itself too seriously, and embraces it own corniness in an endearing way. But if "corny" is your kryptonite, you should probably stay as far away from this show as possible.But if you are just looking for some fun, and are not taking everything too seriously, I can strongly recommend this show. At the end of the day, it just works. The combination of story, atmosphere, setting and characters all complement each other to create a world that is entertaining for the viewers.The characters are quite diverse, and all - including the female characters - are treated as whole people. Which is very refreshing to watch.Most of all, this show has a lot of potential. For the younger actors to gain experience and grow into the characters, and for the worldbuilding to expand and become even richer. There is lots of room for more stories to be told.My only real regret about this show is that there weren't more episodes, and I truly and sincerely hope that they will get a second season, since this is one of the most fun shows to come on Netflix in a while.

title: Brilliant, funny, and heartfelt
author: ashlyraiti
body: I had no idea what to expect going into this show, and I was absolutely blown away.The writing, acting, set design, and attention to detail are all absolutely brilliant. The emotional character arcs are heartfelt and touching, and at the end of the season you're left with a satisfying conclusion while still desperately wanting to see more. I needed an immediate rewatch, and I wasn't disappointed. The second playthrough lets you pick up details in the script and setting that lay the path for a carefully constructed narrative.The cast has incredible chemistry. You absolutely believe that the leads have known and had each other's backs for decades, and all of the characters are so richly realized and funny and charming and earnest that I could watch another five seasons of this, easily.This is probably the best show Netflix has ever put out.

title: Need a second season - captivating!
author: hazzy-67961
body: The acting and storytelling in this short season is incredible.The chemistry between the 2 lead characters is flawless but also every other character is well written and comes across as a complete and rounded person. The women especially are unique in being allowed to be messy and complicated and fierce, unapologetically.The cinematography is beautiful as is the sound track, it creates a really wonderful atmosphere for the show.Each episode has its own contained storyline which still fits wonderfully into the overall narrative. There is a strong supernatual/horror aspect but (as someone who is a massive wimp) I didn't find it too overwhelming.It gives strong supernatural vibes (but make it modern and less afraid to be gay).Representation is wonderful hear and just understated and inclusive, as it should be.This is aimed at a YA audience but as someone rather older than that I still found there was lots to relate to and it is the most enjoyable show I have watched in a long time.I really hope it gets picked up somewhere for a much needed second season (and more!)

title: No Sovl
author: drael64
body: I wanted to like this, and I didn't even really have high expectations. It follows a relatively modern formulae of 'quirky' but trope heavy characters experiencing 'quirky' supernatural challenges. The plot isn't terribly interesting, the characters aren't particularly relateable or compelling, a lot of choices in show seem orientated around progressive message fiction (ie conveying certain popular moral messaging), rather being for any genuine creative reason. It's not terribly subtle and tbh, this sort of writing is not only generally just bad writing (which this absolutely typifies), but it also fails at it's purpose - a good moral story takes the viewer on a journey from point a to point b. A bad moral story just presents some things as right or wrong and in the process convinces nobody.In short, this show lacks soul. It lacks anything creative, interesting, compelling or human. It's not funny, exciting, mysterious or charming. And even that would be okay, if it was moderately entertaining, which even a commodity TV series with a low bugget, it fails to acheive. Do not, at all recommend - and if you don't believe me, look at how few people have even rated this show - no one even knows it exists, and that's for a reason.

title: Superb show
author: photarlight
body: Fun, witty and moving show about two English ghostly teens (one Edwardian, one from the 80s) who use the time they have to solve the mysteries other ghosts bring to them. When the case of a living medium crosses their desk the trajectory of their afterlives change forever.This show revels in clever details and gives more on a rewatch. It approaches its characters with sensitivity and explores their regrets and traumas wisely.It's not a dreary show, though. There is a lot of humour and heart. The friendships are fleshed out and delightful, the characters all have depth and dimension. It's easily one of the best-written shows I have seen in years. I maintain hope for further seasons because BOY could this be a classic if it is allowed to be.

title: Brilliant! You won't be disappointed... Netflix, get on with renewing this!
author: idkhow-76954
body: I'm not great at writing reviews, so I'll try to keep this brief. (Me, after finishing this review: well, that was a lie...)Dead Boy Detectives is an incredibly creative Sci-Fi/Fantasy show that deserves so much more love than it's getting. Although it is based on a series of comics by Neil Gaiman (I believe? I haven't yet read them), from what I've heard, it takes some departures from these and does very well for it. Creator Steve Yockey should be incredibly proud of what he's accomplished here, alongside all the other writers, directors and cast members.Moving into its incredibly diverse cast of characters, George Rexstrew and Jayden Revri put in brilliant, heartfelt performances as the titular Dead Boy Detectives, Edwin and Charles respectively. The core cast of four, filled out by Kassius Nelson as amnesiac psychic Crystal and Yuyu Kitamura as the charming Anime nerd Niko, are all incredibly charismatic and likeable, while also being flawed, realistic characters who grow as the series goes on.The writing and direction deserve a special mention as well. The story is engaging and leaves you wanting more, while the cinematography and costume/scenery design are so good I was constantly pausing to take screenshots. (And, as an aside, the sheer amount of queer representation in this is staggering, and frankly wonderful. Considering what the current climate is like for queer people today, this type of casual representation is very important, and I commend the show for this.)Ultimately, this is the kind of show Netflix should be looking to make more of. I am always a little scared when Netflix has the rights to a brilliant show, as they seem to never quite make the right decision on whether to renew (especially when talking about shows with lots of queer characters, like First Kill, The Midnight Club or Julie and the Phantoms.)Congrats to everyone who worked on Dead Boy Detectives, I'm sure there are plenty of awards and much love coming your way!

title: This show needs more promotion.
author: AJsok2003
body: I loved this show but it sucks to know that I barely knew about it less than 5 months ago when the teaser trailer came out on youtube. I hope this show will get more steam and hope people will want to watch it. Because I thought it was scary and funny at the same time. Neil Gaiman and Netflix make a great team. The humor and the music in this show really made a true show.I also did not realize that the actress from another paranormal show called Supernatural was it this show. It was good to see Ruth Connell in this show. I thought her character was a clever one. She played it so well.I hope this show gets another season because it was spooky and funny at the same time. And I loved the music also.

title: Brills! Need another season
author: fallingshadows
body: I really liked this show. It did such a great job of mixing supernatural with comedy, which is so hard to do. There was a theme of growth, strength in community, and self-forgiveness while being light hearted, fun, and funny. It was cinematically well put together, it was cute but not cheesy, and I loved the characters. The main characters, but also the supporting ones... The cats (!), the profane little sprites, Kashina, Angie, the Mick 💜.I really wish there was going to be another season. There is so much potential in the story left, and it was clearly strength to go on. I think it would be one of those shows that gains traction with the "masses" as it goes on.I wish I'd watched it sooner, maybe there be another season if more people watched it sooner. But probably not. So often when I like a show they don't renew it, no matter how fast I get to it.

title: Best Netflix show in years
author: asidianmorris
body: This show is funny, quirky, creepy, and unapologetically queer. Its brilliant writing and the main cast's incredible acting make it impossible to put down once you start it. You'll come back for a rewatch to appreciate the tight foreshadowing in both the script and the setting on the second time around.The monsters are endearingly campy, because this show knows what its real monsters are: facing abuse, cruelty, neglect, and struggling to be your best self despite unfair, often painful circumstances.The devotion the characters show for one another is touching and rare to see on screen, and the irreverent, delightful chaos of the pacing makes the absolute most of the eight episode format so that nothing is wasted.I absolutely fell in love with this heartfelt, earnest gem of a show.

title: Sigh
author: notwist
body: What could have been a decent spin-off from the Sandman universe ends up only keeping the worst parts. In typical Netflix fashion it's turned an interesting brand into a teenage coming of age-drama where everybody's gay for some reason.Every single main character is as physically attractive as they are vapid and utterly boring, and the only thing you need to compare to understand that Netflix has utterly violated yet another IP is to compare the cover art of the TV series to that of "The Children's Crusade". London is immediately replaced with the US for no reason other than pandering to an American audience, doom and gloom is replaced with a graphical profile reminiscent of "Stranger Things" since it's the only series Netflix has widely succeeded with, and somewhere along the way all creativity bleeds out, the idea dies and you spend a season watching a corpse of an idea -- or perhaps more accurately a ghost.

title: Beautiful inside and out, adducting to watch and owns my entire heart!
author: istarmaria
body: This show is wonderfully written, wonderfully acted and full of beautiful cinematography.The characters are full of personality and charm, delightful and easily lovable. The relationships between the characters are undoubtedly the focal point of the show, and the actors were truly made to bring them to live!Behind the fun and happy exterior that this show presents at first, hides deep emotion and a serious love for human relationships. Platonic love and romantic love given equal weight in this world, and I could not be happier.Have not stopped watching this show since it came out, and I am still desperately hoping for a second season. I have never felt as represented on screen as with this show.I recommend everyone to watch this! Bring snacks, time and fun, and maybe a few friends with you!

title: Campy, Queer, Delightfully Unexpected
author: pamela-rehn
body: I never leave reviews, but I created an IMDB account just to talk about this show: that should tell you how gobsmacked I was by it! As a lover of all things weird, whimsical, and supernatural I've been disheartened in recent years - nothing has quite filled the void shows like Charmed and Buffy the Vampire Slayer left in the genre... until Dead Boy Detectives.Dead Boy Detectives is, without a doubt, one of the best shows of 2024.I went into it with reservations, not wanting to get my hopes up, and I had no expectations for what to expect as I'd never read the source material. It took no more than 15 minutes before I realized I was enthralled; I watched the entire series in one night, and then have watched it an unfathomable amount of times since.I rated it a 10 because there's simply nothing like it on any platform right now. It's brilliant, gripping, hilarious in a way that feels authentic. So many "edgy" shows in the last few years suffer from stilted dialogue that tries to be funny, "hip," and youthful, but it always feels forced in a way that borders icky or cringe-inducing (Riverdale is a perfect example of this). The Dead Boy Detectives writing team struck a perfect balance, and the show never comes off like it's trying too hard.You will laugh, you will cry, and you will have a good time from beginning to end. The protagnoists are flawed and complex, but extremely lovable and you'll root for them with ease. The main boys, "Best mates" and business partners Charles Rowland and Edwin Payne, have an effortless chemistry that will pull at your heartstrings and endear you to no end. The antagonists are delightful and even when you hate what they're doing you love to watch them do it. If you love a good villain, Dead Boy Detectives delivers over and over again.For a first season, I was blown away at how quickly it found its footing and how easily its characters pulled me in. It's a little exposition heavy in the beginning, but that's the only negative thing I can even think to say (and, if I'm being honest, I found the exposition to be helpful in establishing the rules of their universe).All this to say, this show is special. It's charming, weird, and full of heart. You can tell that every person who worked on this project loved what they were doing and cared about the details.Dead Boy Detectives is a diamond in the rough; I will be singing its praises to anyone who will listen for years to come. If you are looking for a supernatural drama that is a little spooky, very magical, and filled to the brim with themes of shame, facing past traumas, found family, self-acceptance, love in all its many forms, and loss... this show is for you. It genuinely, truly, has it all.

title: Beautiful, heartwarming LGBTQ+ quirky horror.
author: sarajfletcher-53478
body: Dead Boy Detectives stole my heart, cementing itself as one of my favourite shows. And I've watched a lot of TV in my time. It reminded me a lot of Buffy, which is another favourite of mine.The story combines creepiness and fun in a spectacular way, combining it with excellent writing and perfect acting. Jayden Revri and George Rextrew are phenomenal in the title roles, with Kassius Nelson and Yuyu Kitamura making up the core four.At its heart though, the story is about acceptance, friendship and found family, and those are the elements that made it win my heart. I love this show and hold out hope that it will beat the odds and get uncancelled. It did not deserve it's fate.

title: Powerful
author: natecurrier
body: Quite the devastating story. Probably the most heart wrenching piece of "entertainment" I've ever seen was episode #6. The younger Price sisters are amazingly well portrayed by 2 actresses I had never heard of (Lola Petticrew and Hazel Doupe). Hope to see them get more mainstream roles going forward. Anthony Boyle also jumped off the screen in every scene he was in. The show couldn't have been cast any better.I was only vaguely familiar with this story and haven't read the book, so I can't speak to the shows accuracy, but I can say the dialogue is well written and the directors did a fantastic job.Would absolutely recommend watching this show. Although, I wouldn't suggest watching it in 1 day like I did as you'll lose some sleep.

title: A good watch but an extremely one sided narrative
author: deriece95
body: I'll start by saying that the production of this series is excellent, the acting is great, and the overall story is gripping. As someone from Northern Ireland it's always great to see anything from here portrayed in T. V or film, but there is usually a sense that it's a "B rate" production at best. I am thrilled to say that is not the case with 'Say Nothing', this series was so we'll done that I imagine it will be viewed and praised by people the world over. Things like this are usually only interesting to people from the island, people that were directly involved, or history buffs. But I think this will appeal to a broader audience as it is portrayed as a drama series with characters at it's heart.I can't tell you how many times I have been watching something and have heard the Nortern Ireland accent butchered to the point where I cringe. I have always thought to myself 'if only we had some top actors (that aren't Liam Neeson) who could star in these roles'. We'll im not sure where they've been hiding, but they finally found them! The acting was excellent throughout the entire show, and it's great to see some home grown talent getting some much needed and deserved recognition. I was unfamiliar with most of the cast in this show, but if at least one or two don't go on to be house hold names in the UK I will be surprised (particularly the actors who played the Price sisters).I haven't read the book, though I would imagine it's more historical and focused on the facts of what happened during the troubles. The show definitely keeps this in mind the historical and cultural impact throughout, although it is mostly character driven. It does a great job of developing the characters and portraying all sides of characters involved and showing a multitude of emotions for people we'd probably rather see as one dimensional in real life.My only reservation with this show is that I felt the narrative of the troubles was slightly one sided. The focus is of course on the IRA/ republican movement, as such, it's no real surprise that they are viewed as the protagonist. However, there are two sides to the story with the Belfast conflict and it feels as thought the protestant/ unionist side was left out completely.That being said, I think they done a good job of showing how nasty things got and how the lines got blurred between what is right and wrong, even in war times and even when you are convinced that the only right opinion is yours.I expect this will be a hard watch for many people, especially those directly effected and those who may still be grieving the loss of loved ones. My hope is that people can enjoy it for what it is, an excellent piece of television on a topic that most of the world may have forgotten or never even heard of, and I hope prejudice doesn't get in the way of enjoying a good show.

title: Powerful and Fast moving !
author: kelly_john
body: This series asks the difficult question, if the State discriminates against you, and you use non violence to seek justice. But are met with violence, is the use of counter violence justified. The fact that the story allows us to see the view point of all players adds to the depth of this issue. Traces the evolution of the recent conflict in Northern Ireland through the the lives of two sisters. Fast moving and beautifully filmed and directed. Powerful acting by both make and female leads, especially the two sisters. This series is a must see for anyone with an interest in the 30 yr conflict in Northern Ireland.

title: Extremely good
author: tsmrm02
body: As someone from the north, it's very surreal to see such a high quality TV series about this period. The series clearly attempts to provide balance when looking at this period. Obviously the main focus towards the end is the disappeared, particularly Jean McConville and a few ex IRA volunteers, but it does an excellent job in portraying the motivations and circumstances of those who got involved with the IRA. The characters on all sides are developed and acted brilliantly, particularly Dolours Price and Brendan Hughes, and the odd bout of humour is very welcome and lands well. Overall this is a sometimes exhilarating but also thought provoking watch, I certainly felt it was worth taking a day out to watch!

title: Demonstrates the futility of oppression and the trauma of resistence
author: tleaf-00150
body: The book Say Nothing is an excellent and evenhanded examination of the Cause and what it cost. The series follows the book very closely and communicates the major themes and and the tragic lessons of that brutal period of the occupation. The show is art dully done and well crafted. The acting and casting choices captures the essence of the people the show is about. It manages to inform as well as entertain and tells a story that has been seldom told.The details of the people and the places is fantastic. One can marvel over the production values of every episode and historicity of the production. Little things like a brand of cigarettes or the way one is served take away fish and chips combined with a certain character grabbing an Armalite AR18 was a really nice touch.The real Dolours Price was known to be funny and charming and that shines through. She proves to be very likable. Many of the characters are very likeable, even the ones you feel you shouldn't.Its a very human story humanely told. It helps one outside the co flict understand the motivations of why someone would take up arms against another. It wasn't really about catholics vs protestant. That was just rhe arbitrary line that was drawn to divide the working class and working poor people of Ireland and pit them against each other.Also, there was a comment from another review about immigrants invading Ireland. There were immigrants who fought for a free and united Ireland. It was never about how your last name was spelt or which church to prayed at. It was about poor people fighting for equal rights and to be free and that's what this story is about and the price that is paid for that struggle. To compare an influx of immigrants from troubled lands to the Oliver Cromwell is to dishonor the names of those who suffered and sacrificed. The moment we turn on those seeking refuge or deny them comfort, we would be no better than those who sneered and jeered at our ancestors who left Ireland and went to other countries like America where Irish weren't all thay welcome either.

title: Well done series on a very troubling topic
author: bentaylorsimpson
body:
I highly suggest reading the book for additional context/info, but the series does a fantastic job covering the material.Really well-acted across the multiple age eras of the principal characters.The larger themes to me are:
-in war, everyone thinks they are on the right side
-how far will you go for a cause you believe in, and what happens when that belief is tested or wanes
-the sacrificial pawns of war who carry the most risk typically are easily discarded in the end
-the larger "code" of silence within communities goes too far sometimes
-the spoils of war tend to go to the bureaucrats, not the soldiersOverall an incredibly well-done miniseries.

title: Probably the best Drama Series on the Troubles
author: mwpmcxh
body: The casting is absolutely spot on. The main players, Gerry Adam's, Brendan Hughes and Dolours Price were cast absolutely perfectly. You'd swear you were actually there reliving History. It's gritty, it's exciting and they have Belfast of the 1970's to a tee.. You'd honestly think you were watching a documentary is that well shot.. I'm only a few episodes in but so far it's edge of your seat stuff..So far they have done a good job of showing two sides of the story and they didn't shy away from showing how the troubles started. The Protestant/Loyalist Population with the help of the Police beating and burning the Catholics out of their homes..

title: Very painful but a must see
author: dadi-bh12
body: It's not often that I write a review but this series it's extremely well done and moving.It narrates real events that took place in northern Ireland between 1971 to recent years, including the bombing of the old Bailey in London.The fact that it's not fiction it makes it a lot more interesting to watch. It's very raw, and at times very painful to watch. Rightly or wrongly, It was incredible for me to see the conviction of some of the IRA members, especially the two sisters, and what they were prepared to do for the cause of a unified Ireland.I think everyone should be watching it to remember and not forget this tragic contemporary history.

title: A Masterpiece!
author: mncmphcys
body: This is possibly the best piece of media I have ever seen! It is a masterpiece of storytelling and directing with the character development superbly crafted and depicted. Growing up in Northern Ireland during the 'Troubles' I can testify that the imagery, brutality and pain are all very real. The acting is excellent and the director should be given full credit for turning an incredible story book into a cinematic masterpiece! I would give this six stars if I could. It ranks with Breaking Bad and The Shawshank Redemption.It brought me to tears, several times and at its conclusion I had to leave my house around midnight and drive around the city, just to wind down from its emotional impact. It really is a must see!

title: Feminists save the men of the IRA
author: rochfordsimon
body: A very well produced series for the FX Network in America and distributed internationally.It is emotional and pulls on the heart strings. Which is a great core value for a drama. Flows along nicely and detailed.Women have been a part of the freedom fight for centuries. They fought and died in many battles directly or indirectly. Women were always a part of the IRAThis show makes out that 2 young, strong and intelligent women educated the IRA and changed it forever. While a true story, it has a modern day agenda attached to it. As seen in 90% of TV shows these days.The ugliness of all sides is shown and touched on. That's something realistic and truthful in this show.Well worth watching.

title: Amazing depiction of the war.
author: holohanmartin
body: This is one amazing piece of TV.It chronicles a very difficult period in Irish history and shows its characters (and therefore true history) warts and all. Dolours and Marion show in graphic detail the old adage "Nature vs Nurture". They were born into a republican activist/volunteer family and they became exactly that. The undeniable and unenviable truth is that all politics is born of war and this is something Irish people should remember. The so called legitimate parties in Irish politics are no better & most definitely not any different than Sinn Féin, they just have better spin doctors.

title: Best TV mini-series of the year, period
author: paul-allaer
body: As Episode 1 of "Say Nothing" (2024 release from the UK; 9 episodes ranging from 41 to 50 min each) opens, it is "Belfast 1972" and we are reminded that this is "Based on a True Story". A woman is being taken away from her house, leaving her kids behind. We don't know why or who took her. We then go to "Dublin, Ireland, 29 Years Later" and we meet. Dolours Price. She is about to be interviewed as part of an oral history of the Troubles. At this point we are 10 minutes into Episode 1.Couple of comments: there have been many movies and TV series and documentaries about the Troubles before, but I don't recall ever having seen anything like "Say Nothing", which brings the 3 decades that were the Troubles with a fresh look. The series follows several events and jumps back and forth in time, but somehow it brings the main themes of the Troubles with a clearer perspective than ever. While the differences and the fighting fighting between the Protestants/British Army versus the Catholics/Irish-minded gets of course plenty of attention, less obvious issues such as the Disappeared by the IRA are also included. There are plenty of solid acting performances, none more so than Lola Petticrew as Dolours. Beware: this mini-series is not for the faint of heart. At the end of it all, I felt like I had received an emotional gut punch. This mini-series is riveting from start to finish, even if some moments are uncomfortable. (As an aside, within minutes of watching Episode 1, I realized that I needed English subtitles, as I was missing about half of what I was hearing (Northern Ireland accents and all...)"Say Nothing" started streaming on Hulu a week ago. I read a positive review of it in the New York Times, and then I found out that it is currently rated 91% Certified Fresh on Rotten Tomatoes, and for good reason. I watched this in night nights of 3 episodes each and I was simply transfixed. If you are in the mood for a top notch drama or simply curious to learn more about the Troubles, I'd readily suggest you check this out, and draw your own conclusion.

title: Deep "Troubles"
author: Lejink
body: I've not read the recent best-selling book on which this television series is based but nevertheless found it a tough and challenging watch. Spanning the Troubles of Northern Ireland in the late 60's through to the 90's, two stories are intertwined, one concentrating on the life of Dolours Price, a young Catholic girl brought up in a strongly Republican household. Her father previously took up arms in the struggle and her mother is obviously just as committed to the cause of a united Ireland.
