body: Terminator Zero panders to the American audience by supplying an animated show with a lot of familiar traits. Cool action sequences, feelings of hampered dread (because we all know what to expect now), a strong female lead and a ruthless "male" robotic killer (oh boy where have we seen THAT before).It just seems like such a derivative that there's nothing new or special about it. Sure it's got a lot of parts to keep it fun, but where's the substance? And the dialogue seems so phoned-in. I feel like this could have been something great.There are a lot of cheesy, corny, predictable lines. But, the show also tries to take on a Japanese culture spin to it, and it plays out kinda cool.

title: entertaining addition for fans of both anime and The Terminator.
author: amesmonde
body: In 1997 Tokyo, AI developer Malcolm Lee is finalizing Kokoro, designed to rival Skynet. On the eve of Judgment Day, he and his children are hunted by a mysterious robot assassin, while a soldier from 2022 arrives to protect them.Written by Mattson Tomlin and directed by Masashi Kudo, Terminator Zero adopts the visual aesthetics of Seoul Station and Ghost in the Shell. The top-tier voice cast, including Rosario Dawson and Timothy Olyphant, adds depth to the tense, action-packed story that echoes many Terminator themes.Tomlin and Kudo deliver an entertaining anime take on the franchise, blending the isolated horror of a lone infiltrator that echoes James Cameron's gritty T-800, portrayed by Arnold Schwarzenegger, while also introducing new, compelling characters. Tomlin includes a few twists of sorts and the fresh narrative injects new elements that really pay off.It stands out by capturing the tone of the original Terminator while offering a sleek visual style. Unlike Blade Runner: Black Lotus, it avoids over-reliance on CGI, focusing instead on sharp, dynamic animation that feels true to the franchise.Overall, while it sets up a potential second series, it's an exciting and entertaining addition for fans of both anime and The Terminator.

title: Interesting story with average action
author: Vancour
body: I felt it was overall a pretty good watch. The storyline has a few nice twists and turns I didn't see coming yet enhance the Terminator mytho's rather then take away from it. I liked that it took place in an alternative 1997. Its characters are alright, the scientist was probably the most interesting of the bunch followed by the Misaki later. The story they carried pretty much made the Series good for me.The action, although pretty dynamic, gets pretty ridiculous at times when the unstoppable Terminator always has to miss or take a few seconds to actually kill its target, or wait... just long enough for someone else to intervene and save the day. But, I guess they needed flashy fight scenes to sell this, not intense ones. Ah well.

title: I need more Terminator Universe
author: ilter-142-82841
body: When I learned that a new Terminator animation was coming, it first reminded me of Animatrix and I got excited. With Animatrix, we were able to learn a lot about the Matrix Universe. That's why I believed with Terminator Zero, we could see a lot about Terminator Universe.I watched all episodes and to be honest I did't get what I expected. Malcolm and Kokoro's dialoges could have been shorter and we could have seen the more of the universe. I know, Malcolm and Kokoro's dialoges were important and we learned their philosophical toughts about humankind and machiens, but I think it could have been explained faster.On the other hand, Terminator Zero's time travelling system is not parallel to the other Terminator movies. Because on the movies we learned that time is linear. But in the series it is explained that a new timeline occurs when someone travels in time. Also, Terminators don't have facial expressions, for example T-800 learned smiling from John Connor so hard. But in Terminator Zero, Terminator usually has an angry face and sometimes smiles evilly.Consequently, it is nice to see Terminator Universe again but I hope in the second season they will able to show us a lot about Terminator Universe.

title: A fighting chance for the resistance in this plot
author: AziziOthmanMY
body: *"Terminator Zero"* marks a triumphant return for the *Terminator* franchise, standing tall above recent installments like *Dark Fate* and *Terminator 3: Rise of the Machines*. Where those films struggled to recapture the magic of the original entries, *Terminator Zero* not only revitalizes the series but also introduces a fresh plotline that breathes new life into a story that had begun to feel repetitive.This latest installment smartly avoids the pitfalls of its predecessors by steering the franchise in a bold new direction. The introduction of an innovative storyline, while rooted in the familiar themes of man versus machine, feels both contemporary and relevant. By reimagining some of the series' core concepts, *Terminator Zero* manages to inject a much-needed sense of urgency and intrigue, setting the stage for a potential new era of *Terminator* films.One of the standout features of *Terminator Zero* is its balance of action and narrative. The film delivers the intense, high-octane action sequences fans have come to expect, but it also takes the time to explore its characters and their motivations in greater depth. This added layer of complexity enhances the overall experience, making it more than just a spectacle of explosions and robot battles.However, *Terminator Zero* is not without its flaws. While the new plotline is refreshing, there are moments where the film feels burdened by the weight of the franchise's legacy. Some of the callbacks to earlier films, while nostalgic, can come off as forced, potentially alienating newer audiences. Additionally, the pacing can be uneven, with certain segments dragging on longer than necessary, disrupting the film's otherwise tight narrative flow.Another point of contention is the film's reliance on anime style. While the special effects are impressive, there are instances where the digital spectacle overshadows the storytelling. In some cases, the heavy use of the style detracts from the raw, gritty feel that made the original *Terminator* films so iconic.In summary, *Terminator Zero* is a significant improvement over recent *Terminator* entries, offering a fresh plotline and a renewed sense of direction for the franchise. Despite some minor missteps, it successfully reinvigorates the series and provides a solid foundation for future installments. For fans of the franchise and newcomers alike, *Terminator Zero* is a must-see that brings the *Terminator* saga back to life.

title: WOW!
author: sbkw1983
body: Let me first say that I passionately dislike movies or shows with untouchable girl bosses. I was expecting similar here. Instead, she's maternal, vulnerable, and the terminator kicks her ass (and doesn't toss her around).The story has horror elements, and it's clever. No stupid jokes. No redundant action scenes. Episodes 1 to 4 were quite good -- 8/10. Episodes 5 to 8 were outstanding -- 9/10. The story left me genuinely impressed.I am dead serious when I say this is the best entry since T1 and T2. The 2nd half especially, narratively, was outstanding. Finally a worthy followup to T1 and T2.It must be stressed that the entire show needs to be viewed if you want questions answered. And I recommend subtitles.P. S: No, the terminator doesn't have the aim of a stormtrooper. If you watch the beginning carefully, you'll see it terminates two targets (one in a locker + one wielding a grenade) before the protagonist moves.

title: Not what I was expected
author: popica13
body:
The Terminator movie series has a special charm because it is centered on the Terminator. Whether it is negative (in the beginning) or positive (along the way). From here the title: TERMINATOR.Then, the movies in the series are action movies in which tension plays an important role, more than in other action movies.Now, after watching the Terminator Zero series, I have conflicting feelings:1. I wanted to stop after the first episodes - because everything moves in slow motion, not recommended for a supposed action series;2. The series is definitely not centered on the TERMINATOR (although he has significant appearances) - he is not the main character - which detracts from the interest in the subject. When you're waiting for a Terminator series - you want a Terminator in the foreground: MAIN ROLE, FIRST!3. The multitude of characters complicates the subject;4. In the end - the main character - even the Key character - is nothing from the BEST TERMINATOR MOVIES (Terminator + his victim) is the AI - which here is a mixture of religion - philosophy - technology (as it is in trend these days) which he has nothing to do in a Terminator movie (in my opinion). A Terminator movie/series is generally a simple movie that fascinates through tenacity, survival, inner strength, exploring one's own limits - which come from the character NOT FROM DIRECT PHILOSOPHY!!Conclusion:
the purpose of the series is lost: the Terminatorthe topic is complicated by the too long duration and the multitude of characters (why other robots... of so many types, each with its own story - this is already a new topic, another series). It could have been a series of a maximum of 5 episodes and I think it would have turned out betterIt's a cute series, a true Anime, but it doesn't (at all) capture the spirit of the TERMINATOR movies. It's a 6 on IMDb for me.P. S. We should remember that Terminator and Alien first two movies were simple, clear and that's what made it GREAT!

title: When's the 2nd Season!?
author: philewill
body: Series Rating System - Rewatchability Within a Month:10: Would watch again soon.7: Not anytime soon.4: Once was enough.1: I regret watching it.When rating a TV series, the way it ends is as important as how it starts. A great beginning doesn't make up for a bad ending, whether it's due to cancellation or poor writing. If the series had potential but was ruined by a bad or rushed ending, it gets a 4. If it was bad from the start, it's a 1.No matter how the show concludes, whether it was rushed, canceled, or ended as intended, it will be rated based on the entirety of all seasons, using the four-score system outlined above.

title: Season 1 Review: Terminator reboot in manga styles, decent....
author: joebloggscity
body: If you were despaired by the news of another Terminator show, then let me tell you that you can relax, this is a fine showing, which is saying something after the lucklustre run over the years after T2 (albeit I did like Terminator Salvation).By coincidence this week I have watched/finished both reboots to the old Arnie Sci-fi classics that were Terminator Zero Anime series and this Predator:Prey movie, and personally I was happy & mildly surprised by both.We have a manga/animated series, and Season 1 is an interesting but not necessarily revolutionary redoing of the Terminator story. Based in Tokyo, we have the same story of a Terminator and human sent back to the past to change history. We have our lead protagaonist, Malcolm Lee, who is under threat from the Terminator, whilst his family find out the truth of who he truly is as they come under threat too.Now, this first season clearly owes a big debt to the seminal Ghost in the Shell, and unashamedly follows similar styles, in particular the existential monologues by certain characters. This adds some gravitas to the story and really keeps your interest.In truth, the whole backbone to the Terminator narrative has now been flogged to death, and no reboot is going to resolve that. However, the ideas remain, and this series adds a new welcome development to the films.I recommend it to all. It's got the basic concepts as well as new ones to make it of interest.

title: Terminator 2 Fan approval
author: santosh-38368
body: I came across this anime and thought i should give it a chance.Also, i didnt had high hopes, and was actually scared of them #$%^&* it up bad time.But what a treat this is!They stayed true to the original and there will be a lot of scenes of the movies but then just a little bit different. For example the two keys to open the vault simentaniously with Miles Dyson.This is deffinitly worthy of the Name Terminator!The story telling is very good, and goes a bit more in depth then the movies about for example the time travels. Its easy to watch. Im writing this after seeing the first 5 episodes straight after the other and will go on.The animations are good, the pace of the story is good, the action is beyond good. And it could go all ways. Im going to watch further.

title: Really good but the dialogue is cringe at times
author: Omninerd
body: The animation is really great although some of the artists really don't know human anatomy very well. The muscles of some of the characters look out of place especially overly protruding abs but no obliques.The plot is great. The characters are great. The action is great. The ending keeps you engaged for a second season.The biggest gripe I have is the phenomenally stupid dialogue where the writers up to date flavor of the month moral understanding of the world is the exact moral understanding that a general artificial intelligence arrives at.To me there is some insouciant complacence in this kind of writing. The most intelligent AI is supposedly thinking like a 2024 female college student.The most cringe line was: "I want to be a woman because men always bring war and violence" or something like that.I still rate this fairly high because this didn't have too much of an impact on the rest of the show but considering how much time the writers spent on it I have to mention it here.If it hadn't been for that this could have been a 9.On a side note, the time travel is absolut hooey, terminator was always a prime example of stupid kind of time travel.

title: Stay Away If You Actually Like Terminator
author: cyguration
body: Only the last three episodes are any good. I'm not going to spoil anything, but for eight episodes that clock in at just under half an hour each, one would think that they would move at a brisk pace... right? Nope.The first episodes lures you in with some over-the-top action featuring deuteragonist Eiko, who is portrayed as a super-human soldier when the plot calls for it. To their credit, throughout the series she is shown to be vulnerable, but the show never bothers to explain WHY she was sent back in time. Even when the show does attempt to explain the why, they still don't, which will leave anyone who actually pays attention to circle back around to the "Why?" after all the big reveals take place in the last two episodes.The whole thing is overly contrived and nonsensical once you start thinking about things, and the show leaves you with more questions than answers them. Perhaps this is Netflix's way of luring people in and attempting to get them to stick around for a second season? I can't say for sure but the main issue is that if you're a fan of Terminator, there is little here to lure you in.There are barely a few scant interesting action encounters where you're left wondering what's going to happen or how it will play out? But after that it's all formulaic.Actually, worse yet, the show takes the TV-MA opportunity to throw bodies at the screen in droves; anyone who isn't a main character is dispatched in gruesome and unnecessary ways. I'm no prude here, but literally everyone other than the main cast are just dispatched and gunned down in the most senseless and unsatisfying ways imaginable, almost like someone speed-running a video game where the NPCs just don't matter.It made the action feel pointless when you knew that any non-main character would be dispatched in fractions of a second. This was never actually the case in the Terminator franchise, though. While yes, it did have high body counts, people weren't balloons filled with red goo, popped at every turn. Even the police station shootout int he first film saw the Terminator receiving some formidable resistance, and the T-101 in the second film still received quite a bit of damage from the police force during the Cyberdyne infiltration.Here? Well, the Terminator receives damage but only from Eiko. It becomes groan inducing really.But beyond that, the whole point is a slog. Lots, and lots, and lots of anime-style monologuing and soliloquies that just seem to go on endlessly. The only important bits take place in the last two episodes. And once it's all revealed, you're left wondering, did we really need all of the exposition in the previous episodes? Really???The thing is, it doesn't tread new ground. It goes over the same talking points ad nauseam, and does so in a very trite and derivative way. What you're left with is a series that has flashes of intensity, but having the first half of the series depicting Eiko with super-human capabilities took all the wind out of the intensity or horror elements, but then trying to humanize here in the back-half of the series while slowing the pace way down with lots of needless chatterboxing about things that just weren't that important made the show feel like a slog to get through.At the end of it I was still left with more questions than answers, and the answers we did get just weren't very good ones.The thing is, this is basically an anime set within the universe of Terminator, but if you were expecting a horror-thriller like Terminator 1 or a sci-fi action romp like Terminator 2, or finally a proper future-war setting like Terminator Resistance, well prepare to be disappointed because Terminator Zero is not that series.I only gave it a 5 because the last two episodes were decent enough, and I did like the police station setup, but the execution of how that played out was kind of dumb. And the way everyone was just a meatbag that was easily disposed of if they weren't a main character made the stakes feel pointless and the world feel like cardboard.So yes, stay away if you actually like good Terminator fanfare.

title: "I didn't have high hopes".
author: JamesEdwardAnthonyFoster
body: It's honestly a breath of fresh air to finally see them doing something different with the Terminator franchise. Let's face it we've had more then enough movies like 5 at this point things were getting really stupid although I did enjoy Terminator Dark Fate. The first 5 minutes is done very well in the year 2022 Eiko a resistance soilder is hiding in a metal locker with 4 bullets in her pistol left there she's observing a terminator walking through the bricks and rubble left in the room killing any soilders on the floor still alive. There's some somewhat violent gun scenes here and honestly some great action sequences the animation is gorgeous and looks amazing for a first episode it really just starts of with a bang. No slow pacing or anything like that starting right of with some guns firing and everything after that we go to the year 1997 and things calm down for a little while. The series has an familiar cast to like Rosario Dawson who voices an AI in the Skynet building and Timothy Olyphant who voices the Terminator. I've only seen the first episode but this anime has promise and definitely could be something special.

title: Definitely Surprise Of The year
author: Ttdf122
body: I loved it and the way they explained the time travel aspect being different timelines opened up in time instead of the same timeline over and over, which means terminator has a massive multiverse going now lol, in a never ending war. Fully enjoyed the series, the violence and blood was good the Terminator looked scary and intense like the original one. I hope this will help revive the franchise in some way, love to see Future War movies done properly and get back to the original horror tone. Easily the deepest, most nuanced story in the whole franchise. "Zero" is to Terminator what "Andor" is to Star Wars.

title: The contrast makes the character evolve
author: tillettrenart-800804
body: I haven't been a fan of Manga since I was a child that enjoyed MAZINGER Z, so it took me a while to get used to the rythm, and tone. My 1st positive reaction was smiling with the robotic Cat, which has some tender moments rarely found in Californian productions. In other words, Japanese do know how to make a robotic cat, simpatico. And by Chapter 7 I was completely digging the Japanese Approach to Robots: who else better elaborating in the Robotics topic, in contrast to Hollywood? And btw, it's actually an International team, as the developer Mattson Tomlin is Romanian, who cowrote the 8 chapters with Director Masashi Kudô. And among the producers the USA and Israel are present. Expect a very sober editing by Akari Saitô, just once I thought WTF, with an abrupt cut of a Misaki moment.Sure, it took long for me to settle in because I am too used associating TERMINATOR with Arnold; the kick ass Brad Fiedel main theme; and the American Way of Sci-fi Action. But now after finishing experimenting TERMINATOR ZERO, I believe the original appeal to Cameron/Hollywood's creation, will only evolve, as you find out what happens when other cultures give their take on the matter. Some of us are so die hard Cameron fans and its original approach that could not have pondered this story could take place in Japan. Find out what will you go missing, and what will be a fresh take never seen before under Hollywood's standard rule book: the extreme violence going on in this Manga can blush any Live Action Violence from the West; the profound philosophical conversation between Malcolm and his Creations goes one step further programming mature material, via Cartoons! The cliffhanger at the end promisses this is just the beginning of a -let's hope-, long exploration of the most leved Robot creature in Film History. I doubt anyone watches Terminator to feel fear: befriend the enemy! Lol. Afterall Judgement Day includes every corner in the Planet, so by taking some heat off Skynet as it "shares the mic" with Japan the chance to either "terminate" once for all the War between Humans and their Creations, or making the fire bigger, before some other World team takes over the "War effort vs. Machines".

title: Surprisingly good
author: lazarkochakovacic
body: When I first saw this, I thought it was just going to be a "money scheme bad show", but it was surprisingly good, everything from the animations (which is in my opinion the less important part) to the story, I feel like this show explained the time travel concept from all movies before this one, also I really love that the plot is not the same like in every Terminator movie before, the characters are new, the plot is new, but it's still Terminator and that's what i LOVE about this show. Also, I have to mention the plot twists, you just can't easily predict what is going to happen next, let alone get bored with the story. I am really happy that this show is cannon and I wouldn't mind for this to be the last Terminator.

title: Absolutely worth watching
author: mssshreyes
body: Title. Just finished watching it and have to say it definitely met expectations and held up to its Terminator brand while also acting as an excellent blend with anime. From the action to storytelling and pacing, everything was really fun to go through.So yes, definitely give it a watch. I watched it over a span of 3 days but it is definitely binge worthy. The last three episodes were what made my time. All the twists were not predictable but plot wise really crucial.The fact that this is my first review on IMDB says a lot about what a good watch it was. 100 percent recommended, must watch if you think about/plan about watching it.

title: More of the Same, Even in Anime Form
author: jjenk911
body: Netflix was cheeky enough to release this on August 29th, which on that day 27 years ago, Skynet gained sentience to bring about Judgment Day. Now, throw a Japanese version of Skynet - Kokoro - and throw two similar stories together in a blender and see what happens.I'm on episode 5, and I like what I'm seeing. Some of the writing is repetitive, Malcolm Lee trying his damedest to convince Kokoro that humanity is worth saving. Perhaps Kokoro doesn't see it that way; or Kokoro will follow Skynet's rule to take over human life. Could Kokoro go to war with Skynet, pitting their resources against one another? That could be explored in season 2 if Netflix keeps it around.For now, I'm optimistic. Maybe the last three episodes might answer my questions.

title: Same Same but Different
author: nash_jawdat
body: The show took a different turn from the movies.Since terminator 3 I was not impressed with any of the terminator movies. Until I have finally watched this one. This series was amazing and might have potential to beat the goat (terminator 2) in terms of the story.It kept me on the edge of my seat and intrigued on what's coming next.The writing was very well executed but the graphics are not my favorite. However, some parts of the shows graphics appeared to be quite different in a good way.I hope to see Arnold as a terminator in the future.Overall, great start of the season and the ending was good too.

title: Amazing!
author: mamudinhogaming
body: I must say, normally I don't like animes that much yet just because it is the Terminator related I wanted to give it a try and finished it in a day. However, the storytelling had made me feel like in the Terminator universe. I am starting to think it is way better than Sarah Connor TV Series. Of course it can't be like the legendary first two movies but when you compare it with the latest movies and the show I think if you are an anime or terminator fan you should give it a try. After a few episodes you would probably finish the whole season (eight episodes) in a day or two. Hopefully, there will be more seasons since I can't get enough of this tv series.

title: franchise goes Japanese
author: SnoopyStyle
body: It's 1997 Tokyo. Malcolm Lee has created Kokoro, an AI system to rival Skynet. A female soldier from the year 2022 is sent back in time to protect Malcolm and his family from a Terminator. While Malcolm communes with Kokoro, the Terminator is pursuing his three kids and their nanny Misaki.I love placing the Terminator franchise in Japan. The animation is suited for it. I have my doubts about the Kokoro room. Quite frankly, it would be more real to have a Professor X head gear. I love the Terminator chasing the group and the masses of iRobots. Sometimes, the group gets away from the Terminator too easily, but I can live with that. I also do like the resolution by making it an uncertain choice.

title: Expanding the lore but with terrible writing
author: LynneParks
body: I generally enjoyed the expansion to the Terminator lore. We get the point of view of Skynets take over from another country. But the writing and the characters were very bad. I thought their development and motivations were extremely basic. All of the characters. I have seen all these stories before and all these types of characters as well. It was very tedious to watch the same stories again and again. And the worst part is the lack of explanation and the just trust me approaches to critical problems. This show was exhausting and I only finished it because I don't like abandoning shows before they last episode. Summarily, great concept but the execution was lacking....

title: Really good
author: cssbatista1987
body: I'm a bit of a critic of anime, especially anything that comes from Netflix. It was with this in mind that I watched Terminator zero. The pace is moderate and the animation could be a little better, nevertheless, the series turned out to be very exciting, with no obvious plot.People need to forget about the Terminator film before watching this one, the plot is set in Japan, and although the story may be related to the American Terminator (something we may see in the future) it seems to me that this is going in a different direction (like a different timeline that was created). The soundtrack is also very interesting, and goes well with the series. I hope to see more soon.

title: From the first to the last second!
author: ikal1
body: I must be honest and say that I thought I would watch one, maybe two episodes, and then give up on the series-but that didn't happen.The series combines the most recognizable elements of Terminator (mostly from the second movie) and adds new twists that elevate the story to heights that the entire franchise lacks.The plot is as addictive as typhus fever, and after watching the first episode, you'll have no choice but to admit that you're hooked on the series like a junkie on crack. The story is exceptional, the characters are well-crafted with a few (annoying but necessary) cinematic clichés. The action is perfectly directed, fluid, and energetic. The animation needs no comment-pure perfection.All in all, this is a serious series that has the potential to present the Terminator story in a new, incredibly exciting way. A second season is inevitable, and I hope that the next episodes will stick to the path set by the first season.

title: Nothing you haven't seen already
author: adrenachrome
body:
TL;DR version: Derivative pseudo-philosophical garbage masquerading as deep insight.600 word review:
Going the anime route for an established franchise isn't a novel idea (the Animatrix did it already) but that's not what sinks this series.No, what kills it is pulling plot ideas, dialogue and scenes from all the other Terminator films (yes, even Dark Fate, as wretched as that film was) mashes them together, and presents it as something new. Alien:Romulus did this as well, and that film was complete crap as well.The 3 kids in this further the plot along by being idiots, which is a huge strike against this, or any other, film. They detract heavily from what the writers were trying to say, but ultimately the nonsensical plot (complete with possibly the longest death-exposition dump scene in modern film history) that is rushed in at the very last minute really sinks this.Utterly forgettable and like Alien:Romulus, an insult to a franchise already teetering on the edge of irrelevance.2/10 (the 2 is for the rather well done animation)

title: A great original Terminator movie
author: expresscontent
body: Where should I begin? I was pleasantly surprised that this animate series brought back the original Terminator movie vibe (Gloom and doom and loss of life). This series is definitely not at the same league as the newer Terminator movies (which the last 2 movies are the worse and messed everything up). This series continue the original storyline but changed a few things to fit the perspective from Japan's view (making it a new story line). The story line dialog and the intensity is great. I am almost done with the last episode but wouldn't mind if they make a new Terminator like this one.Hollywood should take notes and learn a few things from screen writers from Japan. They focused way to much on political/identity and forgot about making a good story into movies.

title: Better than all the live action sequels
author: marineproductions1
body: Over the years, terminator sequels and spin-offs have tried to replicate the magic of the original, but many have fallen into the trap of recycling the same narrative and thematic elements.This led to a stagnation in the franchise, as many of the films relied heavily on the same tropes: time-traveling cyborg assassins, relentless chases, and apocalyptic visions of a future dominated by Skynet.But this show is different. It has way more substance than the other sequels. It not only moves the story forward but also brings a level of innovation and emotional depth that has been sorely missing in many of the recent installments.It has a new way of looking at the story universe and it can be a good example of how to do a sequel to an established franchise that does rely on cliches.I highly recommend everyone take a look at this series.

title: Simply Amazing
author: danyfs12
body: Gritty, stylistic, complex, thoughtful and easily digestible given 30-minute episodes... After reading the negative reviews here I'm pretty sure most of them didn't watch it through but rather didn't like the initial construct or some singular critique near the beginning and wrote it off. They ultimately missed the explanations, as well as the very thoughtful and complex plot, the layers of introspection, game theory dynamics, and the well-written character development. Without any spoilers I'll say there are twists and turns as they weave the story together so it's worth acclimating at the beginning so you can thoroughly enjoy the rest. Initially I was skeptical of the anime approach but didn't take me long to really appreciate it and see how it was most likely the best path to push the limits on a gritty, stylistic take that was very fitting for the new story it told built on the foundation of the classic plot. They also go deeper into the specifics of the story's timeline which was just the cherry on top. Well done! Will be rewatching season 1 as I wait for season 2.

title: You've been Netflixed
author: bertrandma
body: I don't watch much anime, but when I watch anime, it's usually Studio I. G. As a market, anime is extremely formulaic and most of its consumer base seem thankful for this. I. G. Normally stands out for trying to do more than just rehashing high-school isekai tropes: for this alone, they deserve praise. Not everything they've done is amazing, but it's usually competently animated, and often enough visually ambitious. At the best of times (i.e. Ghost in the Shell) it is well written too.So I had high hopes for their Netflix collab. Afterall, Netflix's Devilman--however imperfect--was surprising at many level. And the first few minutes of Terminator Zero do not disappoint: remarkable drawing, daring animation, cinematic shots and excellent soundtrack, it's nearing Mamoru Oshii levels.Unfortunately it's all down hill from there. If action scenes remain pretty good (if less inventive) throughout, the characterisation is pretty terrible, as becomes abundantly clear by the end of the first episode. The series happily buys into facile intergenerational narrative, with three utterly detestable and unconvincing children characters, and a range of flat secondary characters. Some of them have excuses to be flat, others do not, but they all feel like cardboard cut outs.The worse however is definitely the writing itself, where everything has to be spelled out at least two or three times, to ensure it all remains accessible even to the most intellectually challenged (or least attentive) viewer.Someone once characterised Emily in Paris as being 'ambient television': a show designed to move so slowly and predictably that you can actually do something else while watching it, without risking to miss anything. That's one way to put it: the optimistic way. I'm not at all sure that people do something else while watching Netflix. The showrunner for Netflix's Witcher adaptation complained the producer imposed changes to the script in order to 'dumb it down' for American audiences. I'm not sure American audiences are dumber than the average Netflix spectator (who knows?), however I think this is a more convincing explanation than 'ambient television': in order to cater to the absolute maximal audience, everything needs to be spelled out, not once but twice. Don't leave anything to the viewer's imagination, and most importantly, don't leave anything ambiguous.The result is a weird mix: an attempt to make an 'adult' anime (and here IG shines as always), which at the same time is so simple and so slow that an eight years old would find it oversimplified. It's kind of depressing and kind of fascinating, in a highway-car-crash kinda way.

title: A Breath Of Fresh Air
author: wwwpaulogarciagardeyahoocom
body: After watching the first Terminator, I couldn't believe that the franchise started with a horror-chasen (I don't know how to spell the word), suspense and action. Because when everyone thinks about the franchise, they mostly think about the second movie, more reliant on action. Which I don't blame them, because I also think and love about the second movie. And after the third movie, everything else went south. I don't know why it sucked but they suck I guess. And now with the release of the series, It's amazing! Brutal like the first three movies if I remember correctly, released on Judgement Day and just pure perfect. I can't wait for season 2 and how the franchise going to be without Arnold.

title: Enjoyed it! I could nitpick and find flaws, but, no. This was GOOD overall.
author: TreeFiddy53
body: As a fan of the OG Terminator (Tr) movies, the announcement for an official Tr anime...by the animators of Ghost in the Shell...had me intrigued. But knowing what has become of the franchise in the recent past, I remained skeptical.It released on Netflix on...sure enough, August 29 aka Judgment Day in the Tr lore. This show is really good (minus a couple logic issues which we'll get to) and a lot of people are calling this the best thing in the franchise since the James Cameron movies in 1991.The show has 8 episodes, < 30 mins each ; a quick binge. You don't have to know anything about the previous movies to watch this show, could be a standalone show if you want it to be. There are several 'easter-eggs' to the first two movies that you'd appreciate if you've seen the films but it is not a necessity. Tr has one of the most iconic themes in film history and while there's a callback, the music for this show is solid as well.The story (with a touch of a Nolan-eqsue ending), very relevant in the age of AI that we live in, ends up being slightly more philosophical than I'd expected but no complaints. A couple characters familiar with Tr and what its capable of engage in a hand-to-hand combat with it, didn't know how to feel about that, but I chose not to nitpick.Overall - A very faithful adaptation of the series with a different take on it while retaining the originality; you've got to watch it for that to make sense. Fans of the movies need to watch this! Non-fans will likely end up watching it and then will go watch the movies. Win-win IMO.

title: Best Terminator Since Judgment Day!
author: jonathanvarleyjv-70104
body: Terminator Zero is the thrilling revival the franchise desperately needed. Set in Tokyo, this Netflix anime series boldly moves away from the familiar Sarah and John Connor saga, offering a fresh take that revitalises the classic themes with a modern twist. The stunning animation and intense action sequences are paired with deep, thought-provoking storylines that explore new characters and complex moral dilemmas.Showrunner Mattson Tomlin brilliantly crafts a narrative that pays homage to the original films while breaking new ground. The show's setting in Japan adds a unique flavor, and the focus on AI evolution and human resistance feels both timely and innovative. The blend of high-stakes action, emotional depth, and gorgeous visuals makes Terminator Zero a standout.With a gripping story that respects its roots yet forges ahead with bold new ideas, this series is a must-watch for fans and newcomers alike. Whether you're here for the nostalgia or excited for the new direction, Terminator Zero delivers on all fronts, proving that the Terminator franchise still has plenty of life left in it. This is, without a doubt, the best Terminator content since Judgment Day.

title: Stunning new story, true to the originals
author: imdb-10463
body: The depth of care at all levels of Terminator Zero is simply breathtaking.Without spoilers, Terminator Zero builds on the foundations of the original movies, but explores a completely new dimension. Direction, characters, animation and - most importantly - story plunge us back into the universe of the Terminator in a way that is both respectful and mind-expanding.Initially familiar scenes - the humans waging war against the machines in the far future - quickly lead to back to the days before Judgement Day itself, this time set in 1997 Tokyo. The ticking clock of Skynet's impending nuclear strike provides a gripping backdrop as we find ourselves rooting for new characters - both man and machine.This is how classic franchises should be honored and taken to the next level. I loved it and I want more.

title: Great philosophy, music and animation
author: arabnikita
body: Terminator Zero (2024)"What Makes you believe humanity is worth saving? Can you name a single good thing that your species has done for this world? Even One?"Questions such as these and a number of others were posed in this series and in many cases, much like the protagonist, I had no answers. When I began watching Terminator Zero, I did expect it to be different in a number of ways as it was an anime. However, I didn't imagine it to be filled with intellectual and philosophical dilemmas which ended up being the most enjoyable element.Terminator Zero, much like the James Cameron films, begins with a girl named Eiko being sent to the past in order to save humanity. What's different is that Eiko is sent back to Tokyo where a brilliant scientist named Malcolm has built his own uber powerful AI in an attempt to stop Skynet's domination. Consequently, Skynet sends a Terminator to stop Eiko and execute its own destructive plan to maintain the steel grip over the throat of humanity.With AI taking a progressively larger and larger space in our modern world, this show raises a number of interesting points both in simple and complex terms. Thanks to its steady pacing, we are able to digest the ideas while being entertained by the beautiful animation, cool action and the brilliant soundtrack that lingered with me after each episode. The Japanese voice acting is fantastic so I obviously recommend experiencing it that way. You can easily binge this show, but I would suggest watching 2 episodes at a time so that you could ponder the concepts that are presented in each episode..Movieswithoutshmovies on Instagram for honest movie and tv reviews.

title: The best cinematography I've ever seen
author: Who_remembers_Dogtanian
body: Although an utterly engrossing and fascinating story, what is so memorable about this is how it looks. Over the years films and TV shows have often tried to be arty, frequently resulting in pompous and cringy pretentiousness. Without wanting to sound pretentious myself, this is the truest most beautiful piece of art I've seen for many a year. It gives you that same awe inspiring feeling of amazement as when you walk into St Vitus Cathedral or see the Taj Mahal for the first time.This is as close to perfection as you can get but to be critical and needlessly picky, I suppose it could be said that it feels a little slow at times. Audiences used to fast moving, all-action dramas might not appreciate this as much as some of us. That pace which gradually ramps up is necessary. It allows you not just to get to know Ripley (played brilliantly by Andrew Scott) but to get to know exactly how he feels and what he's thinking. The genius of this production is that we find ourselves rooting for Ripley, a thoroughly detestable human being. He's got no redeeming features whatsoever yet as much as we grow to passionately detest him, we find ourselves hoping against hope that he's going to get away with it all. It's so exceptionally well written that we're taken on the journey with him and all of his emotional experiences and anxieties.Is it right to enjoy such unpleasantness?

title: Ripley lives!
author: berndgeiling
body: Andrew Scott gives a deeply neurotic and disturbing impression of one of the most beloved psychopaths in movie history. He's a great actor and he knows exactly what he's doing, sharp, precise, intense, on top of his acting skills.Zaillian stretches the story out here, (sometimes a little bit too much in the last three episodes), taking 8 hours, compared to shorter former versions. I must say I like all versions, because Highsmith's original story is of genius quality, and it allows to open a lot of doors to different interpretations. I loved Alain Delon in the Rene Clement classic, as well as Matt Damon in the luscious Minghella version, but comparing the different interpretations in detail would take to long.About this one: Yes, I loved that it was shot in atmospheric black and white (fantastic cinematography, every frame a piece of art!), I loved that this version was slow, I loved that it was so dark, I loved the sardonic humour.I could have easily given this version 10 stars, but, I am sorry to say, the characterization of Freddie Miles didn't work for me here.

title: The cinematographer is the real star
author: mls4182
body: Black and white never looked so beautiful. I doubt even early 1960s Italy was this beautiful. This was the most visually stunning project I have seen in decades.The performances were excellent as well as the direction. The writing was a bit drawn out. This really could have been two hours shorter, but you really don't mind it.If Netflix could come up with something half this good on a semi monthly basis they'd be in the black again. This wasn't just visually appealing it was actually mature and reasonably cerebral. Miles above their usual offerings.Warning: If you watch this, you will become addicted.

title: Can Lucio the cat get an Oscar?
author: betul_ayberkin
body:
The cat saw it all, the looks exchanged between him and Ripley were unbelievable. Such Cinema Noir. 'Ripley" is a masterclass in tension, intrigue, and psychological depth. From its captivating performances to its meticulously crafted plot twists, each episode leaves you craving more. With lush cinematography and a haunting score, it's a mesmerizing journey into the complexities of identity.I just loved it all, the B&W, the acting, the adaptation, directing and soundtracks.I will watch some more work of the director for sure. Well done to all especially Lucio
.I definitely recommend this to everyone.

title: That cat
author: pennyjune
body: All eyes are on the "talented" Thomas Ripley, from the gargoyles and statues to that wonderful cat in his hotel. Shot in such a way that you feel you are there, you notice all the supporting pieces (and sounds), like the heavy glass ashtray, the creaky old lift and newspaper kiosks that set the stage and mood of mid-century Italy.I don't know when I have ever watched such a gorgeous production, and the intrigue is through the roof in this one. Not sure Matt Damon's performance in the earlier version can be topped, but Andrew Scott is a close second. Patience is required, because it is a long series but ultimately rewarding.I was hoping the scenes in Italy would be in color, because... Italy, come on! But I soon accepted the black and white format and now I don't think of it any other way.Bravo for a series actually worth watching on Netflix that was made for adults!

title: A New Face For Tom Ripley
author: marcelbenoitdeux
body: In my mind, Alain Delon in Rene Clement's 1960 "Purple Noon" was the definitive Tom Ripley. Beautiful and totally amoral. Anthony Minghella's 1999 "The Talented Mr Ripley" had a bland but thoughtful Tom Ripley who felt and suffered. Minghella had a superb script, Gwyneth Paltrow, Philip Seymour Hoffman and Cate Blanchett playing riveting, unforgettable characters. There was also John Malcovich in a Liliana Cavani version, and although I've seen it, I don''t remember it, isn't that terrible? And the Wim Wenders version with Dennis Hopper doesn't count, good film, but it doesn't count as a version of Patricia Highsmith's novel. Now this. Ripley, the series. Hours long, in black and white. My first reaction was to rejected it but the truth is that I finish seeing it over a week ago and stayed with me, I can't shake it off. Why I wonder. And the reason is very simple. Steven Zaillian's version is truly wonderful. He has de-glamorized it. The whole thing. The story, the characters. Oh the characters. I was so used to see beautiful people playing them, in gloriously glamorous locations. This version is stark and Andrew Scott is like a replicant. No emotions, not even a hint of them. Invisible. As a consequence we do all the work. We gasp or look away. He just goes on. I know I'm going to see Ripley again, maybe not tomorrow but soon. I suspect you will too.

title: One of the best Movie to TV adaptions I have seen
author: densest-solace-m
body: After years of using IMDB without an account after watching Ripley I had to leave a review. This is simply an excellent adaptation by Netflix and stand out performance by very talented Andrew Scott. Maurizio Lombardi dominates the scenes with his performance as inspector Ravini and his style of interrogations reminds my of Christoph Waltz in Inglorious Basterds. The details in each scene and continuity across the episodes makes for a great story. Characters who make small observations eg hotel staff are often leveraged later in the story and no character is irrelevant. Dakota Fanning and Johnny Flynn are both fantastic in this show. The story has been told and used many times however Ripley brings the story to the masses and it is still enjoyable for those who know the story so pause your views on the comparisons and enjoy this excellent adaptation.

title: A beautifully shot retelling of the Tom Ripley story with Andrew Scott a marvel...
author: mdw0526
body: This Netflix series had the most sumptuous cinematography I've seen in a while. Nearly every shot was a work of art, a moment captured in time, a beautiful and sinister view into this retelling of the story of psychopath Tom Ripley. This version takes its time to unfold the story, and Andrew Scott is the perfect actor for the part. Having just seen him in quite a different role in "All of Us Strangers", I was reminded what a versatile and compelling actor he is (and of course great in "Fleabag").While some have called the show "slow", I think our vastly reduced attention spans don't allow us to savor the unspooling of a narrative. I enjoyed the long shots with interesting camera angles and the use of black and white was a genius move, adding to the dark undertones of the show. It was definitely a successful passion project for Steven Zaillian, though I think the role of Dickie could have used an actor with at least a smidge of charisma, and fun fact, the spawn of Sting and Trudie Styler plays Freddie, though only with limited success. Regardless of any minor quibbles, I definitely recommend it.

title: Just accept that this is not the 'Talented' version and enjoy.
author: rah-85301
body: I loved the 'Talented Mr Ripley' version, however, have enjoyed this just as much in a different way. I liked the fact that it didn't just try to copy the last version. I was a bit taken a back at the older Tom Ripley in this version but just decided that a longer time period had passed and got used to it.I thought the actor playing Tom was fabulous and also the different Marge was streets better than Gwyneth Paltrow whom I thought was the big weakness in the previous version.The black and white worked so well with this, more sinister, and moody version. Whilst the colour of the last version worked with the 'Talented' version which portrayed a much more extraverted and upbeat Dickie.The negative element for me this time was Dickie. There seemed to be nothing to like about him and he lacked any charisma at all. He was a bit wooden and sexless to be honest. Last time, you felt that Tom had fallen so in love with the Jude Law version that he could not bear to be rejected by him or live without him. This time, I just felt that Tom wanted to take over his lifestyle but had no feelings for him. So, I think this version has fewer layers to it and something was missing.Still, you just need to accept that this is a completely different version, and it is very watchable and intriguing. Certainly, the actor playing Tom IS the film. I think worth it just for his acting.

title: Tries too hard
author: efd-10467
body: For a start Andrew Scott is 48 years old and looks it, so the persona of the young drifter doesn't fit. Next, not just his deliberately slow dialogue but all the casts methodical serious approach to everything becomes a drag.Add to this this monochrome colouring and the series fails to deliver much punch, surprise or atmosphere apart from dreariness, Ripley is more of a depressed desperate loser than a crafty conman and opportunist.They've put effort and thought Into the production but they have over done the styling, it drowns out the intrigue and fun the story.So an average show, that could have been better.Dakota Fanning's character is so deadpan she flattens most scenes she is in, the beauty and sparkle of Naples is totally lost, the lightness and purity that Gwyneth Paltrow once gave this role, made the character far more appealing.So I'm being generous with a 5, it's mainly for effort, they tried hard but failed.

title: Ripley goes for Greenleaf, and is determined to get him.
author: TxMike
body: The 1999 "Talented Mr Ripley" with Matt Damon and Jude Law is one of my favorites to re-watch. However, being a movie and required to fit the time allowed, we don't learn much about Tom Ripley's back story, his normal life, nor of the many side stories in Europe. We know that, when he is mistaken for a Princeton guy, he doesn't correct the record. We learn early that deception is his friend.In this 8-part series called just "Ripley" we see more clearly that this Tom is a bit older and how he lives the life of a grifter in New York. For example, he encounters the mail carrier and pretends to be going into the Dr Office, is handed the mail, he finds checks that he can cash. Or he pretends to be a bill collector and has a new check sent to his "agency." Using a variety of fictional identities, if a bank gets suspicious he just walks away and destroys that identity. He is slick and unperturbed, a man on his mission.So the entire series has the same core story, with the same core characters and their relationships, but it treats Tom in a distinctly different light. It starts when Mr Greenleaf hires a P. I. to find Ripley, we are not sure why he knows about him, but that is how Tom gets the paid assignment to go to Italy and find Dickie.There are a number of other differences but Tom is forever the grifter and when he realizes what Dicky has he wants it too. He wants that life, and the first episode ends with him practicing in the mirror, introducing himself as Dicky Greenleaf, foreshadowing what the rest of the series will be about.The show is shot in B&W, which I see some complain about. But I love it, to give it that 'film noir' look and feel. With much more running time to play with it goes a bit deeper in some familiar scenes and also adds some that were not included in the movie. And finally, the last scenes and the ending are heading into a completely different direction.In my mind there is no value trying to compare this 6 1/2 hour miniseries to the 1999 movie, they are quite different takes on the same core story. I like what they did here, I like the more deliberate pace, I like the B&W approach, to me it helps it feel like 1960s Italy.Dark but good series, entertaining.

title: Brilliant
author: Too-Tall-for-the-Desert
body: I am struggling to find the words to describe how brilliant this show is. It took me two episodes to find my feet with it, but once in, oh my goodness. The film photography is stunning, it is like watching liquid art. I didn't like the black and white to begin with, but loved it by the end. Light and shade has never been better used. Andrew Scott puts in a masterful performance in the lead role. He does that wonderful trick of being able to have you rooting for him even though you know morally you shouldn't. The supporting cast are excellent, with a particular nod to Eliot Sumner who I had never heard of before, but they are mesmerising.This is not a fast, bang buzz type of show, but like a lot of the finer things in life, if you are prepared to invest yourself, it will reward you in measures.

title: Style AND Substance!
author: kaideneve
body: This masterpiece of a series is completely unique from the movie, and really elicits its own distinctive film noir vibe both in cinematography and dialogue. Purposeful yet subtle performances by all involved; Andrew Scott is absolutely perfect for this role.I haven't seen a TV series interpreted from a film source this well since Hannibal, where Mads Mikkelsen was also perfectly cast and gave an unforgettable performance.What else can be said about this series? A bit of a slow burn, but the pacing is completely suitable, and allows for a bit more fleshing out and development of the characters. Although I love the vibrant colors along the coast of Italy as much as anyone, I feel the choice to use a monochromatic palette here really enhanced the mood and atmosphere of the story.Top notch production in all aspects!

title: What's in a bathrobe?
author: teresa_rosado
body: "They went up to Tom's room, and Dickie tried the bathrobe on and held the socks up to his bare feet. Both the bathrobe and the socks were the right size, and, as Tom had anticipated, Dickie was extremely pleased with the bathrobe". This is a passage from the beginning of this masterful book that is THE TALENTED MR RIPLEY (1955), by Patricia Highsmith, already adapted to the cinema more than once. As a huge fan, I was curious to watch the series RIPLEY (2024), but always suspicious that it wouldn't bring anything new. I was completely mistaken.Only someone who really likes the story and has in-depth knowledge of it could carry out an adaptation of this level of quality, managing to turn the text around in an intelligent and original way, inverting several elements, most notably the fact that Dickie hates the robe that Tom chose, which activates an expression of disappointment in Tom, that goes completely unnoticed by Dickie, but could very well be the trigger for the hatred that Tom begins to nurture for Dickie.The poor choice of robe is proof that Tom neither has refined taste nor occupies the social position he would like. This will be remembered later by Freddie Miles, when he glimpses the robe hanging on a door. In the end, even Tom realizes that that robe is not worthy of his new status, putting it in the trash. This importance attributed to the robe is, in fact, an excellent appropriation by the series creator, Steven Zaillian, of an element that, in the book, is only briefly mentioned in the beginning.Freddie Miles also goes from being redheaded and plump to being dark-skinned and slender. Mongibello, a fictional town, is replaced by the real Atrani. Furthermore, both Tom and Dickie are well over 25 (if Andrew Scott initially seems unsuited to the role, the course of the story will prove otherwise, with his interpretation work being remarkable). Such adulterations confer some distinctive features to the series, although the essential remains, that is, a protagonist completely devoid of compassion, driven by envy, the desire to rise socially and the survival instinct, starting to kill whenever he feels threatened, but never feeling remorse. Someone who doesn't like himself and wants to be someone else, as shown, paradoxically, by the reflection that the mirror gives back to him when he wears Dickie's clothes. Paradoxical is also a the way it makes us feel as spectators: we end up wishing that Ripley will not be caught just to satisfy the curiosity of understanding where his amorality leads us.In addition to inviting us to once again enter Tom Ripley's universe, the greatest triumph of this series is, without a doubt, the aesthetic-visual effect achieved with the choice of black and white, a beautiful photography and very well filmed and linked sequences (the boat sequence is perfect), which accentuates the atmosphere of suspense and mystery, inevitably transporting us to Hitchcock's films.In the last part we are surprised by the appearance of John Malkovich, who played Tom Ripley in RIPLEY'S GAME (Liliana Cavani, 2002), in what we can consider a brief homage to the previous films. It's such a shame that the song we hear in the distance, in part VII, is not a fragment of "Tu vuò fà l'americano" (who doesn't remember Matt Damon and Jude Law making this song memorable, in Anthony Minghella's version, from 1999?).

title: Wonderful
author: mathewcaswell
body: I don't often post reviews but I was compelled to do so as I really can't understand the 1/10 reviews. It seems that some people can't move beyond the book or film. This is beautifully acted, beautifully shot. I found it a real feast for the eyes and mind. I binged watched it in two days which is a shame as I wished I'd made it last longer. At times I wished it would burst into colour as I remember the film which was very colorful and Italy is best served in colour. But the subject also excellently fits black and white. Enjoy and don't be put off by the strange reviews as this is a really nice series.

title: Amazing
author: Rogermex
body:
Five minutes into this and I'm in awe that it is one of the most brilliant black & white movies I have ever seen, and I've seen many. Andrew Scott blows away previous versions of Ripley. The cinematography is extremely skilled, I can't wait to get back to seeing the whole thing. Folks who claim "black and white is boring" would be better advised to go sit in a megaplex and watch idiotic Marvel spectacles. Have fun. It's
about time someone really did an A-1 job of filming a Patricia Highsmith novel. Ripley is an abolutely classic depiction of a psychopath. Yeah, I watched Matt Damon and John Malkovitch, but this is an advance. Looking forward to more from the same director.

title: Beautiful, but poor casting
author: jewellz48
body: The aesthetic of this series is absolutely gorgeous. I enjoyed the black and white, and the contrast with the sharp, modern resolution. The cinematography reminded me of the movie Roma, and they both share a leisurely quietude, but the similarities end there.Roma managed to infuse itself with a quiet determination of character and moments of joy. This rendition of The Talented Mr Ripley spends too much time meandering through picturesque hallways and stairs, and not enough time establishing relationships and motive. Beautiful but empty.The casting was also all wrong. All three leads should be in their 20s, but only one is. And of course it's the female character who is young, paired with men who are obviously in their 40s. I wanted to be able to move past it, but it was too distracting, particularly in light of the glacial pacing. Ended up being a beautiful waste of time.

title: If Fellini & Hitchcock directed Ripley..
author: dobraashe
body: I just started episode 6 and I must say this miniseries is exactly what The Talented Mr Ripley needed - a deep dive into his character and motivation. I like the choice of a not so pretty boy for the lead actor. Both Alain Dolan (Purple Noon) and Matt Damon (1999 version) were stunningly gorgeous and fantastic in their roles but Andrew Scott brings a guy next door earthiness/sliminess to the character of Tom Ripley. He's someone who could easily blend into the crowd and go unnoticed. But, with each episode, he captures my attention no less than Dolan or Damon.I'm loving the black & white cinematography and interesting camera angles which work well together to highlight the beauty of Italian architecture and the coast.The noticeable lack of music is soothing and helps connect with the characters and the sounds in their environment. To me the sounds are like another character in the story.With the strong supporting characters in the previous versions of Ripley, I was initially not sure of the characters of Marg, Dickie, and Freddie - but they grew on me and became very believable. I especially enjoy Freddie being British not American. The Brits do snobby so well!Now I'm looking forward to the introduction of the inspector and how the next 3 episodes unfold...Thank you to all involved in making this project.

title: Why is Tom Ridley middle aged?
author: ElwoodPDowd1
body: Part of Tom Ridley's engaging charm is his earnest boyishness and his eagerness to please. So why cast a nearly 50-year-old man in the role? Andrew Scott is a respected actor, but this part is all wrong for him. I've enjoyed both the Matt Damon and Alain Delon versions, where Tom's youthful beauty opens doors ~ or at least leaves them ajar. And the black-and-white photography doesn't work here. Dickie Greenleaf's life was one of technicolor luxury; let us see it in all of its Mediterranean opulence. So very disappointed by the creative decisions that mar this newest version of Patricia Hightower's thriller.

title: A brilliant study of the psychology of the sociopath.
author: peggygrypma
body: A most brilliant series...one of the most nuanced and subtle portrayals of the psychology of the sociopath/ narcissistic personality disorder. There are scant few films or series that reflect any depth of understanding of the 'dangerous personality'. This series is one of the few exceptions. Contrary to Hollywood stereotypes, people like the character Tom Ripley do not necessarily stand out from the crowd; they can be charming and 'friendly', yet there is a social awkwardness, a vacant stare, an emptiness and a paranoia that can explode into unexpected repressed rage and manipulative, parasitic and predatory behaviour. These personality characteristics are portrayed with subtlety and depth by the actor who plays Tom Ripley, all accentuated by stunning black and white cinematography. He was in my opinion, much more effective and much more complex and interesting than the original Ripley played by Matt Damon. Please bring on more shows like this on Netflix!!

title: Cinematographic jewel in the form of a series
author: leonardooliva-16135
body: We are possibly in the presence of one of the series of the year.A new version of the 1999 film and more faithful to the book by Patricia Highsmith.Thriller, suspense, drama, excellent performances and better photography than Masters of the Air or even Shogun.It is a series that simmers and it is not until chapter 3 that the plot takes shape and does not stop until a very good ending.It is a work of art, really. Many will be fascinated by photography where you see works of art that are analogous to the feelings of the protagonist. Others will be outraged by the main character's amoral nature. The truth is that we should all agree on one concept. It is a major cinematographic art: the shots, the perspectives, the shadows, lights and even the walking or the noises shock. The construction of environments and the period recreation is perfect. We really believe that we are in Rome, Naples, Atrani and endless places to visit. A great success that it is filmed entirely in black and white.The performances of Andrew Scott and Dakota Fanning are very good. The counterpoint of Ripley and Ravini is impressive and all the events, at that time of course, are extremely believable.Multiple nods to the book and the movie that can be seen.With an ending a little more open and less "dark" than in the aforementioned film.Mandatory appointment at this year's awards ceremony and a great success from Netflix, which luckily comes with very good material this year.

title: Masterpiece
author: dc_nelson
body: I was hesitant at first to watch this. I don't know why. An absolutely stunning masterpiece. The acting was unbelievable, creepy, believable, and kept me glued the entire time. The cinematography was stunning. You felt as if you were in every single place that Ripley was. Although it was in black-and-white, you really can feel Italy. There was not a single actor that did not live up to their part.I've seen the movie many years ago, and I enjoyed it. But I have to say, this remake was far superior than the original. I would love to see other shows redone in this matter. Everything about it was visually stunning.

title: Should if the world was fair have every award possible
author: beingmaggie
body: This was a masterpiece of cinematography blew my mind it was everything a thinking person, a creative could want. Thank god there are still artists out there prepared to invest the time and patience into projects of this calibre. I can only imagine the patience required by the actors waiting around for each shot to be set up this was a special series on so many levels really it can only speak for itself. I wanted a ticket to Rome after watching and to see the works of carrivagio. Apart from the stunning visuals wow the storytelling is something else again .this was rich filmmaking at its very best.

title: The Italians!!
author: gbbonkers
body: So much has been written about the magical cinematography, lighting and lead actors but I haven't seen much about the Italian actors. They were Magnifico!! If not for them the pace of the film might have been hard to bear. Every one of them had a distinct character and an interesting face. Inspector Ravini was particularly intriguing. His dialog was subtle - and even hilarious at times - and he played it with aplomb. The hotel front desk clerks were wonderful and distinctly memorable. All of the Italian supporting cast in minor roles were also delightful. Seeing the towns, the cities, the art, the roads, the homes, the architecture, the cars, was visually sumptuous. I'll be watching it a second time, just to see it all again and discover what I missed.

title: About black and white and all the rest
author: rogeriodacostapereira
body: For those who complain. First of all, it's not black and white. It's much more than that. The nuances, the shadows... It's almost perfect. You can't get that in colour. Even the paintings have a little extra with this option.So, it's a question of art. Either you see it. Or you don't. And I really mean "see".About all the rest. 10 stars for the casting. Andrew Scott at his best. The evolution he gives to the character is remarkable. And Dakota Fanning is a complete surprise, here.The story. This is not the book. It's based on it. I imagine it's hard for the one stars to understand the difference. This is not "The Talented Mr. Ripley". It's "Ripley".

title: Beautiful, brilliant and ingeniously paradoxical
author: cliew5473-107-917925
body: This series is by far one of the best that I've ever seen, not only in terms of its plot and its characters but also due to its excellent cinematography. Almost the entire series is set in Italy during the 1960s. This setting combined with it being shot in black and white creates a very authentic "vibe." You almost feel as though you are actually there, witnessing all of these events unfold. The cinematography is superb, with the camera often focusing on random things that make them feel significant even though they necessarily are not. Even the use of silence in this film somehow seems to play a role. All of this somehow adds to the overall underlying eeriness of the show as well as its brilliant psychological complexity. One thing I find most interesting about this series is that the main character seems to serve as both the protagonist and antagonist in this film, resulting in a sense of the paradoxical within the viewer and perhaps even a bit of cognitive dissonance. I know what he's doing is wrong and yet somehow I find myself hoping he will get away with it. I suppose this is all due to being under its spell, as the entire series truly is captivating. I really hope to see a second season (and more) from this series, as it really is a masterpiece. I have fallen deeply into the ever-intriguing world of Thomas Ripley, and I'm not sure I ever want out.

title: Tragically ruined by otherwise one of the best actors right now
author: ciecire
body: Beautifully photographed. I watched and watched but only for the same reason I'd sit through a travel documentary. Unfortunately, the cinematography is the best this production could offer. If not for the earlier and far better adaptation of the Highsmith book, I might have actually liked this series. I don't think it's a casting issue - how could it be with such a brilliant ensemble?, but more an acting direction issue. Andrew Scott (I am a fan, believe me) eventually grew tiresome in his intensity. The range of emotion he is well equipped to convey (fear, tension, delusional, frustration, anger, hopefulness,....) got spun to endless repetition in the series. And ultimately in expressing such range, he forgot to be likeable (or at least a character that drew curious interest in his awkwardness) the way Matt Damon managed to do in the 1999 film. That Marge and Dickie take Damon's Ripley in their circle as a friend was thus believable. This was not the case in this 2024 series. Andrew Scott was too sinister and strange throughout that it made no sense for him to have struck a friendship Marge and Dickie (or anyone for that matter) at all. The sexual tension and attraction between Matt Damon and Jude Law (and Gwyneth Paltrow) was also sadly lost. And the levity and flirtatiousness in Gwyneth's portrayal of Marge was replaced by the more sombre and resultingly boring Dakota Fanning. Well acted overall - the actors did their job, but the director took the characters where they should not have gone. So unexpected that acting direction would be the flaw of this series, given the strong cast.

title: Cinematic brilliance
author: Amrit_TheBritishVoiceArtist
body: Be warned, once you start, this series will keep you hooked.Ripley is depicted very differently to the charming person from the film.Awkward. Calculating. Desperate.That's how I'd sum him up.And this is not only filmed beautifully in crisp 4K with visual finesse and a Hitchcock feel.It has just the right attention to sound design with a beautiful composition.The character reactions, where more is said with less words kept me intrigued.It is a mini series but you'll feel like you're watching one great movie after the next as you go from episode to episode.And one I'd be happy to watch more than once.

title: Boring at the beginning, fascinating at the end
author: doganerdogmus
body: I was quite bored at the first four or five episodes of the show, couldn't stop myself from giving small breaks while watching it at the beginning. Then the last three episodes grabbed me, and I finished them in just one night. The slow build-up initially made it hard to stay engaged, but the payoff was worth it. The plot twists and character development in the latter part of the series were thrilling. The performances, especially the lead, were commendable, adding depth to the story. Overall, while it started slow, Ripley ended up being a captivating watch that kept me hooked till the end. Ok to watch.

title: Still life
author: dierregi
body: The first of Highsmith's novels about psycho Tom Ripley, re-interpreted in a series of sterile, icy vignettes filmed in gorgeous black and white.Probably to save money on the settings, only corners of the locations mentioned are shown (NY, Atrani, Naples, can't see a thing in San Remo, etc...) Since I'm Italian, I found the Italian locations particularly disappointing. The series was shot in cold weather and seeing Dickie and Marge alone on the beach and then bathing in the sea was weird. I never saw an Italian beach (or village) so deserted, not even in winter. It looked like only three people lived in Atrani and Naples was not much better (never seen the city so clean and orderly).As mentioned by others, Andrew Scott is too old to play Ripley, described as a 25 yo in the novel, nor has he the charisma of a psycho, but mostly looks sneery and frozen-faced. Johnny Flynn seems too young to be moving into Tom's circle, and Dakota Fanning doesn't seem to have much of a range, except sulking. Freddy, the elephant in the room - let's say it mercifully - is "miscast", a far cry from the malignant but hearty presence of Hoffman in the Minghella movie. However, it's an excellent example of nepotism.Each episode seems crystallized in minimum, emotionless dialogue, from the dreary NY opening to the cold meeting of Tom and Dickie. One wonders why Dickie would invite Tom to stay with him when their relationship boils down to concise, almost surgical sentences about nothing. The "investigative" sessions are a joke, even given low investigative standards. The episode of the boat is conveniently forgotten; no appeal such as "Have you seen this man?" is made in newspapers about the allegedly "missing" Ripley and the Italian authorities never contact the American Embassy to get info about the people involved.All episodes are like Dickie paintings, limp and lifeless, mediocre attempts to produce feelings only an original could evoke, be it film noir, Hitchcock, or the more recent "Talented Mr. Ripley".

title: What a tangled web we weave...
author: grantss
body: 1961. Tom Ripley, a small-time fraudster, is hired by millionaire Herbert Greenleaf to visit his son Dickie in Italy and bring him back to New York. Dickie has been squandering his inheritance on lavish, unproductive living and Greenleaf believes that Ripley, being a friend of his, can convince him to straighten up and come home. Ripley goes to Italy but has other plans in mind.A clever, intriguing mini-series, based on the novel The Talented Mr Ripley by Patricia Highsmith, which also gave us the 1999 movie, and created and written by Steven Zaillian, writer of The Irishman, The Night Of, Moneyball, American Gangster, Gangs of New York and Schindler's List, among others.Starts slowly - the first two episodes set the series up - but after that it is absolutely riveting viewing. Ripley shows his intentions and after that the plot generally involves him trying to cover things up. Often one elaborate plan results in some unintended consequence that he then has to cover up. The cat-and-mouse games between Ripley and the Italian police, especially the highly resourceful Inspector Ravini, are brilliant.It's all very clever and generally quite plausible. There's instances where just the slightest misfortune, a meeting between two unconnected people who know him, a policeman looking more closely at photos, and he's done for. Such is the tight line the plot walks and it's enthralling.The black-and-white cinematography creates a great film noir-like atmosphere and a very classy feeling. Italian scenery, art and architecture are used extensively and these greatly enhance the series.I largely watched this because of the broader plot (I thought the 1999 film The Talented Mr Ripley was very good) and because I admire Andrew Scott's work, especially his portrayal of Moriarty in Sherlock. He is not disappointing, putting in a spellbinding performance as Tom Ripley.Supporting cast is great too with Maurizio Lombardi as Inspector Ravini to the fore.Brilliant mini-series.

title: On the trace of Caravaggio
author: alessandro-spiandore
body: A stunning 8-episode miniseries filmed in some of the most beautiful cities in Italy. This American production, entirely shot in black and white, is set in the early 1960s. The series is a noir that is at times comic and at times grotesque, following the biographical traces of the legendary artist Caravaggio. The production demonstrates a meticulous attention to detail in both direction and cinematography. The setting and historical reconstruction are nothing short of excellent, bringing the atmosphere of the era vividly to life.
